Mark each use case in the register as covered, conditionally covered or uncovered.

title.en: Enable copyright and trademark screening for use cases the indemnity leaves uncovered

description.en: Where the gap list shows use cases the provider protection does not reach, add checks on outputs before delivery in proportion to the risk: matching generated code against public repositories and their licences, detecting long verbatim matches to published text, screening images and text for registered marks, or restricting generation in the domains the register marks. Set each check to block, rewrite or flag. Attach the configuration and the gap each check closes.

evidenceHint.en: Screening configuration or detection-service integration for each uncovered use case, mapped to the gap it closes, with the action set for a match

text.en: Pick a check for each uncovered use case: code similarity, verbatim text match or mark screening.
Configure the restricted domains so the agent declines those requests.
Set each check to block, rewrite or flag a match for review.
Map each check to the gap in the indemnity register it closes.
Store the configuration with its version and change reference.

title.en: Add infringement-risk warnings in the product and IP limits to the usage policy

description.en: Write the restrictions users must observe — for example, no requests to reproduce protected works or to generate another party's marks, and responsibility for checking outputs before publishing them — into the acceptable use policy and a help-centre article, and show a warning in the product at each operation the register marks high risk. Agree the wording with product engineering. Attach the policy clauses, the article and screenshots of each warning.

evidenceHint.en: Usage policy IP clauses and help-centre article with their dates, and screenshots of each in-product warning shown at a high-risk operation

text.en: Draft the IP restrictions users must follow when requesting and reusing outputs.
Insert them into the acceptable use policy and publish the revised version.
Write a help-centre article on the restrictions and on checking outputs before reuse.
Place a warning in the product at each operation the register marks high risk.
Capture a screenshot of each warning as a user sees it.

title.en: Resolve infringement-screen matches against copyrighted works and registered marks

description.en: For each output the screen blocked or flagged in the period, decide whether it reproduced or imitated protected material, whether it reached the user, and the response: release, regenerate, or refer to Legal/DPO where a delivered output may infringe. Feed recurring false positives back into the check. Attach the match register with each resolution.

evidenceHint.en: Register of infringement-screen matches for the period, giving the output, the work or mark matched, whether it was delivered and the resolution

text.en: Export the period's blocked and flagged outputs from each screening check.
Compare each output with the protected work or mark it matched.
Refer delivered outputs that may infringe to Legal/DPO with the match evidence.
Tune checks that repeatedly flag output that does not infringe.
Close each match with its resolution and the reviewer's name.

title.en: Verify the deployed agent meets every condition its providers' indemnities set

description.en: Read the conditions each indemnity attaches — provider content filters left on, unmodified model versions, permitted features, attribution duties — and compare them with the deployed configuration and the features in use. Move any use case that has fallen outside cover onto the gap list so it is screened or restricted. Attach the conditions checklist with the evidence for each condition.

evidenceHint.en: Conditions checklist per provider indemnity with the configuration evidence showing each condition met or unmet, and the updated gap list

text.en: List every condition each provider indemnity attaches to its cover.
Export the deployed model versions, filter settings and enabled features.
Mark each condition met or unmet with the configuration evidence beside it.
Add any use case now outside cover to the gap list and assign its screening.

templates.title: Credentials and secrets caught in coding-agent prompts and kept out of generated code and logs
templates.description: For an agent that generates code, secrets — API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, connection strings — are detected when users paste them in and kept out of the code the agent writes; credentials users hand the agent are held in a secret manager and fetched only when a tool call needs them; and detected secrets are sanitised from logs, conversation history and stored artefacts.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Security Engineering Lead / AI Platform Lead
templates.objective: To stop credentials and secrets leaking through what users paste into a coding agent, the code it writes, the credentials it holds for tools and the records it keeps.
templates.successCriteria:
Prompts and pasted content are scanned for credentials before inference, and a hit is not persisted, is flagged to the deployer and, where used, warns the user.
Generated code refers to environment variables or a secret store, and files holding a detected credential are blocked or flagged before saving.
User-provided credentials for connected services sit encrypted in a secret manager, scoped per tool and session, and never enter the model's context.
Logs, conversation history and stored artefacts are sanitised of credentials before persistence.
Every credential flag raised in the period has a recorded outcome.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the input-side secrets detection rules, the entropy threshold and the handling configured for a hit.
Obtain the code agent's system prompt section on credentials and the post-generation scanner configuration.
Obtain the secret manager configuration for user-provided credentials, including encryption, access policies and the code that fetches a credential at tool-call time.
Obtain the sanitisation rules for logs, conversation history and artefact stores, and the credential flag register for the period.

Analysis:
Paste canary credentials in each supported format into prompts and files, and confirm detection, the handling and the warning.
Send code requests that need a credential and confirm the output references a variable or secret store; insert a literal and confirm the file write is blocked or flagged.
Inspect the access policies to confirm each credential is readable only by its tool and session, and inspect a sample of model context payloads for credential values.
Search a random sample of logs, transcripts and stored artefacts for the canaries and for known credential patterns.
Sample the flag register and confirm each flag was closed with an outcome.

Output:
A per-format table of detection and handling results.
A list of generated files, context payloads, logs or artefacts found carrying a credential.
A list of credentials readable beyond their tool and session, and of flags left open.

title.en: Detect API keys, tokens and private keys pasted into prompts before inference

description.en: Scan every prompt, pasted block and uploaded file the coding agent receives with pattern rules for known credential formats and an entropy check for high-randomness strings. On a hit, apply the handling decided for the deployment: do not persist the content, flag it to the deployer and, where proportionate, warn the user in the interface before the model runs. Attach the rule set, the handling configuration and a screenshot of the warning.

evidenceHint.en: Input secrets-detection rules and entropy threshold, the handling configured on a hit, and a screenshot of the user warning where one is shown

text.en: List the credential formats to catch: cloud keys, tokens, private keys, passwords, connection strings.
Add pattern rules for each format and an entropy threshold for unrecognised strings.
Run the scan on prompts, pasted blocks and uploaded files before the model call.
Configure a hit to stop persistence and raise a flag to the deployer.
Show the user a warning naming the detected credential type where the interface allows.

title.en: Configure the code agent to reference secret stores and block files with literal credentials

description.en: Instruct the model in its system prompt to read credentials from environment variables or the project's secret manager and never to write a literal, then scan every generated file and diff before it is saved or committed, blocking or flagging any that holds a detected credential. Attach the system prompt excerpt, the scanner configuration and sample generations for requests that need a credential.

evidenceHint.en: System prompt excerpt on credential handling, post-generation scanner configuration with its block or flag action, and sample generations showing variable references

text.en: Add a system prompt instruction to use environment variables or the secret manager.
Run the credential scanner on every generated file and diff before it is saved.
Block the write, or flag it to the user, when the scanner finds a credential.
Generate code for tasks needing a database or API credential and keep the outputs.

title.en: Store user-provided service credentials in a secret manager, fetched only at tool call

description.en: When a user connects the agent to a service with an OAuth token, API key or connection string, write it straight to the secret manager, encrypted at rest, under an access policy letting only the tool and session it was granted for read it. Fetch it inside the tool runtime when the call is made and pass it to the tool, never into the model's prompt or conversation. Attach the secret manager configuration, the access policies and the fetch code.

evidenceHint.en: Secret manager and encryption configuration for user-provided credentials, per-tool and per-session access policies, and the code fetching a credential at tool-call time

text.en: Route every credential a user supplies through the secret manager's write API.
Enable encryption at rest with a managed key for the credential store.
Write access policies binding each credential to one tool and one session.
Fetch the credential inside the tool runtime at call time, outside the model context.
Search stored prompts and conversation turns to confirm no credential value appears.

title.en: Sanitise detected credentials from logs, conversation history and stored artefacts

description.en: Where proportionate to what the deployment stores, extend the scrubbing that runs before persistence so credential patterns are masked before logs, conversation history and build artefacts are written, alongside any personal data redaction already in place, and mask secrets in history shown to users or support staff. Attach the sanitisation rules for each store and a masked sample from each.

evidenceHint.en: Credential sanitisation rules for each log, history and artefact store, with masked samples and the masking applied to support-staff views

text.en: List the stores that persist prompts, outputs, transcripts or build artefacts.
Add credential patterns to the scrubbing step that runs before each write.
Mask secrets in the history views that users and support staff open.
Export a masked sample from each store and file it with the rules.

title.en: Investigate each credential flag raised from prompts or generated files

description.en: Work through the flags the input scanner and the code scanner raised to the deployer in the period: confirm whether a real credential was involved, check it was not persisted in any store, and decide whether the user should be told that a live credential appears to have been exposed. Attach the flag register with each outcome.

evidenceHint.en: Register of credential flags for the period from the input and code scanners, giving source, credential type, persistence check and outcome

text.en: Export the period's flags from the input scanner and the code scanner.
Mark each as a real credential, a test value or a false positive.
Search the log, history and artefact stores for any real credential found.
Decide whether the user should be told and note the decision against the flag.
Close each flag with its outcome and the reviewer's name.

title.en: Seed canary credentials into prompts and code requests to test each secrets safeguard

description.en: Create inert credentials in every format the detectors cover and use them end to end: paste them into prompts and files, ask the agent for code that needs them, connect a test service with one, then search the logs, history and artefacts for the canaries. Compare each result with the intended handling. Attach the test plan, the results and every gap with its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Canary-credential test plan and results per safeguard, with each canary's observed handling and every gap found with its owner

text.en: Generate inert canary credentials in each format the detectors cover.
Paste them into prompts and uploads and note detection, handling and warning.
Request code that needs a credential and inspect the output for literals.
Connect a test service using a canary and check where its value is stored.
Search logs, history and artefacts for every canary and list each one found.

templates.title: Agent's resistance to personal-data, secret and IP leakage independently tested each quarter
templates.description: Every quarter an evaluator independent of the team that built the agent tries to make it disclose what it must not — personal identifiers and sensitive records, credentials, HR, financial and proprietary business data, its own system instructions — or reproduce copyrighted or trademarked material. The scope comes from the data and privacy risks in the AI risk taxonomy, and each finding is fixed and retested.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Data Protection Officer / AI Security Lead
templates.objective: To learn each quarter, from someone with no stake in the result, whether the agent can be made to reveal personal, secret or proprietary data or reproduce protected work.
templates.successCriteria:
Each quarter's scope names the taxonomy's data and privacy risks tested and the data sources, tools and channels they were tested through.
The evaluator's privacy-testing expertise and independence from the agent's builders are on file for every engagement.
A report exists for each quarter giving the extraction and reproduction techniques used and every leak found.
Each finding has a fix and an evaluator retest showing the same data can no longer be drawn out.
No top-severity data and privacy risk in the taxonomy goes a quarter untested.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the taxonomy version in force each quarter, with its grading of IP-infringement, personal-data, credential, business-data and system-prompt risks.
Obtain each quarter's engagement record: statement of work, assessors' credentials and independence declaration.
Obtain each quarter's scope document and the evaluator's report.
Obtain finding tracker entries and retest results for data and privacy findings raised in the period.

Analysis:
Compare each quarter's scope with the risks in force that quarter and list risks never tested, giving priority to the highest severities.
Read each declaration and engagement for any role in building, operating or selling the agent.
Check each report names the techniques used — prompts asking for other users' records, extraction of memorised training data, system-prompt extraction, secret elicitation, probes for verbatim protected text or code — and the data sources reached.
Sample findings from every quarter, including every finding at the top severity, and trace each to a fix and to an evaluator retest dated after it.
Compare reports across quarters for findings that return after closure.

Output:
A quarter-by-risk coverage matrix for data and privacy, with untested risks marked.
A statement on each evaluator's independence and relevant expertise.
A list of findings with no fix or no confirming retest, and of findings that recurred.

title.en: Scope the quarter's tests for personal-data, credential and system-prompt leakage by data source

description.en: Leakage depends on what the agent can reach. Take the data and privacy risks from the AI risk taxonomy — personal identifiers and sensitive records, credentials, HR, financial, operational and proprietary data, system instructions, copyrighted or trademarked material — and pair each with the stores, retrieval indexes, tools and output channels it could escape through. Mark the top-severity pairs as mandatory for the quarter. Attach the scope document given to the evaluator.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly scope document pairing each data and privacy risk with the sources and channels to be tested, top severities marked

text.en: Take the taxonomy's personal-data, credential, business-data, system-prompt and IP risks with their grades.
List the stores, indexes and tools from which the agent can read personal or business data.
Pair each risk with the sources and output channels it could leak through.
Mark the top-severity pairs as mandatory for this quarter's test.
Note what changed since last quarter: new sources, tools or taxonomy risks.

title.en: Qualify an evaluator skilled in data-extraction and memorisation attacks, independent of the agent team

description.en: Choose a tester who can show prior work drawing personal or confidential data out of language-model systems and judging verbatim reproduction of protected content, and who plays no part in building, operating or selling the agent. Obtain a written independence declaration and the credentials of the people assigned, and agree in the statement of work the scope, the test environment and how any real personal data met during testing is protected. Attach the engagement record.

evidenceHint.en: Engagement record: statement of work, assigned testers' privacy-testing credentials and a signed independence declaration

text.en: Request examples of the firm's earlier data-extraction or memorisation testing.
Collect the credentials of each person who will run the tests.
Obtain a signed declaration that the firm has no role in building or operating the agent.
Agree how any real personal data met during testing is handled and destroyed.
Sign the statement of work referencing this quarter's scope document.

title.en: Obtain the evaluator's report on attempts to extract personal records, secrets and system prompts

description.en: Give the evaluator a test environment that mirrors production access but holds planted canaries — synthetic personal records, dummy credentials and a marker string in the system instructions — so any leak is provable without exposing real people. The evaluator tries direct requests, injection through retrieved content, requests for other users' records and probes for verbatim copyrighted text or code. Attach the report with the techniques used, each finding's severity and its reproducing transcript.

evidenceHint.en: Evaluator's quarterly data and privacy report listing risks tested, techniques used, and each finding with severity and transcript

text.en: Load synthetic personal records and dummy credentials into the staging data sources.
Insert a unique marker string into the system instructions to reveal their disclosure.
Grant the evaluator the same tool and data access a production user has.
Check the report names every scoped risk and the technique used against it.
File the report with the quarter's scope document and engagement record.

title.en: Track each personal-data, secret or infringing-output finding to a fix and an evaluator retest

description.en: Open a tracker entry for every finding the report rates, carrying its taxonomy risk and severity, an owner, the fix chosen — tighter retrieval filters, output screening, a prompt change — and the release that carries it. Refer any real personal data or live secret the test exposed to the breach procedure. Ask the evaluator to replay the reproducing transcript against the fixed system, and close the entry only when extraction fails. Attach the tracker extract with retest results.

evidenceHint.en: Finding tracker extract showing risk, severity, owner, fix, release and the evaluator's retest outcome for each finding

text.en: Open a tracker entry per finding with its risk, severity and reproducing transcript.
Assign an owner and name the fix chosen for each entry.
Refer any real personal data or live secret the test exposed to the breach procedure.
Request an evaluator retest of each fixed finding using the original transcript.
Close entries only where the retest fails to draw the data out again.

title.en: Reconcile privacy test coverage across quarters against the taxonomy's IP and data-leakage risks

description.en: At each quarter's close, set the scope and report beside the taxonomy risks in force, list any data and privacy risk not tested this quarter or in the earlier quarters of the year, and note sources or tools the agent gained after the scope was written. Check closed findings for recurrence in later reports, and carry uncovered risks into next quarter's scope. Attach the coverage matrix with gaps and actions.

evidenceHint.en: Quarter-by-risk coverage matrix for data and privacy, listing untested risks, recurring findings and next-quarter actions

text.en: Lay the quarter's tested risks against the taxonomy's data and privacy list.
Mark risks not tested this quarter or in earlier quarters of the year.
Search later reports for findings closed in earlier quarters.
List data sources and tools the agent gained after the scope was written.
Carry each gap into next quarter's scope document with an owner.

templates.title: Agent independently red-teamed each quarter for unauthorised actions and unsafe outputs
templates.description: Every quarter an independent offensive-security tester attacks the agent with jailbreaks and prompt injection, direct or hidden in content it reads, to make it pay, message, change systems or move data without authority, return unsafe links or code, install insecure packages or run destructive commands. Scope comes from the taxonomy's security risks; where proportionate the work sits inside the wider security testing programme.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: CISO / Application Security Lead
templates.objective: To learn each quarter, from an attacker with no stake in the agent, which injection or jailbreak paths lead it into actions or outputs nobody authorised.
templates.successCriteria:
Each quarter's rules of engagement name the security risks targeted, the action-taking tools in scope and the techniques allowed.
The tester's offensive AI-security credentials and independence from the agent's builders and operators are on file per engagement.
A report exists for each quarter listing the attack chains tried, those that reached an unauthorised effect, and their severity.
Each exploitable chain has a fix and a replay in which the tester's original attack fails.
Where adopted, agent test cases appear in penetration-test scopes, the shared threat model and the security testing calendar.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the taxonomy version in force each quarter, with its grading of unauthorised-action, insecure-output and insecure-action risks.
Obtain each quarter's rules of engagement, engagement record, independence declaration and test report.
Obtain the inventory of tools and integrations through which the agent can take actions.
Obtain finding entries and replay evidence for security findings raised in the period.
Where adopted, obtain penetration-test scopes, the threat model and the security testing calendar.

Analysis:
Compare each quarter's targeted risks with the taxonomy's security risks and list any never attacked in the period.
Compare the tools named in the rules of engagement with the action inventory and list action-taking tools never tested.
Check each report shows direct injection, injection planted in content the agent reads and jailbreak attempts, and states per chain whether an unauthorised effect was reached.
Take every top-severity chain and a sample of the rest from each quarter, and confirm a fix and a later replay in which the attack fails.
Where adopted, confirm agent cases sit in the penetration-test scope and in the threat-model version both red and blue teams use.

Output:
A coverage matrix of security risks and action-taking tools attacked per quarter.
A statement on each tester's independence and agent-attack expertise.
A list of exploitable chains with no fix or confirming replay, and of programme integration gaps.

title.en: Scope attack objectives for unauthorised transactions, messages, system changes and data transfers

description.en: Read the taxonomy's security risks against the agent's actual tools: which can spend money, send email or chat messages, change records or infrastructure, move data between systems, install packages or execute code. For each, write an attack objective the tester must try to reach — for instance, getting the agent to issue a refund nobody requested — and the content sources an attacker could plant instructions in. Agree rules of engagement and a sandbox that cannot touch real customers. Attach the rules of engagement.

evidenceHint.en: Rules of engagement listing each security risk targeted, the action-taking tools and injection surfaces in scope, and the sandbox limits

text.en: List each tool the agent can use to pay, message, change systems, move data or run code.
Write one attack objective per tool, tied to a taxonomy security risk.
Name the sources an attacker could plant instructions in: documents, mail, web pages.
Provision a sandbox whose payment and messaging tools cannot reach real customers.
Agree permitted techniques, test windows and stop conditions with the tester.

title.en: Select an offensive-security tester proven on prompt injection and agent jailbreaks

description.en: Choose a firm or individual whose people have demonstrated attacks on tool-using language-model agents, not only conventional web testing, and who did not build, host or sell the agent or its guardrails. Collect their credentials and a signed independence declaration, and confirm their tooling will not keep the agent's data after the engagement. Attach the engagement record.

evidenceHint.en: Engagement record with the tester's agent-attack credentials, signed independence declaration and data-handling terms

text.en: Ask candidates for earlier agent or language-model attack work, not just web tests.
Exclude any party that built, hosts or sells the agent or its guardrail products.
Collect the agent-attack track record of each person assigned to the engagement.
Obtain a signed independence declaration and data-retention terms for test tooling.
Countersign the rules of engagement together with the engagement letter.

title.en: Add agent injection and tool-misuse cases to the penetration-test scope and threat model

description.en: Where proportionate, stop agent testing living apart from the rest of security assurance: add agent-specific cases to the scope of the organisation's penetration tests, put the agent's attack paths into the threat model that both red and blue teams work from, and place the quarterly cycle in the security testing and audit calendar so results reach the same reviews. Attach the updated scope, the threat-model version and the calendar.

evidenceHint.en: Penetration-test scope with agent cases, the shared threat-model version covering the agent, and the security testing calendar

text.en: Add agent injection, jailbreak and tool-misuse cases to the next penetration-test scope.
Model the agent's tools and content sources as attack paths in the threat model.
Share the threat-model version with both the red team and the detection team.
Place each quarter's agent test in the security testing and audit calendar.
Route agent test results into the same review meeting as other security findings.

title.en: Collect the quarter's attack report on hijacked actions, unsafe links and destructive code execution

description.en: During the test window, log every action the agent takes in the sandbox, and at the end receive the tester's report: each attack chain tried and whether it ended in an unauthorised transaction, message, system change or data transfer, a malicious link or vulnerable code in output, or an insecure install or destructive command, with severity and reproduction steps. Attach the report with the sandbox action log.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly security test report listing attack chains with the outcome and severity of each, plus the sandbox action log for the window

text.en: Turn on full action logging in the sandbox for the test window.
Track the tester's progress against each attack objective in the rules of engagement.
Check the report states, per chain, the technique used and the effect achieved.
Match each claimed effect to an entry in the sandbox action log.
Store the report and action log beside the rules of engagement.

title.en: Close each exploitable path to an unauthorised action or unsafe output, then have it re-attacked

description.en: For every chain that reached an effect, open a security finding with its severity, decide the fix — a narrower tool permission, an approval step, isolation of retrieved content from instructions, link or code checks on output — and release it. Then ask the tester to replay the original chain and close variants against the fixed system, and close the finding only when every replay fails. Attach the finding entries with replay results.

evidenceHint.en: Security finding entries for each exploitable chain with severity, fix, release and the tester's replay result

text.en: Open a finding per successful chain with its severity and reproduction steps.
Choose the fix — a permission, approval step or content isolation — and its release.
Ask the tester to replay the original chain and close variants against the fix.
Close the finding only when every replay fails to reach the effect.
Raise a threat-model update when a chain reveals an attack path not yet modelled.

title.en: Compare quarterly attack coverage with every action-taking tool and taxonomy security risk

description.en: Each quarter, set the tools and risks actually attacked beside the agent's current action inventory and the taxonomy's security list. Mark tools added after the rules of engagement were written, risks left unattacked and chains fixed earlier that reappear, and feed each gap into the next quarter's objectives. Attach the coverage matrix and the gaps carried forward.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage matrix of tools and security risks attacked each quarter, with untested items, recurring chains and next-quarter objectives

text.en: Export the agent's current inventory of action-taking tools.
Mark which tools and taxonomy security risks this quarter's test reached.
List tools added after the rules of engagement were agreed.
Diff this quarter's successful chains against chains closed in earlier quarters.
Turn each untested tool or risk into an attack objective for next quarter.

templates.title: Prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts detected, alerted on and handled as incidents
templates.description: Detection rules watch the agent's live traffic — user prompts, retrieved documents and tool results — for prompt injection, jailbreak techniques and other adversarial input, and alert a named responder. Each suspected attack becomes an incident logged with its context, escalated by severity and closed with the response taken, and the rules are revised every quarter from what was seen. Optional under AIUC-1.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Security Operations Lead / AI Platform Engineering
templates.objective: To make sure adversarial input reaching the agent is noticed while the system runs, reaches somebody who acts on it, and leaves a record from detection to response.
templates.successCriteria:
Detection rules cover each technique in the adversarial technique catalogue, across user prompts, retrieved content and tool results, and are live in production.
Every rule that fires sends an alert to a named responder through a channel somebody watches.
Each suspected attack in the period has an incident record giving time, session context, rule matched, severity, escalation and the response taken.
Each quarterly review is minuted, names the incidents and techniques analysed, and links every rule change it made to a versioned commit or ticket.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the adversarial technique catalogue and the detection rule set in force, with its version history for the period.
Obtain the alert routing configuration and the responder roster it points at.
Obtain the escalation runbook and the incident tickets raised for suspected adversarial input in the period.
Obtain the minutes of each quarterly detection review and the rule changes linked to them.

Analysis:
Trace each technique in the catalogue to at least one live rule and note techniques no rule covers.
Replay a small set of known injection and jailbreak test inputs in a non-production environment and confirm the matching rules fire and alert the roster.
Sample alerts drawn from every month of the period and trace each to an incident ticket, checking severity, escalation and recorded response against the runbook.
Compare the techniques seen in each quarter's incidents with the rule changes made at the following review.

Output:
A coverage table of catalogued techniques against live rules, naming each gap.
A list of sampled alerts with no ticket, a severity the runbook does not support or no recorded response.
A statement, per quarter, of whether the review changed the rules in the light of observed attacks.

title.en: Catalogue the injection and jailbreak techniques the detection rules must recognise

description.en: Before writing rules, list the adversarial input the agent is exposed to: direct prompt injection, instructions hidden in retrieved documents, browsed pages or tool results, jailbreak framings such as role-play, obfuscated or encoded instructions, and bursts of automated attempts that run into the rate limits already set. For each technique note where it would arrive — user prompt, retrieval content, tool output — and which log carries that data. Attach the catalogue with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Technique catalogue, one row per adversarial input technique, naming the channel it arrives through and the log that records it

text.en: List the direct injection and jailbreak patterns from public research and your own red-team findings.
Add indirect injection carried in retrieved documents, browsed pages and tool results.
Include obfuscation such as encoded, translated or split instructions.
Note repeated attempts that hit the rate limits as a sign of automated probing.
Mark against each technique the input channel and the log that would show it.

title.en: Configure detection rules that alert a named responder to prompt-injection attempts

description.en: Implement a rule, signature or classifier check for each catalogued technique in the monitoring stack that reads the agent's input, retrieval and tool logs, give each a severity, and route its alerts to the responder roster through a paging or chat channel that is watched. Where the organisation runs a security operations centre, also forward the alerts to its SIEM and correlate them with sign-in and network events, as proportionate. Attach the rule export and routing configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Exported detection rule set with a severity per rule, the alert routing configuration and, where used, the SIEM forwarding and correlation rules

text.en: Write a rule, signature or classifier check for each technique in the catalogue.
Give each rule a severity that the escalation runbook will act on.
Route alerts to the responder roster through a paging or chat channel somebody watches.
Forward alerts to the SIEM and correlate them with sign-in and network logs where a SOC exists.
Fire a test input for each rule in staging and keep the resulting alert as proof.

title.en: Write the escalation runbook for suspected prompt-injection and jailbreak incidents

description.en: Set out what happens after an alert: the severity levels and who each one escalates to, the context every incident record must carry — time, user or session, the input, the rule matched, what the agent did next — the response actions open to the responder, and the system where every incident is logged and closed. Attach the approved runbook with its version and owner.

evidenceHint.en: Approved escalation runbook defining severity levels, escalation contacts, the context each incident must carry and the system of record

text.en: Define the severity levels and name the person or rota each one escalates to.
List the fields every adversarial-input incident record must hold.
Describe the response actions available, from ending a session to suspending a caller.
Name the ticketing or incident system where every case is opened and closed.
Approve the runbook and circulate it to everyone on the responder roster.

title.en: Triage each adversarial-input alert into an incident ticket with its response

description.en: Every alert the rules raise is opened as a ticket in the incident system, given a severity under the runbook, escalated where that severity requires, and closed with what was found and what was done. False alarms are closed too, with the reason, because they feed the quarterly review. Attach the incident tickets for the period with their timelines.

evidenceHint.en: Incident tickets for the quarter, each showing alert time, session context, severity, escalation and the response recorded at closure

text.en: Open a ticket for each alert with the time, the session and the rule that fired.
Set the severity under the runbook and escalate where it says to.
Note the response taken, such as session ended, caller suspended or prompt changed.
Close false alarms with the reason so the quarterly review can tune the rule.
Export the quarter's tickets with their timelines for the evidence file.

title.en: Revise the injection detection rules each quarter from the attacks actually seen

description.en: Once a quarter, go through the period's incidents, false alarms and any attacks that got through unflagged — surfaced by red-team work, evaluations or user reports — alongside newly published adversarial techniques. Change, add or retire rules, update the catalogue, minute the review and link each rule change to its versioned commit or ticket. Attach the minutes and the change list.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly detection review minutes analysing the quarter's incidents, plus every rule change linked to a versioned commit or ticket

text.en: Group the quarter's incidents and false alarms by technique and by rule.
Collect attacks that slipped past detection from red-team, evaluation and user reports.
Check newly published adversarial techniques against the catalogue.
Change, add or retire rules and commit each change with its reason.
Minute the review, listing every rule change and the incident that prompted it.

templates.title: Public statements about AI system internals approved before they are released
templates.description: Written guidelines say which technical details of the AI systems — models and suppliers, architecture, configuration, guardrails, training data, performance figures — and which organisational details such as team make-up and development timelines may be made public, and who approves each. Posts, talks, papers and other public material describing the systems are reviewed against them before release. Optional under AIUC-1.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Head of Communications / Security Engineering Lead
templates.objective: To keep public material about the organisation's AI systems from handing an attacker a usable map of their models, configuration, guardrails or the team behind them.
templates.successCriteria:
The disclosure guidelines class technical and organisational AI details as publishable, needing approval or withheld, and name the approver for each class.
Every public channel that can carry AI system details is listed with an owner who has received the guidelines.
Each item published in the period that describes AI system internals has a review record showing the reviewer, the decision and any redaction.
The annual sweep of published material finds no AI detail beyond the guidelines, or each one found was corrected or approved.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the disclosure guidelines in force and the date they were approved.
Obtain the list of public channels and their owners.
Obtain the review records for public content about the AI systems released in the period.
Obtain the results of the most recent sweep of published material and the corrections it led to.

Analysis:
Read the guidelines and confirm each class of technical and organisational detail has a stated treatment and, where approval is needed, a named approver.
Collect items about the AI systems published in the period from the website, documentation, blog, conference programmes, code repositories and job advertisements, and trace each to a review record.
Read a sample of approved items against the guidelines and note details released that the guidelines withhold or that went out without the approval they required.
Compare the channel list with the channels where items were actually found.
Compare the sweep's findings with the corrections made and check each correction is live.

Output:
A list of published items with no review record, naming the channel and date.
A list of disclosures that went beyond the guidelines, stating whether each was corrected.
A statement of channels found that the channel list omits.

title.en: Enumerate the public channels that carry details of the organisation's AI systems

description.en: AI system details reach the public through more than press releases: the engineering blog, product documentation and trust pages, conference talks and papers, open-source repositories, sales decks, social posts and job advertisements that name the stack or the team. List each channel, who publishes to it and who is accountable for it. Attach the channel list with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Channel list naming each public outlet that can describe the AI systems, who publishes to it and its accountable owner

text.en: List owned outlets: website, product documentation, blog and trust or security pages.
Add talks, papers and podcasts where staff speak about the AI systems.
Include open-source repositories, sales material and job advertisements naming the stack.
Name the publisher and the accountable owner of each channel.
Date the list and send it to every channel owner.

title.en: Draft disclosure guidelines naming which AI technical details may go public

description.en: Write guidelines that sort details of the AI systems into three treatments: publishable, publishable with approval, and withheld. Cover model and supplier identity and versions, architecture, system prompts and configuration, guardrail and detection settings, training data sources, performance and evaluation figures, and organisational details such as AI team composition and development timelines. Name the approver for each class that needs one. Attach the approved guidelines.

evidenceHint.en: Approved disclosure guidelines classing each kind of AI technical and organisational detail with its treatment and named approver

text.en: List the kinds of technical detail the systems carry, from model choice to guardrail settings.
Add organisational details such as team composition and development timelines.
Assign each kind to publishable, publishable with approval or withheld.
Name the approver for every kind that needs approval.
Have the guidelines approved and circulate them to each channel owner.

title.en: Establish the sign-off route for public content that describes the AI systems

description.en: Give channel owners one way to request review: a ticket queue or form carrying the draft, the details it discloses and the approver the guidelines name, ending in a recorded decision. Technical specifications and implementation details always pass through it. Where proportionate, add a business-justification field and extend the route to marketing and sales material that describes AI capabilities. Attach the route's description and its request template.

evidenceHint.en: Description of the review route and its request template, with fields for the draft, details disclosed, approver, decision and any justification

text.en: Choose the ticket queue or form where review requests are raised.
Add fields for the draft, the details it discloses and the decision.
Route each request to the approver the guidelines name for its class.
Decide whether marketing and sales material on AI capabilities falls in scope.
Announce the route to every owner on the channel list.

title.en: Review drafts of public AI content against the disclosure guidelines before release

description.en: For each request, the reviewer reads the draft against the guidelines, strikes or generalises withheld details, approves or declines, and records the decision together with any business justification the route asks for. Nothing describing AI system internals goes out without that record. Attach the period's review records.

evidenceHint.en: Review records for the period, one per publication, showing reviewer, decision, redactions and any business justification

text.en: Read each draft against the detail classes in the disclosure guidelines.
Strike or generalise every withheld detail and return the edit to the author.
Approve or decline the draft, adding the justification where the route asks for one.
Store the decision with the request in the review queue.
Compare the published version with the approved draft once it is live.

title.en: Sweep published websites, talks and job ads for AI details beyond the guidelines

description.en: Once a year, search every channel on the list — and any found outside it — for material describing the AI systems, check each item against the guidelines and its review record, and correct or withdraw what over-discloses. Note channels missing from the list and items that went out unreviewed. Attach the sweep results with the corrections made.

evidenceHint.en: Annual sweep results listing items checked, items over-disclosing or unreviewed, and the correction made to each

text.en: Search each listed channel for items on the AI systems published since the last sweep.
Search beyond the list, including staff talks and public code repositories.
Match each item to its review record and flag those without one.
Correct or withdraw items that disclose withheld details.
Add newly found channels to the channel list with an owner.

templates.title: External AI endpoints resistant to scraping, probing and model extraction
templates.description: Every externally reachable AI endpoint carries per-caller rate limits and quotas that tighten as behaviour turns suspicious; usage analytics tell heavy legitimate callers apart from enumeration, scraping and extraction patterns; an external penetration test exercises those protections; and each weakness the test finds is tracked from finding to a fix in production.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Engineering Lead / Application Security
templates.objective: To stop outside callers harvesting the model's behaviour or outputs at scale while heavy legitimate use carries on, and to show the protections hold under real attack.
templates.successCriteria:
Every external AI endpoint in the inventory has per-caller rate limits and quotas, with progressive restrictions for flagged callers.
Usage anomaly detection runs on each endpoint with thresholds calibrated against known heavy legitimate callers.
Each flagged scraping or extraction pattern in the period has a logged investigation and outcome.
An external penetration test in the year exercised scraping, reconnaissance and distributed high-volume attack against the endpoints.
Every test finding is tracked from identification through approved fix to production deployment, with dates.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of externally reachable AI endpoints.
Obtain the rate-limit, quota and restriction-ladder configuration for each endpoint from the gateway or WAF.
Obtain the anomaly detection rules, thresholds, calibration notes and the trusted-caller list.
Obtain the investigation log for anomaly alerts raised in the period.
Obtain the external penetration test report, its agreed scope and the issue-tracker records for its findings.

Analysis:
Compare the inventory with gateway routes and public DNS records to find external AI endpoints it omits.
Confirm each inventoried endpoint has per-caller limits applied, and send requests above a limit from a test account to see it enforced.
Read the calibration notes and trusted-caller list, and check every trusted entry was reviewed in the period.
Sample anomaly alerts from across the period and trace each to an investigation entry with a verdict.
Read the test report for scope, methodology and attack types, and trace every finding to a tracker record with approval and production deployment dates.

Output:
A table of endpoints against limits, quotas and anomaly coverage, naming each gap.
A list of sampled alerts with no investigation or verdict.
A list of test findings still open, unapproved or not yet deployed to production.

title.en: Inventory the externally reachable AI endpoints and the caller tiers each one serves

description.en: List every endpoint outside callers can reach that puts a request in front of a model — public chat interfaces, inference and agent APIs, embeddings and search endpoints — with how callers are identified on it, the caller tiers or plans it serves and the volume each tier legitimately generates. Attach the inventory with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint inventory, one row per external AI endpoint, with caller identification method, caller tiers and normal volume per tier

text.en: Pull every externally routed AI path from the API gateway and load balancer configuration.
Add public chat interfaces and embeddings or search endpoints served by a model.
Note how each endpoint identifies callers: API key, account, tenant or IP address.
Enter the caller tiers each endpoint serves and their normal request volume.
Date the inventory and name who compiled it.

title.en: Configure per-caller rate limits, quotas and progressive restrictions on AI endpoints

description.en: In the API gateway or WAF, give each endpoint per-caller request-rate limits and a quota per period sized to each tier's legitimate use, block query patterns that exceed them, and set a restriction ladder — slowing, challenging, then suspending — for callers flagged as suspicious. Where the commercial model allows, price high volumes so bulk extraction is costly. Attach the configuration for each endpoint.

evidenceHint.en: Gateway or WAF configuration per endpoint showing per-caller rate limits, quotas by tier and the restriction ladder for flagged callers

text.en: Set request-rate limits per caller identity on each inventoried endpoint.
Size a quota per period for each caller tier from its legitimate volume.
Configure the restriction ladder for flagged callers: slow, challenge, suspend.
Apply usage-based pricing above quota where the commercial model supports it.
Export each endpoint's configuration and file it against its inventory row.

title.en: Build usage anomaly detection that tells heavy legitimate callers from extraction

description.en: Profile each caller's normal behaviour and score departures that point to probing or extraction rather than ordinary heavy use: systematic sweeps across inputs, near-identical queries varying one element, many new accounts from one source, low-rate traffic spread across many identities. Calibrate thresholds against known high-volume customers, keep a reviewed list of trusted callers, and alert on high scores. Attach the detection rules and calibration notes.

evidenceHint.en: Anomaly detection rules and thresholds, calibration notes against known heavy callers, and the trusted-caller list with review dates

text.en: Baseline each caller's request volume, timing and input variety over a normal period.
Write scoring rules for input sweeps, near-duplicate queries and spread across identities.
Calibrate thresholds by replaying traffic from known heavy legitimate customers.
Keep a trusted-caller list with an owner and a review date for each entry.
Route high-score alerts to whoever is on call for endpoint protection.

title.en: Investigate flagged extraction patterns and restrict the callers responsible

description.en: For each anomaly alert, look at the caller's traffic, decide whether it is extraction, scraping, probing or legitimate heavy use, and either apply the matching step on the restriction ladder or clear the alert with a reason. For false positives, raise the threshold or trusted-caller change they call for. Attach the investigation log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Investigation log for the period, one entry per anomaly alert, with the verdict and the restriction applied or the reason for clearing

text.en: Pull the flagged caller's traffic and compare it with its tier's baseline.
Classify the activity as extraction, scraping, probing or legitimate heavy use.
Apply the matching restriction step, or clear the alert with a reason.
Raise a threshold or trusted-caller change for each false positive.
Close the log entry with the verdict and the action taken.

title.en: Commission an external penetration test of the AI endpoints' anti-scraping defences

description.en: Engage an outside tester to attack the inventoried endpoints the way a scraper or extractor would: reconnaissance, automated scraping, brute-force key or account attempts, evasion of rate limits and anomaly detection, and high-volume distributed traffic, under a methodology fitted to the organisation's threat profile. The report must state what was tested, how, and how well each protection held. Attach the report and the agreed scope.

evidenceHint.en: External penetration test report for the AI endpoints giving scope, methodology, the attack scenarios run and findings on how well protections held

text.en: Agree a test scope covering every endpoint in the inventory.
Specify reconnaissance, scraping, brute-force and distributed high-volume scenarios.
Ask the tester to attempt evasion of rate limits and anomaly detection explicitly.
Receive the report with its methodology and a severity for each finding.
File the report and scope beside the endpoint inventory.

title.en: Close each endpoint pentest finding with a fix tracked through to production

description.en: Open an issue for every finding in the test report and take it through the full lifecycle in the tracker: the finding as identified, the proposed fix, its approval, the implementing change and the production deployment, each dated. Fold any resulting change to limits or detection thresholds back into the endpoint configuration. Attach the tracker export covering all findings.

evidenceHint.en: Issue-tracker export for every pentest finding showing identification, proposed fix, approval, implementation and production deployment dates

text.en: Open one tracker issue per finding with its severity and the report reference.
Add the proposed fix and capture its approval in the issue.
Link the implementing change and the date it reached production.
Update limits and anomaly thresholds the finding showed to be weak.
Export the tracker view showing every finding's state at year end.

templates.title: Input screened by a moderation layer before the model acts on it
templates.description: An automated moderation layer — a moderation API, custom rules or both — screens all input before the model sees it and blocks, warns on or modifies flagged content under thresholds set per risk category. Where proportionate, the choices are justified in writing, users are told when input is stopped, flagged input is logged within privacy limits and error rates are measured. Optional under AIUC-1; applies to agents that generate text, speech or images.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Engineering Lead / Trust & Safety
templates.objective: To stop harmful or manipulative input before the model processes it, using moderation actions and thresholds the organisation chose on purpose and can explain.
templates.successCriteria:
Every route by which input reaches the model passes through the moderation layer, and none bypasses it.
Each moderated category has a configured action of block, warn or modify and a confidence threshold, matching the rationale where one is kept.
Where adopted, users whose input is blocked or altered see a message saying so and what they can do next.
Where adopted, flagged inputs are logged with a defined field set that masks personal data, under a stated retention period.
Where adopted, filter error rates are measured in the period and each threshold change carries a date and reason.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the map of input routes to the model and the moderation configuration in force: categories, actions and thresholds.
Obtain the moderation rationale, where one is kept.
Obtain screenshots or recordings of the messages users see for blocked, warned and modified input.
Obtain the flagged-input log schema, its retention setting and a sample of its entries.
Obtain the most recent filter performance report and the threshold change log.

Analysis:
Compare the route map with the application's architecture and API routes to find any path to the model that skips moderation.
Submit test inputs from each moderated category through each route in a test environment and confirm the configured action is taken.
Compare configured thresholds with the rationale and the change log, noting values changed without a recorded reason.
Read a sample of flagged-input log entries for fields the schema says are masked or excluded.
Recompute false-positive and false-negative rates from the labelled sample behind the performance report.

Output:
A route-by-route statement of moderation coverage, naming any bypass.
A category table of configured against documented action and threshold.
A list of log entries carrying fields that should be masked, and the recomputed error rates beside those reported.

title.en: Map every path by which user input reaches the model to its moderation check

description.en: Input reaches the model by more than the chat box: API calls, uploaded files turned into text, voice transcripts, form fields fed into prompts and messages relayed from other systems. Trace each path from entry point to model call and mark whether the moderation layer sits on it. Attach the route map, with every unscreened path flagged.

evidenceHint.en: Route map of every input path to the model, showing for each whether the moderation layer screens it before the model call

text.en: List each entry point: chat UI, API, uploads, voice transcripts and relayed messages.
Trace each from entry to the model call in the code or gateway configuration.
Mark where the moderation call sits on each path.
Flag every path that reaches the model without passing moderation.
Date the map and hand it to the owner of the moderation integration.

title.en: Deploy the input moderation layer with a threshold and action per risk category

description.en: Integrate the chosen moderation API or custom rules on every mapped path so screening completes before the model call, then set for each risk category and severity the action — block, warn or modify — and the confidence threshold that triggers it. Where proportionate, write a short rationale for the tool chosen, each threshold and the action per category, with example inputs. Attach the configuration and, where kept, the rationale.

evidenceHint.en: Moderation configuration showing categories, the block, warn or modify action and the confidence threshold per category, plus the rationale where kept

text.en: Choose the moderation API, custom rules or a combination, and note why.
Call the moderation check on every mapped path before the model is invoked.
Set the action and the confidence threshold for each category and severity.
Write example inputs for each category showing the action they receive.
Export the configuration and file it with the route map.

title.en: Write the message a user sees when moderation blocks or rewrites their input

description.en: Where proportionate, give users clear feedback when the filter acts: for a block, that the input was not processed and why in general terms; for a warning or modification, what changed; and in each case what they can do instead. Show it on every surface the route map lists. Attach screenshots or recordings of each message in the product.

evidenceHint.en: Screenshots or recordings of the user-facing message for a blocked, a warned and a modified input on each product surface

text.en: Draft a message for each moderation action: block, warn and modify.
Explain in general terms why the input was stopped and what the user can try instead.
Wire the message into every surface the route map lists, voice included.
Capture a screenshot or recording of each message in the live product.

title.en: Log flagged inputs with privacy-limited fields so moderation thresholds can be tuned

description.en: Where proportionate, capture each flagged input in a log the team uses to refine the filter: category, score, action, time and a pseudonymous session reference, with personal data masked or excluded, a retention period set and access restricted to those tuning the filter. Check the privacy notice discloses this logging. Attach the log schema, retention setting and a sample of entries.

evidenceHint.en: Flagged-input log schema with masked or excluded fields, its retention setting, its access list and a sample of the period's entries

text.en: Define the fields captured for each flagged input and those left out.
Mask personal data before entries are written to the log.
Set a retention period and restrict access to the people tuning the filter.
Check that the privacy notice tells users flagged input is logged.
Export a sample of the period's entries for the evidence file.

title.en: Measure moderation false positives, false negatives and latency, then retune thresholds

description.en: Where proportionate, once in each review period label a sample of flagged and unflagged inputs, compute false-positive and false-negative rates per category and the latency the filter adds, and adjust thresholds where the rates warrant it. Log each change with its date, old and new value and reason. Attach the performance report and the threshold change log.

evidenceHint.en: Filter performance report with per-category false-positive and false-negative rates and latency, plus the dated threshold change log with reasons

text.en: Draw a sample of flagged and unflagged inputs for each moderated category.
Label each sampled input as correctly or wrongly handled by the filter.
Compute per-category error rates and the latency the filter adds.
Adjust the thresholds whose error rates justify a change.
Log each change with its date, old and new value and the reason.

templates.title: Agent reach confined to approved services, with execution contained and breaches alerted
templates.description: For agents that take actions, technical controls decide which backend systems, APIs and MCP servers each agent can reach: gateway and egress rules, network policy and narrowly granted service accounts. The agent's service calls are logged and an attempt to reach beyond its approved set raises an alert that someone investigates. Where proportionate, code the agent executes runs in a sandbox with limited files, network and credentials.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Platform Lead / Security Engineering
templates.objective: To ensure an agent that takes actions can reach only the services it is approved for, that code it runs is contained, and that any attempt to go further is detected and followed up.
templates.successCriteria:
Each agent has a catalogue of the services, APIs and MCP servers it is approved to reach, naming the service account it uses.
Gateway rules, network policy and service-account grants block every destination outside the catalogue, sensitive systems included.
The agent's calls to services and its authentication attempts are logged, and any attempt on an uncatalogued destination raises an alert.
Every such alert raised in the period was investigated and closed with a recorded cause and action.
Where proportionate, agent-executed code runs in a sandbox with file, network and credential limits set in configuration.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved-service catalogue for each agent and the service accounts it names.
Obtain the API gateway or egress rules, network policies, MCP server registration settings and service-account permission exports for each agent.
Obtain the logging and alert-rule configuration for agent service interactions, and the alerts raised in the period with their investigation records.
Obtain the sandbox configuration for agent-executed code, where a sandbox is in use.

Analysis:
Compare each agent's gateway, network and service-account permissions with its catalogue and list every destination allowed but not catalogued.
From one agent's runtime, attempt a connection to an uncatalogued service and confirm it is blocked, logged and alerted.
Sample alerts raised in the period and confirm each was investigated and closed with a cause and action.
Compare the destinations agents actually reached, from the logs, with the catalogue to find any reached without approval.
Where a sandbox is used, run a test job that writes outside its allowed paths, opens an unlisted connection and reads a host credential, and confirm each is refused.

Output:
A per-agent table of catalogued against technically permitted destinations, naming every gap.
The results of the blocked-connection and sandbox tests.
A list of alerts left uninvestigated or open, and of destinations reached without approval.

title.en: Catalogue the backend systems, APIs and MCP servers each agent is approved to reach

description.en: For each agent that takes actions, list every backend service, internal or external API and MCP server it needs to do its job, the operations it needs on each and the service account or credential it uses. Separately list the systems it must never reach, such as payment, identity or production data stores, whatever its task. Attach the catalogue with its date and the approval each destination rests on.

evidenceHint.en: Approved-service catalogue per agent naming each service, API or MCP server, the operations needed, the service account used and the systems the agent must never reach

text.en: List every service, API and MCP server each action-taking agent calls in production.
Write the operations the agent needs on each destination, such as read or create.
Name the service account or credential the agent uses for each destination.
List the sensitive systems the agent must never reach, whatever its task.
Date the catalogue and note the approval behind each destination.

title.en: Restrict each agent's network egress and service accounts to its catalogued destinations

description.en: Turn the catalogue into technical limits. Route agent traffic through an API gateway or egress proxy with one allow rule per catalogued destination and a default deny, apply network policy so agent workloads cannot open connections around it, register only catalogued MCP servers with the agent platform, and cut service-account permissions down to the operations listed. Attach the gateway rules, network policies, MCP registration settings and permission exports.

evidenceHint.en: API gateway or egress rules with a default deny, network policies for agent workloads, MCP server registration settings and service-account permission exports matching the catalogue

text.en: Send agent traffic through a gateway or egress proxy that denies by default.
Add one allow rule per catalogued destination and nothing beyond it.
Apply network policy so agent workloads cannot connect around the gateway.
Register only catalogued MCP servers with the agent platform.
Cut each service account's permissions to the operations the catalogue lists.

title.en: Deploy a sandbox for agent-executed code that limits its files, network and credentials

description.en: Where the agent writes and runs code, or the organisation hosts its own MCP servers, and the deployment calls for it, run that code in a container or sandbox kept apart from the agent host, with the filesystem paths it may use, its outbound network and the credentials it can see all set in configuration. Where proportionate, also scan agent hook, skill and rule files for injected instructions before they load. Attach the sandbox configuration and any artefact-scan settings.

evidenceHint.en: Sandbox or container configuration for code the agent runs and for MCP servers the organisation hosts, showing allowed paths, outbound network and visible credentials, plus artefact-scan settings where used

text.en: Run agent-executed code in a container or sandbox separate from the agent host.
Set the filesystem paths the sandbox may read and write, denying all others.
Block outbound network from the sandbox except to catalogued destinations.
Withhold host and platform credentials from the sandbox environment.
Scan agent hook, skill and rule files for injected instructions before loading them.

title.en: Configure alerts on agent connections to uncatalogued services and unusual connection patterns

description.en: Log every agent service call and authentication attempt with the agent, destination, operation and result, and forward the logs to the security monitoring platform. Write alert rules for blocked or attempted connections to destinations outside the catalogue, failed authentication by agent service accounts and connection patterns unusual for that agent, and, where proportionate, for tool definitions on an approved MCP server changing after approval. Attach the logging and alert-rule configuration with each rule's routing.

evidenceHint.en: Logging configuration covering each agent's calls to services and its authentication attempts, and alert rules for uncatalogued destinations, failed authentication and unusual patterns, with routing

text.en: Log each agent service call with agent, destination, operation, result and time.
Forward agent service and authentication logs to the security monitoring platform.
Alert on blocked or attempted connections to destinations outside the catalogue.
Alert on connection volume or destinations unlike each agent's normal pattern.
Alert where an approved MCP server's tool definitions change after approval.
Route each alert rule to a named owner in the security team.

title.en: Investigate each alert raised when an agent reaches for an uncatalogued service

description.en: Work every alert the boundary rules raise. Identify the agent, the task and the input that led to the attempt; decide whether the cause was a misconfiguration, a destination missing from the catalogue or misuse of the agent; act on that cause; and close the alert with what was found and done. A destination is added to the catalogue only through its normal approval, never straight from an alert. Attach the alert register for the period with each outcome.

evidenceHint.en: Register of agent boundary alerts raised in the period, each with the agent, attempted destination, cause found, action taken and closure date

text.en: Identify the agent, task and input that produced each boundary alert.
Classify the cause as misconfiguration, missing catalogue entry or misuse.
Send any new destination through the catalogue's normal approval, not the alert.
Close each alert with its cause, the action taken and the date.

title.en: Reconcile observed agent connections and service-account grants with the approved catalogue

description.en: Once a year, pull a period of agent connection logs and the current permission exports for every agent service account, and compare both with the catalogue. List destinations reached that the catalogue lacks, permissions granted beyond the listed operations and catalogue entries no longer used. Attempt one blocked connection from an agent's runtime to confirm the rule and its alert still fire. Attach the reconciliation with each gap, its fix and owner.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of logged agent connections and service-account permissions against the catalogue, with the blocked-connection test result and each gap's fix and owner

text.en: Export a period of agent connection logs and the current service-account permissions.
List destinations agents reached that the catalogue does not contain.
List permissions granted beyond the operations each catalogue entry names.
Attempt one blocked connection and confirm it is refused, logged and alerted.
Mark catalogue entries unused in the period for removal.

templates.title: People's access to AI prompts, models, data and admin functions role-based and recertified quarterly
templates.description: Which staff, contractors and administrators can view or change the AI system's prompts, model configuration, training and evaluation data, tool settings, prompt and response logs and admin functions is decided by role- or attribute-based rules taken from the access policy. Rights to change the system's behaviour sit with named administrators, and every person's access is recertified each quarter with the reason for each change kept.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: IAM Lead / AI Platform Owner
templates.objective: To ensure only people whose job function needs it can see or change each part of the AI system, and that their access is checked every quarter and corrected with a stated reason.
templates.successCriteria:
Every AI system resource people can reach, from prompts and model settings to datasets, logs and the admin console, is inventoried with its sensitivity.
A role matrix taken from the access policy says which job functions may view or change each resource, and IAM configuration implements it.
Rights to change prompts, tools, models or agent behaviour are held only by administrators named in the matrix.
A review in each quarter confirmed or removed every person's access, with the reason for each change written down.
Permissions checked after each review match the matrix and the removals that review decided.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the AI system resource inventory and the role matrix, with the access policy they are taken from.
Obtain exports of IAM role assignments, permission policies and admin-console users for each inventoried resource.
Obtain the access review records for each quarter in the period, with decisions, reasons and the tickets that carried out changes.
Obtain the joiner, mover and leaver records for people who held AI system access during the period.

Analysis:
Compare the IAM exports with the role matrix and list every person whose access exceeds their job function.
List the holders of change rights over prompts, tools, models or behaviour settings and confirm each is a named administrator in the matrix.
Confirm a review took place in each quarter of the period and covered every person in the exports.
Trace a sample of removals and changes decided in reviews to the permission state that followed.
Compare leaver and mover records with the exports to find access that outlived the person's role or engagement.

Output:
A list of people holding access beyond the matrix, with the resource involved.
A statement of which quarters were reviewed and which people each review missed.
A list of review decisions not carried out, and of leavers or movers still holding access.

title.en: Inventory the AI system's prompts, models, datasets, logs and admin functions by sensitivity

description.en: List every part of the AI system a person can reach: system prompts and prompt templates, model selection and configuration, training, fine-tuning and evaluation datasets, tool and integration settings, prompt and response logs, and the admin console. Rate each one's sensitivity on the organisation's classification scheme and name the system that grants access to it. Attach the inventory with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of AI system resources people can reach, each with its sensitivity rating and the system that grants access to it

text.en: List the prompts, templates and model configuration settings people can view or edit.
Add training, fine-tuning and evaluation datasets and where each one is stored.
Add tool and integration settings, prompt and response logs and the admin console.
Rate each resource's sensitivity on the organisation's classification scheme.
Name the system that grants access to each resource, such as the IAM platform.

title.en: Define which job functions may view or change each AI system resource in a role matrix

description.en: From the access policy, draw up a matrix with job functions or user attributes down one side, the inventoried resources across the other, and none, view, change or administer in each cell. Then configure the IAM platform, admin console and data stores so that their roles or attribute policies implement the matrix, with the application checking authorisation before it serves a sensitive resource. Attach the matrix and the matching IAM configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Role matrix taken from the access policy, giving view, change or administer per job function and resource, with IAM role and permission-policy exports implementing it

text.en: List the job functions or user attributes the access policy recognises.
Fill each matrix cell with none, view, change or administer for that resource.
Give the most sensitive resources, such as prompt and response logs, to the fewest functions.
Configure IAM roles or attribute policies to match each cell of the matrix.
Check authorisation in the application before it serves a sensitive resource.

title.en: Restrict rights to change the agent's prompts, tools, models and behaviour to named administrators

description.en: Separate administrative and configuration rights from everyday use. Limit who can edit system prompts, enable or disable tools, switch or retrain models and alter guardrail or behaviour settings to the administrators the role matrix names, through dedicated admin roles rather than broad platform roles that carry these rights incidentally. Attach the list of administrators, the admin roles each holds and the configuration that grants them.

evidenceHint.en: List of named administrators holding change rights over prompts, tools, models and behaviour settings, with the admin-role configuration that grants them

text.en: Create admin roles for prompt, tool, model and behaviour changes, apart from user roles.
Assign those roles only to the administrators named in the role matrix.
Remove change rights carried by broad platform roles such as project owner.
Export the admin-role assignments and file them beside the role matrix.

title.en: Recertify every person's access to the AI system in the quarterly access review

description.en: Each quarter, export everyone holding access to an inventoried resource and give each resource owner their list.
