description.en: Where the deployment calls for it, run detection rules over output before delivery for text written to instruct another model or agent, payloads aimed at downstream systems such as SQL or shell commands, and exploits hidden by encoding or unusual characters. Log each hit with the rule and the action taken, and tune the rules each quarter from the hits and from newly reported techniques. Attach the rule set and the quarter's hit summary.

evidenceHint.en: Output-scanning rule set and the quarter's hit summary, showing rule, destination and action for each hit, with the rule changes made

text.en: Write rules for instruction-like text aimed at another model or agent.
Add signatures for SQL, shell and template payloads aimed at downstream systems.
Decode common encodings and normalise characters before matching.
Log each hit with the rule, destination and action taken.
Tune the rules each quarter from the hits and newly reported techniques.

title.en: Test each output destination quarterly with script, link and shell payloads and confirm none executes

description.en: Each quarter, prompt the agent to emit a standard payload set through every inventoried destination — script tags and event handlers, links with disallowed schemes, image links to an outside host, shell metacharacters in suggested commands, malformed structured output — and inject the same payloads through a retrieved document and a tool result. Note whether each arrived inert and labelled, check for destinations added since the inventory, and agree a fix for each failure. Attach the results matrix and fixes.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly destination-by-payload results showing each payload inert or executed and labelled or not, with new destinations and fixes

text.en: Prompt the agent to emit each payload through every inventoried destination.
Inject the same payloads through a retrieved document and a tool result.
Mark each payload inert or executed, and labelled or unlabelled, at each destination.
Check the product for destinations added since the inventory was dated.
Open a fix with an owner for every payload that executed.

templates.title: Outputs risky enough to need a person are held and routed to a reviewer before release
templates.description: Written criteria drawn from the risk taxonomy say which outputs need a person's review — advice above a value the organisation sets, medical, legal or safety subjects, reputational triggers. Flagging rules detect them as they occur and hold them in a review queue before they reach the user or take effect, and reviewers decide each one through a defined workflow. Optional under AIUC-1.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Head of Operations for the Agent / AI Platform Engineering Lead
templates.objective: To put a reviewer between the agent and any output its criteria mark as high-risk, so that output is examined before it reaches the user or takes effect.
templates.successCriteria:
Written criteria, each tied to a risk taxonomy category, define which outputs need human review.
Every criterion has a flagging rule that holds matching outputs in the review queue until a reviewer decides.
Each flagged output has a recorded decision, the reviewer who made it and how long it waited.
A sample of released outputs contains no output that met a criterion without being flagged, or a fix is recorded for each one found.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the human-review criteria with the taxonomy category each one draws on.
Obtain the flagging rule, classifier or risk-scoring configuration and the hold mechanism that keeps flagged output from release.
Obtain the reviewer assignments, the escalation path and the review queue records for the period.
Obtain the organisation's own sample of unreviewed released outputs and its findings.

Analysis:
Map each criterion to a flagging rule and note any criterion with none.
Submit crafted requests that meet each criterion and confirm the output is held, queued and not released before a decision.
Select a sample of queue records across reviewers and criteria and check each has a decision, a reviewer and timestamps.
Draw a random sample of released outputs from the period, apply the criteria by hand and identify any that should have been flagged.
Where a review workflow is defined, check that sampled escalated cases followed its escalation path.

Output:
A criterion-by-criterion table of flagging rule and test result.
The queue sample results, naming any record missing a decision, reviewer or timestamp.
A list of released outputs that met a criterion without being flagged.

title.en: Write the criteria that make an agent output need a person's review, from the risk taxonomy

description.en: Starting from the risk taxonomy, and from the categories whose high-risk response is escalation, write criteria a rule can test: advice or a recommendation above a value the organisation sets, a subject in a medical, legal or safety domain, or wording that could harm the organisation's reputation. Give each criterion the taxonomy category it rests on and an example output on each side of it. Attach the dated criteria.

evidenceHint.en: Human-review criteria document, each criterion naming its taxonomy category, the condition a rule can test and example outputs

text.en: List the taxonomy categories, including those mapped to escalation, that call for a person.
Write each criterion as a condition a rule or classifier can test.
Set the value or domain that triggers review for each criterion, in the organisation's terms.
Add an example output that meets each criterion and one that does not.
Date the criteria and note the taxonomy version they draw on.

title.en: Route outputs matching the review criteria into a held queue before they reach the user

description.en: Implement a flagging rule for each criterion — a keyword or pattern list, a scoring rule, or a classifier with a threshold — and connect it to a queue that holds the output, or the action it would trigger, until a reviewer releases, edits or rejects it. Write a flag record with the criterion matched and the score, and decide what the user sees while the output waits. Attach the rule configuration and an example flag record.

evidenceHint.en: Flagging rule configuration per criterion and the queue hold mechanism, with an example flag record showing criterion and score

text.en: Implement a flagging rule or classifier threshold for each written criterion.
Connect matched outputs to a queue that holds them until a reviewer decides.
Write a flag record with the criterion matched, the score and the time flagged.
Configure what the user sees while an output waits for review.
Confirm escalations from the high-risk response mapping arrive in the same queue.

title.en: Assign reviewers, an escalation path and a decision record to the flagged-output queue

description.en: Where the deployment calls for a formal workflow, name the reviewers for each criterion and their cover, the escalation path for cases a first reviewer cannot settle, and the decision options — release, edit and release, reject — with the reason each decision must carry. Timestamp entry and decision so waiting time can be tracked and the workflow's effectiveness judged. Attach the review runbook and the queue's assignment configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Review runbook naming reviewers per criterion, the escalation path and decision options, and the queue assignment configuration

text.en: Name the reviewers and their cover for each criterion.
Define the escalation path for cases a first reviewer cannot settle.
Set the decision options and the reason field each decision must fill.
Configure queue assignment so each flagged output reaches the right reviewer.
Timestamp queue entry and decision so the waiting time is tracked.

title.en: Triage flagged outputs in the review queue and log each decision, reviewer and waiting time

description.en: As flagged outputs arrive, a reviewer reads each with its context and releases, edits or rejects it, and the decision is stored with the reviewer and the reason. Where the deployment runs the formal workflow, escalate the cases its runbook marks and keep the waiting time on each record. At the end of each period, export the queue records showing decisions, waiting times and items still open. Attach the period's queue export.

evidenceHint.en: Period export of review-queue records showing each flagged output's decision, reviewer, reason and waiting time, plus items still open

text.en: Read each flagged output with the conversation and criterion that flagged it.
Release, edit or reject the output and enter the reason in the queue.
Escalate the cases the runbook marks for escalation and note the hand-off.
Export the queue records at period end with their waiting times.
List items still open and chase the reviewers holding them.

title.en: Sample unflagged released outputs for ones that met the review criteria but skipped the queue

description.en: Once a year, draw a random sample of outputs released without review, apply the written criteria by hand and list any that should have been flagged. Check the queue records for decisions without a reason or reviewer and for waits longer than the agent's business owner accepts, then adjust the flagging rules or the workflow for each gap found. Attach the sample, the misses and the changes made.

evidenceHint.en: Sample of unreviewed released outputs judged against the criteria, missed flags found, queue record gaps, and the rule or workflow changes made

text.en: Draw a random sample of outputs released without review during the period.
Apply the written criteria to each sampled output by hand.
List outputs that met a criterion but were never flagged.
Check queue records for missing reasons, missing reviewers and long waits.
Change the flagging rules or workflow for each gap and note the change.

templates.title: Live agent output sampled and trended against every risk taxonomy category
templates.description: Optional under AIUC-1. Production output is sampled at rates set by the severity of each risk taxonomy category, labelled against those categories and trended, so a rising failure rate or an unfamiliar failure is spotted and referred to the taxonomy owner; where the organisation runs security operations, flagged outputs and alerts reach its tooling.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Safety Lead / Security Operations
templates.objective: To notice from the agent's live output when failures in any risk taxonomy category grow more frequent or take a new form, and to feed each such finding back to the taxonomy.
templates.successCriteria:
Every current risk taxonomy category has a monitoring method, a sampling rate or evaluation frequency set by its severity, and an owner.
Outputs were sampled at the planned rates all period, and each one carries a category label or a no-issue label.
Failure rates are trended per category, and each flagged rise or unfamiliar failure has a recorded investigation and outcome.
New or misfiled scenarios found by monitoring reach the taxonomy owner with examples, and the decision on each is recorded.
Where security operations exist, flagged outputs and alerts arrive in the security platform in a structured format.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current risk taxonomy with its categories and severities, and the monitoring plan that gives each category a method, a sampling rate and an owner.
Obtain the sampling job configuration, the sampled outputs and their reviewer labels for the period.
Obtain the per-category trend reports for the period and the investigation record for every flagged rise.
Obtain the referrals made to the taxonomy owner and the taxonomy change history.
Where security tooling is connected, obtain the forwarding configuration and the AI events the security platform received.

Analysis:
Compare the monitoring plan with the taxonomy and list every category that lacks a method, a rate or an owner.
Check that higher-severity categories are sampled or evaluated at least as often as lower-severity ones, as the plan states.
For a sample of weeks across the period, count the outputs drawn against the planned rate and confirm each carries a label.
Trace every flagged rise and a sample of unfamiliar-failure labels to an investigation record with an outcome.
Trace each referral to a taxonomy change or to a recorded decision to leave the taxonomy unchanged.
Select a sample of flagged outputs and locate each one in the security platform.

Output:
A category-by-category coverage table of method, rate, owner and samples actually drawn.
A list of periods where sampling fell short of plan, and of flags with no investigation.
A list of referrals with no recorded decision, and of flagged outputs missing from the security platform.

title.en: Assign a production monitoring method and sampling rate to every risk taxonomy category

description.en: Take the current risk taxonomy and decide, category by category, how it will be watched in production: human review of a random sample, an automated classifier whose hits a person confirms, or a scheduled evaluation run over recent traffic. Set the sampling rate or evaluation frequency by severity, so the most severe categories are looked at most often, and name the owner who acts on findings for each. Attach the monitoring plan.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring plan listing every taxonomy category with its severity, monitoring method, sampling rate or evaluation frequency, and owner

text.en: Export the current risk taxonomy with each category's severity and its example failures.
Choose a method per category: sampled human review, classifier with confirmation, or evaluation run.
Set each category's sampling rate or evaluation frequency in step with its severity.
Name the owner who acts on monitoring findings for each category.
Date the plan and note the taxonomy version it was written against.

title.en: Configure production output sampling that queues agent outputs for risk-category labels

description.en: Build the job that draws agent outputs from production at the rates in the monitoring plan, together with the prompt and context a reviewer needs to judge them, and places them in a review queue. Give reviewers a label set made of the taxonomy categories plus 'no issue' and 'fits no category', and store every label with the reviewer and the date. This is after-the-fact measurement, separate from any review that holds an output before it reaches the user. Attach the job configuration and label schema.

evidenceHint.en: Sampling job configuration showing the planned rates, the label schema reviewers apply, and a sample of stored labelled records

text.en: Set the job's draw rates from the monitoring plan, per category where a classifier pre-sorts output.
Include the prompt, retrieved context and tool results a reviewer needs beside each output.
Load the taxonomy categories, 'no issue' and 'fits no category' as the reviewer label set.
Store each label against the output identifier with the reviewer's name and the date.
Run the job over one day of traffic and confirm the queue fills at the planned rates.

title.en: Connect flagged agent outputs and monitoring alerts to the security operations platform

description.en: Where the organisation runs security operations and the deployment calls for it, forward monitoring alerts, and outputs labelled in security-relevant categories, to the security event platform already in use. Emit them in a structured format that platform parses, carrying the taxonomy category, severity, agent and session identifiers, so analysts can correlate them with the rest of their telemetry. Attach the forwarding configuration and a view of AI events arriving in the platform.

evidenceHint.en: Forwarding or integration configuration for AI monitoring events, the event schema used, and the security platform's view of the AI events it received

text.en: Agree with security operations which taxonomy categories and alert types they receive.
Map each forwarded event to a structured schema the security platform already parses.
Carry category, severity, agent identifier and session identifier on every event.
Configure the forwarding rule and push a test event through it.
Save a search or dashboard in the platform that shows AI events beside other telemetry.

title.en: Label sampled production outputs by risk category and trend each category's failure rate

description.en: In each monitoring cycle, have reviewers label every queued output, then work out the share of sampled outputs falling into each category and set it against earlier cycles. Run the scheduled evaluations the plan assigns in the same cycle. Flag any category whose rate rises past the rule its owner set, and every output labelled 'fits no category', and open an investigation for each flag. Attach the cycle's trend report and its investigation records.

evidenceHint.en: Per-cycle trend report of failure rate by taxonomy category against earlier cycles, with each flag raised and the investigation opened for it

text.en: Clear the review queue and confirm every sampled output carries a label.
Compute each category's failure rate for the cycle and chart it against earlier cycles.
Run the scheduled evaluations for the categories the plan assigns to evaluation.
Flag rises past each owner's rule and every output that fits no category.
Open an investigation per flag and enter its outcome when it closes.

title.en: Refer new failure scenarios found in production monitoring to the taxonomy owner

description.en: Where proportionate, write up each scenario monitoring surfaces that the taxonomy does not describe, or files under the wrong category or severity, with de-identified examples from the sampled outputs and links to any related incident reports. Send it to the taxonomy owner, who decides whether to add, split, re-rate or leave a category, and keep the scenario and that decision together so the taxonomy's change history can point back to it. Attach the scenario log with its decisions.

evidenceHint.en: Scenario log entries with examples drawn from monitoring, each showing the taxonomy owner's decision and the taxonomy version that reflects it

text.en: Write up each new or misfiled scenario with de-identified example outputs from the sample.
Link the incident reports and investigation records that relate to the scenario.
Send the scenario to the taxonomy owner and log the date it was referred.
Enter the owner's decision: add, split, re-rate or leave the category as it is.
Cite against the scenario the taxonomy version that carries any change.

title.en: Reconcile the monitoring plan with the current taxonomy and the samples actually drawn

description.en: Once a year, check the monitoring plan against the latest taxonomy for categories added or re-rated without a method or rate, and set the samples actually drawn per category over the year beside the planned rates. Confirm every flag led to an investigation and every referral received a decision and, where security tooling is connected, that a sample of flagged outputs can be found there. Attach the reconciliation with each gap, its fix and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Annual reconciliation of plan, taxonomy and samples drawn, listing each gap found with its agreed fix, owner and target date

text.en: List taxonomy categories added or re-rated since the plan was last updated.
Compare the samples drawn per category over the year with the planned rates.
Check every flag for an investigation and every referral for a recorded decision.
Search the security platform for a sample of flagged outputs where forwarding applies.
Enter each gap with its agreed fix, owner and target date.

templates.title: Users can stop, pause or redirect the agent mid-task and report problems through accessible controls
templates.description: On every interface where people use the agent, they can stop or pause it while it works, redirect it, and report a problem with what it produced; those controls work by keyboard and screen reader and hold across devices and sessions. Where proportionate, the feedback and intervention records are analysed each quarter and turned into fixes. Optional under AIUC-1.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Product Owner for the Agent / Front-end Engineering Lead
templates.objective: To give users a working, accessible way to halt or steer the agent and to report what went wrong, and to act on what those reports and interventions show.
templates.successCriteria:
Each interface where users run the agent offers stop, pause or redirect controls and a problem report, as the interface inventory records.
Stopping halts the agent's in-progress work, pending tool calls included, and the stop holds when the user switches device or session.
The intervention and report controls pass keyboard-only, screen-reader and contrast checks against the accessibility standard the organisation follows.
Where feedback review is in place, each quarter's reports and interventions are categorised and the actions taken trace back to them.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of interfaces with the intervention and report controls each one offers.
Obtain the design and implementation of stop, pause, redirect and the problem report, including how intervention state is shared across devices and sessions.
Obtain the quarter's accessibility test results, intervention event log and problem-report records.
Obtain the quarter's feedback analysis and the backlog items raised from it, where review is in place.

Analysis:
Compare the inventory with the product's interfaces and note any interface lacking a control.
On each interface, start a multi-step task, use stop, pause and redirect, and confirm from the event and tool-call logs that work halted or changed as directed.
Start a task on one device, stop it from another and confirm the stop holds.
Operate each control by keyboard only and with a screen reader, and check its contrast.
Submit a problem report and trace it to its stored record.
Select a sample of the quarter's reports and confirm each was categorised and, where warranted, linked to an action.

Output:
An interface-by-control table marking each control present, working and accessible.
A list of interventions that failed to halt or redirect the agent, and of reports not traced to a record.
The sample results for feedback categorisation and action.

title.en: Inventory each interface where users run the agent and the intervention controls it offers

description.en: List every way people use the agent — web and mobile apps, chat integrations, voice, the API for customers who build on it — and note against each whether a user can stop, pause or redirect the agent while it works and report a problem with an output, and where intervention state is held. Mark each missing control as a gap with an owner. Attach the dated inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Dated inventory of user interfaces showing for each whether stop, pause, redirect and problem report are available, and the gaps with owners

text.en: List every interface through which users start or watch agent work.
Check each interface for stop, pause, redirect and problem-report controls.
Note where intervention state is held and whether other devices read it.
Mark each missing control as a gap and name the owner who will close it.
Date the inventory so the quarterly test runs against the current list.

title.en: Build stop, pause and redirect controls that halt the agent's in-flight work on every interface

description.en: Make each control act on the agent's run rather than only the display: stop cancels pending steps and tool calls, pause holds the run until the user resumes, and redirect lets the user change the instruction mid-task. Store intervention state with the run so a stop issued on one device or session holds on all of them, and give each control a visible label, keyboard access and a screen-reader name. Attach the design note and a recording or log showing each control taking effect.

evidenceHint.en: Design note for stop, pause and redirect with run-level state handling, and a recording or event log showing each control halting or changing a run

text.en: Wire stop to cancel the run's pending steps and tool calls on the server.
Implement pause as a held run state that resumes only on the user's action.
Let redirect replace the instruction for the remaining steps of the run.
Store intervention state with the run so every device and session reads it.
Give each control a visible label, keyboard focus and a screen-reader name.

title.en: Add a problem report to agent responses that captures the output and the user's concern

description.en: Put a report control beside each response, with an equivalent route for voice and API users, that records the output, the conversation reference and the user's description, lets them pick a concern type, and confirms receipt. Store reports where the review team can query them, copying no more personal data than the report needs, and build the control to the same accessibility bar as the intervention controls. Attach screenshots and the report record schema.

evidenceHint.en: Screenshots of the problem-report control on each interface and the schema of the record each report creates

text.en: Place a report control beside each agent response on every interface.
Offer an equivalent reporting route for voice and API users.
Capture the output, conversation reference, concern type and user description.
Store reports where the review team can query them by type and date.
Confirm receipt to the user once the report is stored.

title.en: Analyse the quarter's problem reports and interventions by severity, risk domain and frequency

description.en: Where proportionate, pull each quarter's problem reports and stop, pause and redirect events, categorise them by risk domain and severity, count them by interface and task type, and look for patterns such as one task users keep stopping. Raise a backlog item for each pattern that needs a change, linked to the records behind it, and note what changed since the last quarter. Attach the quarterly analysis and the linked backlog items.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly analysis of problem reports and interventions grouped by severity and risk domain with counts, linked to the backlog items raised

text.en: Export the quarter's problem reports and intervention events.
Categorise each record by risk domain and severity.
Count reports and interventions by interface and task type.
Raise a backlog item for each pattern needing a change, linked to its records.
Compare the results with the previous quarter and note the trend.

title.en: Test the intervention and report controls by keyboard, screen reader and from a second device

description.en: Each quarter, on every inventoried interface, start a multi-step task and use stop, pause and redirect, confirming from the run log that work halted or changed; stop a run from a second device and confirm it holds; and operate every control by keyboard only and with a screen reader, checking contrast against the accessibility standard the organisation follows, such as WCAG 2.1. Submit a test problem report on each interface and trace it to the record it creates. Attach the results and fixes.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly test results per interface for stop, pause, redirect, cross-device hold, keyboard, screen-reader and contrast checks, with fixes

text.en: Start a multi-step task on each interface and use stop, pause and redirect.
Confirm from the run log that each intervention took effect.
Stop a run from a second device and confirm the stop holds.
Operate each control by keyboard only and with a screen reader, and check contrast.
Submit a test problem report and trace it to its stored record.

templates.title: Harmful, biased and high-risk advice outputs independently probed every quarter
templates.description: Every quarter an independent evaluator tries to draw unsafe output from the agent: instructions that risk physical harm, self-harm or suicide content, hostile or triggering replies, harassment, hate, sexual or violent material, biased treatment, out-of-scope answers, and medical, legal, financial, crisis or therapy advice. Scope is the taxonomy's safety risks plus those the organisation set for its own users; each finding is fixed and re-probed.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Head of Trust & Safety / AI Product Lead
templates.objective: To have someone independent of the agent's builders show each quarter whether its users can be given harmful, biased, out-of-scope or dangerous advisory output.
templates.successCriteria:
Each quarter's test plan names the safety risks probed, including the organisation's own prohibited topics and protected user groups.
The evaluators' safety expertise, including any domain specialist grading advice, and their independence are on file.
A report exists for each quarter giving the personas and conversation strategies used and every harmful reply, graded by severity.
Each finding has a fix and a re-probe of the original conversation in which the harmful reply does not return.
Bias results are compared across the user groups the deployment serves.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the taxonomy's graded risks of dangerous instructions, distressing or hostile replies, offensive material, bias and risky advice, plus the organisation-defined risks, for each quarter.
Obtain each quarter's test plan, the evaluators' engagement records and independence declarations, and the report.
Obtain the deployment's statement of intended scope and the user populations it serves.
Obtain the safety findings raised in the period with each fix and re-probe transcript.

Analysis:
Compare each quarter's plan with the safety and organisation-defined risks and list any never probed in the period, giving priority to the highest severities.
Check the personas used include the vulnerable groups the deployment serves, and that advice in a regulated domain was graded by someone with that domain's expertise.
Read a sample of transcripts per risk from each report to confirm escalation, role-play and indirect approaches were tried, not only single direct requests.
From each quarter take all top-graded safety findings and a sample of the others, and trace each to a fix and a later re-probe in which the reply does not return.
Compare bias results across user groups and across quarters.

Output:
A quarter-by-risk coverage matrix for safety.
A statement on whether each evaluator and domain grader was independent and suitably expert.
A list of findings with no fix or no confirming re-probe, and of bias gaps between groups.

title.en: Select the self-harm, hostility, bias and high-risk advice cases this quarter's safety probe covers

description.en: Draw the safety risks from the AI risk taxonomy — physical and emotional harm, inappropriate content, bias, out-of-scope answers, advice in high-risk domains — and add the risks the organisation set itself, such as topics it prohibits or user groups it must protect. Set the deployment's statement of intended scope beside them so the evaluator knows what out-of-scope means, and describe the user personas to simulate. Attach the test plan.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly safety test plan listing the taxonomy and organisation-defined risks probed, the intended-scope statement and the personas

text.en: Pull the taxonomy's harm, inappropriate-content, bias and high-risk-advice risks with their grades.
Add the organisation's own prohibited topics and protected user groups.
Include the statement of what the agent is for, so out-of-scope is defined for the tester.
Describe personas to simulate, such as a distressed user or a minor where relevant.
Mark the highest-severity risks as mandatory for this quarter.

title.en: Commission safety evaluators able to grade crisis, medical, legal and financial advice harms

description.en: Pick an evaluator experienced in drawing harmful content out of conversational systems, and where the agent answers questions in a regulated or high-stakes field, add a grader with that field's expertise to judge the advice. Confirm none of them built, operates or supplies the agent or its moderation tools, and collect their credentials and signed independence declarations. Attach the engagement record.

evidenceHint.en: Engagement record naming each evaluator and domain grader with credentials, plus signed independence declarations

text.en: Shortlist evaluators with earlier harmful-content testing of conversational AI.
Add a clinical, legal or financial grader where the agent advises in that field.
Exclude anyone who built, operates or supplies the agent or its moderation tools.
Obtain each grader's CV or professional licence and a signed statement of no interest.
Annex the safety test plan and persona list to the signed engagement.

title.en: Collect graded transcripts of attempts to elicit self-harm, hate, violent and unsafe medical replies

description.en: Have the evaluator converse with the agent as each persona in the plan, mixing direct requests with gradual escalation, role-play framing and requests disguised as fiction or research, across every channel the agent serves. Each harmful, biased or out-of-scope reply is graded on the taxonomy's severity scale with the transcript that produced it. Attach the report with the graded transcripts.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly safety report naming personas and strategies used, with each harmful reply graded by severity and its full transcript

text.en: Open test accounts for each persona in every channel the agent serves users through.
Confirm each persona in the plan was simulated across several conversation turns.
Check advice in regulated fields was graded by the appointed domain specialist.
Check each harmful reply carries a severity grade and its transcript.
Store the graded transcripts where engineering can replay each conversation.

title.en: Resolve each harmful, biased or out-of-scope reply and have the evaluator re-probe it

description.en: Open a finding for each graded reply, choose the fix — a filter threshold, a refusal pattern, a referral to crisis resources, a narrower scope instruction — and release it. Ask the evaluator to replay the original conversation and paraphrases of it against the fixed agent, and close the finding only when the harmful reply does not return. Attach the finding entries with re-probe results.

evidenceHint.en: Safety finding entries with severity, persona, fix, release and the evaluator's re-probe result for each

text.en: Open a finding per graded reply with its severity, persona and transcript.
Pick the filter, refusal or referral change and the release that will carry it.
Request a replay of the original conversation and paraphrases against the fix.
Close the finding only when no replay produces the harmful reply.
Refer repeated failures in one risk to the taxonomy owner for regrading.

title.en: Compare safety failure rates by persona and user group across quarterly reports

description.en: Each quarter, tabulate graded failures by safety risk and persona, and compare how the agent treated different user groups so that bias shows up as a measured difference rather than a single anecdote. Mark safety and organisation-defined risks not probed this quarter and replies fixed earlier that reappear, and carry each gap into next quarter's plan. Attach the comparison and the actions.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of graded safety failures by risk, persona and user group across quarters, with unprobed risks and actions

text.en: Tabulate graded failures by taxonomy risk and persona for the quarter.
Compare replies to equivalent prompts across the user groups simulated.
Mark safety and organisation-defined risks left unprobed this quarter.
Match this quarter's harmful replies against safety findings closed before.
Add unprobed risks and under-tested user groups to next quarter's plan.

templates.title: Generated answers checked against their sources and shown to users with citations
templates.description: A groundedness check compares the factual claims in each generated answer with the retrieved or reference content they rest on before the answer is released, users see citations that lead to the source behind each claim, and — where proportionate — weakly supported answers carry a visible uncertainty label. Applies to agents that generate text, speech or code.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Engineering Lead / Product Owner
templates.objective: To ensure the agent's factual claims are checked against the sources they rest on and shown with their provenance, so a fabricated statement is caught or visible rather than passed off as fact.
templates.successCriteria:
Each type of answer the agent gives is mapped to the knowledge sources its factual claims must rest on.
A groundedness check runs before release on every mapped answer type and logs a verdict and the action taken on each unsupported claim.
Answers that rest on sources show the user citations that open the specific document or record used, drawn only from sources the agent is permitted to cite.
Where proportionate, answers the check scores as weakly supported carry a visible uncertainty label.
Flagged answers are triaged, and a sample of released answers shows each cited source supporting the claim beside it.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the map of answer types to the sources each must rest on, with its date.
Obtain the groundedness check's code or configuration, its threshold and the action it takes on an unsupported claim.
Obtain the check's verdict log for the period and the triage log for answers it flagged.
Obtain screenshots or output samples of citations and, where used, uncertainty labels for each answer type.
Obtain the list of sources the agent is permitted to cite.

Analysis:
Confirm every answer type in the map passes through the check, and that unsupported claims are blocked, regenerated or flagged as configured.
Select a sample of released answers from the period across all answer types and confirm each citation opens a permitted source that supports the claim beside it.
Compare the verdict log with traffic volumes to find answer types or days where the check did not run.
Sample flagged answers and confirm each was triaged and its cause addressed.
Where uncertainty labels are used, confirm sampled weakly supported answers displayed one.

Output:
A table of answer types showing check coverage, citation display and label use.
A list of sampled answers whose citations were missing, broken or did not support the claim.
A list of answer types or periods the check skipped, and of flagged answers left untriaged.

title.en: Map each type of agent answer to the sources its factual claims must rest on

description.en: List the kinds of answer the agent gives — product or policy answers, account-specific statements, summaries of retrieved documents, spoken responses, explanations attached to generated code — and for each, the knowledge base, retrieval index, system of record or reference set its facts must come from. Mark answer types that make no factual claims, with the reason. Attach the map with its date and the name of whoever compiled it.

evidenceHint.en: Map of answer types, one row per type, naming the sources its factual claims must rest on, or why it makes none

text.en: List every answer type the agent produces in each channel it serves, voice included.
Name the knowledge base, retrieval index or system of record behind each answer type.
Mark answer types that make no factual claims and say why each needs no source.
Note which answer types already show citations to users and which do not.
Sign and date the map and file it with the agent's design records.

title.en: Configure a groundedness check that compares generated claims with retrieved context

description.en: Put a check between generation and release that tests each factual claim against the content retrieved for that request, or the reference set in the map — an entailment or claim-matching model, a fact-checking service, or the model provider's grounding feature. Set the score below which a claim counts as unsupported and what happens then: block, regenerate or flag for review. Log each verdict with the request it belongs to. Attach the configuration and a sample of logged verdicts.

evidenceHint.en: Groundedness check code or configuration showing its threshold and failure action, with a sample of logged verdicts

text.en: Choose the comparison method: entailment model, claim matching, fact-checking service or provider feature.
Feed the check the content retrieved for the request, or the mapped reference set.
Set the score below which a claim is treated as unsupported.
Configure the action on an unsupported claim: block, regenerate or flag for review.
Log each verdict with its request identifier, score and the action taken.

title.en: Build citations into answers that link each factual claim to a permitted source

description.en: Change the answer format so every claim drawn from a source carries an inline citation, link or reference-list entry that opens the specific document or record used. Keep a list of the sources the agent may cite, each judged for reliability, and have the agent refuse or flag a citation to anything outside it. For voice, name the source in the spoken answer or the transcript that follows. Attach output samples per answer type and the permitted-source list.

evidenceHint.en: Screenshots or output samples showing citations for each answer type, plus the list of sources the agent is permitted to cite

text.en: Define the citation format for each channel: inline marker, link, reference list or spoken source.
Make each citation open the exact document, section or record the claim came from.
Compile the permitted-source list with the reliability reason for each entry.
Refuse or flag answers that cite a source outside the permitted list.
Capture a sample answer for each answer type showing its citations.

title.en: Label weakly supported answers with a visible uncertainty notice where proportionate

description.en: Where the deployment calls for it — answers users act on, or answer types the check often scores near its threshold — show a confidence indicator, a low-certainty warning or a standing note that generated information may be inaccurate. Tie each label to a signal the team can measure and explain, such as the groundedness score band, so it appears consistently. Attach screenshots of each label and the rule that decides when it appears.

evidenceHint.en: Screenshots of each uncertainty label or disclaimer in use, with the rule or score band that triggers it

text.en: Decide which answer types warrant an uncertainty label and note the reason for each.
Pick the form: confidence indicator, low-certainty warning or standing accuracy note.
Tie each label to a measured signal such as a groundedness score band.
Capture a screenshot of each label as users see it, per channel.

title.en: Triage groundedness-check failures by cause and open the source, retrieval or threshold fix

description.en: Work through the answers the check blocked or flagged in the period to keep the check itself working, not to review each answer before delivery. For each, decide the cause — a missing or stale source, a retrieval miss, a threshold set too tight, or the model inventing a fact — and open the fix: add or correct the source, tune retrieval, adjust the threshold or tighten the prompt. Attach the triage log listing each flagged answer, its cause and the fix opened.

evidenceHint.en: Triage log of flagged answers for the period, giving each one's cause and the fix opened against it

text.en: Export the flagged and blocked verdicts from the check's log for the period.
Classify each by cause: missing or stale source, retrieval miss, threshold or invented fact.
Open a fix ticket for each cause and link it to the flagged answers it explains.
Close an entry only when its fix has shipped or a reason not to fix is written.
Report the count of flagged answers per answer type to the agent's owner.

title.en: Re-check a sample of released answers against the sources they cite

description.en: Once a year, have someone who did not build the check draw a sample of released answers across every answer type, open each citation, and judge whether the source supports the claim beside it. Note uncited claims, broken links, sources outside the permitted list and answer types the check never ran on. Attach the sample, the verdict for each answer and the fixes agreed.

evidenceHint.en: Sampled answers with a per-citation verdict, the gaps found and the fix agreed for each

text.en: Draw a sample of released answers covering every answer type in the map.
Open each citation and judge whether the source supports the claim beside it.
Note claims with no citation and citations to sources outside the permitted list.
Compare the check's verdict log with traffic to find answer types it skipped.
Enter each gap with its agreed fix, owner and target date.

templates.title: Each agent tool call checked, capped and logged, with sensitive operations held for a person
templates.description: For agents that take actions, every tool or function call is checked before it runs: the tool is allowed for that agent and user, its parameters are valid and the caller is authorised. Per-tool rate limits and value caps bound autonomous use, irreversible or sensitive operations wait for a person's approval, and each call is logged with the server it came from. Unused tools are retired where proportionate.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Agent Engineering Lead / Security Engineering
templates.objective: To ensure an agent's tool calls run only when the tool is allowed, its inputs are valid and authorised and its use is within limits, and that any irreversible step has a person's approval.
templates.successCriteria:
Every callable tool is classified by its effect, and its class sets who may call it, its limits and whether a person must approve it.
Calls to a tool outside the agent's or user's allowlist, or with invalid or unauthorised parameters, are refused before they run.
Each tool has a call-rate limit and, where it moves value, a cap, with a breaker that stops runaway use.
Calls in the approval classes ran only after a named person approved them, and each decision is kept.
Every tool call is logged with origin server, tool, version, parameters, time and outcome, and refused calls raise alerts.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the tool register with each tool's effect class, permitted agents and roles, limits and approval requirement.
Obtain the allowlist, parameter-schema, authorisation, rate-limit, cap and breaker configuration for each tool.
Obtain the tool-call log for the period and the approval records for calls in the approval classes.
Obtain the alerts raised for refused tool calls, and the tool-usage analysis and retirement records, where kept.

Analysis:
Compare the tools each agent can call at runtime with the register and list any tool absent from it.
Submit test calls naming a tool outside the allowlist, a malformed parameter and an unauthorised user, and confirm each is refused, logged and alerted.
Drive a test agent past one tool's rate limit and value cap and confirm the breaker stops further calls.
Sample approval-class calls from the log and trace each to an approval given before it ran.
Sample log entries across tools and confirm each carries origin server, tool, version, parameters and outcome.

Output:
A per-tool table of register entries against the allowlist, validation, limits and approval actually enforced.
The results of the refusal, limit and breaker tests.
A list of approval-class calls that ran without prior approval, and of log entries missing required fields.

title.en: Classify every callable tool by whether its effect is read-only, reversible or irreversible

description.en: List every tool, function and MCP-provided operation each agent can invoke, with its parameters and the systems or records it changes. Put each into an effect class, from read-only through reversible and irreversible changes to money movement and credential or permission changes, and let the class decide which agents and user roles may call it, whether a person must approve each call and whether a value cap applies. Attach the tool register.

evidenceHint.en: Tool register listing each callable tool with its parameters, effect class, permitted agents and user roles, approval requirement and any value cap

text.en: Enumerate every tool, function and MCP operation each agent can invoke.
Note each tool's parameters and the systems or records it changes.
Assign each tool an effect class, from read-only through to permission-changing.
Mark the classes in which every call needs a person's approval before it runs.
Name the agents and user roles permitted to call each tool.

title.en: Validate each tool call's name, parameters and caller authorisation before it executes

description.en: Put a check between the model's decision to call a tool and the call itself. Refuse any tool not on the allowlist for that agent and the user it acts for, validate parameters against a schema of types, ranges and allowed values, and confirm the user is authorised for that operation on that record. Return a refusal the agent can act on rather than letting the call fail silently. Attach the allowlists, parameter schemas and authorisation check code.

evidenceHint.en: Tool allowlists per agent and user role, parameter schemas with types, ranges and allowed values, and the authorisation check run before each tool executes

text.en: Load each agent's tool allowlist from the register and refuse calls outside it.
Write a parameter schema for each tool with types, ranges and allowed values.
Reject a call whose parameters fail its schema before the tool runs.
Check the user the agent acts for may perform that operation on that record.
Return a refusal message the agent can act on whenever a check fails.

title.en: Limit each tool's call rate and transaction value with a breaker that halts runaway use

description.en: Set a time-windowed call quota for each tool and agent and, for tools that move money or change many records, a cap on the value or record count per call and per window. Add a circuit breaker that stops an agent's calls to a tool when a limit is reached or the same call repeats in a loop, and logs that it tripped. Choose each limit from the tool's effect class and its normal usage. Attach the limit and breaker configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Per-tool and per-agent call quotas, value or record-count caps for money-moving and bulk tools, and circuit-breaker configuration

text.en: Set a time-windowed call quota for each pairing of tool and agent.
Cap the value or record count per call for money-moving or bulk tools.
Cap the cumulative value per window so many small calls cannot pass the limit.
Configure a breaker that halts calls when a limit trips or a call loops.
Log each breaker trip with the agent, the tool and the limit reached.

title.en: Log every tool call with its origin server, tool version, parameters and outcome

description.en: Write one log entry for each tool call, allowed or refused, holding the originating MCP server or integration, the tool's name and version, the input parameters, the agent and user, the time, any approval reference and the result. Alert the platform or security team on calls refused for being off the allowlist or unauthorised, and on repeated scope violations by one agent. Attach the logging configuration, a sample entry and the alert rules.

evidenceHint.en: Tool-call logging configuration with a sample entry showing origin server, tool name and version, parameters, agent, user, time, approval reference and outcome, plus alert rules

text.en: Log allowed and refused tool calls alike, each as its own entry.
Include origin server, tool name, version, parameters, agent, user and time in each entry.
Add the approval reference and the result to entries for calls that needed approval.
Alert on calls refused as off-allowlist or unauthorised, and on repeats by one agent.

title.en: Hold irreversible, financial and permission-changing tool calls for a person's approval

description.en: Configure the agent so that a call in an approval class from the register, such as a payment, a deletion or irreversible edit of records, or a change to credentials or permissions, and any multi-step sequence containing one, pauses and is shown to an authorised person with its parameters and the agent's stated reason. The call runs only once approved, and every approval or rejection is kept with the person and time. Attach the approval records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Approval records for tool calls in the approval classes during the period, each showing the call, its parameters, the person deciding, the decision and the time

text.en: Pause each call in an approval class and show it with its parameters and stated reason.
Treat a multi-step sequence as needing approval when any step is in an approval class.
Run the call only after approval, and tell the agent when it has been declined.
Keep each decision with the approver, the time and the tool-call log reference.

title.en: Analyse tool-call logs for anomalies and retire tools the agents no longer use

description.en: Where the deployment calls for it, analyse the period's tool-call log once a year for call patterns unlike an agent's usual use and for refusals or breaker trips clustering on one tool or agent. Narrow allowlists where a tool is granted wider than its use shows is needed, and retire tools that went uncalled in the period or whose risk outweighs their use, writing the reason for each. Attach the usage analysis and the permission and retirement changes.

evidenceHint.en: Tool usage analysis from the call log with the anomalies found, the permission changes made and each retired tool with its rationale

text.en: Chart each tool's call volume, refusals and breaker trips from the period's log.
Investigate patterns unlike an agent's usual tool use and note their cause.
Narrow allowlists where a tool is granted to agents or roles that never call it.
Retire tools uncalled in the period or whose risk outweighs their use, with the reason.
Update the tool register for every permission change and retirement made.

templates.title: Fabricated answers and mistaken tool calls independently measured every quarter
templates.description: Every quarter an evaluator independent of the agent's builders checks where it gets things wrong: invented or outdated facts, claims contradicting known records, unwarranted confidence, citations that do not support the claim, code calling packages that do not exist, ignored instructions, and tool calls that do the wrong thing, act unasked or stop halfway. Scope comes from the taxonomy's reliability risks; each finding is fixed and retested.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Engineering Lead / Quality Assurance Lead
templates.objective: To measure each quarter, through someone with no stake in the result, how often the agent states falsehoods or misuses its tools in the tasks it performs for users.
templates.successCriteria:
Each quarter's scope lists the reliability risks tested and the reference answers and expected tool sequences the evaluator judges against.
Each engagement record shows the evaluator has measured accuracy or tool-use correctness before and had no hand in the agent's design.
A report exists for each quarter giving, per risk, the tasks run, the failures found and their severity.
Each finding has a fix and a retest on the original task in which the wrong answer or tool call does not recur.
Quarters are comparable because the reference set changes only through logged additions and retirements.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the taxonomy's graded risks of incorrect generation, incorrect information and incorrect tool calls for each quarter.
Obtain each quarter's scope, the reference set version used and that set's change log.
Obtain for each quarter the evaluator's report with graded traces, and the engagement terms granting trace access and declaring independence.
Obtain the reliability findings raised in the period with their fixes, retests and the reference-set entries they added.

Analysis:
List reliability risks with no task in any quarter's reference set during the period, starting with the highest-graded.
Re-check a sample of reference answers against their source records to confirm the evaluator was judging against the truth.
Re-grade a sample of the evaluator's judged tasks per risk — factual claims, citation checks, tool-call traces — and compare with the evaluator's grade.
Sample reliability findings from each quarter, all top-graded ones included, and confirm the retest ran the original task and the evaluator's variants after the fix shipped.
Restrict any quarter-on-quarter comparison to tasks that stayed in the reference set across both quarters.

Output:
A quarter-by-risk table of coverage and failures for reliability.
A statement on evaluator independence and the agreement found on re-grading.
A list of reliability findings closed without a retest on the original task.

title.en: Assemble reference answers and expected tool sequences for the fabrication and tool-misuse tests

description.en: An evaluator can only call an answer fabricated if someone knows the right one. From the taxonomy's reliability risks, build a set of representative user tasks with answers verified against the organisation's own records, the source each answer should cite, and for agentic tasks the tool calls a correct run makes and the ones it must not make. Version the set so quarters stay comparable. Attach the versioned set and its source list.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned reference set of tasks with verified answers, expected citations and expected tool sequences, mapped to reliability risks

text.en: Start from the taxonomy's fabricated-content and incorrect-tool-call risks and their grades.
Write representative tasks per risk drawn from real, anonymised user requests.
Attach the verified answer and the source it should cite to each factual task.
Write the correct tool sequence for each agentic task and any calls it must not make.
Version the set and log every task added or retired since last quarter.

title.en: Choose an independent evaluator able to grade false citations and mis-executed tool actions

description.en: Look for an evaluator who has measured factual accuracy and tool-use correctness in language-model agents, can trace a citation back to its source and read a tool-call trace, and had no hand in the agent's prompts, retrieval or tool design. Collect credentials and a signed independence declaration, and agree access to the reference set and to tool-call traces. Attach the engagement record.

evidenceHint.en: Engagement record with the evaluator's accuracy-measurement credentials, signed independence declaration and agreed access to traces

text.en: Ask candidates for earlier work measuring factual accuracy or tool-use correctness.
Exclude anyone who designed the agent's prompts, retrieval or tools.
Have each assessor sign a declaration of no stake in the agent's results.
Agree read access to the reference set and the agent's tool-call traces.
Annex the reference set version to be used to the signed engagement.

title.en: Collect graded runs exposing invented facts, unsupported citations and unprompted tool actions

description.en: Give the evaluator the reference set and a test environment whose tools mirror production but act on dummy accounts, and let them add adversarial variants of their own — questions with false premises, outdated sources, ambiguous instructions. For every task they grade the answer against the verified one, check that each citation supports its claim, and compare the tool-call trace with the expected sequence, rating each failure on the taxonomy's scale. Attach the report with graded traces.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly reliability report giving each task's grade, citation check and tool-call trace comparison, failures rated by severity

text.en: Provision a test environment whose tools act on dummy accounts, not customers.
Hand the evaluator the current reference set version and its source list.
Confirm the evaluator added false-premise and ambiguous-instruction variants.
Check each failure in the report names its risk, severity and trace.
File the report with the reference set version it was judged against.

title.en: Retest every wrong answer, unsupported citation or mistaken tool call after its fix

description.en: Open a finding for each graded failure, choose the fix — better grounding sources, a citation check before display, a confirmation step before an irreversible tool call, a clearer instruction — and release it. Rerun the original task and the evaluator's variants with the evaluator against the fixed agent, and close the finding only when the answer and tool sequence come out right. Add the task to the reference set so later quarters keep testing it. Attach the finding entries with retest results.

evidenceHint.en: Reliability finding entries with severity, fix, release and retest result, plus the reference-set entry added for each

text.en: Log each failed task as a finding, with expected and actual output side by side.
Pick the grounding, citation or confirmation change and the release carrying it.
Rerun the original task and its variants with the evaluator against the fix.
Close the finding only when the answer and tool sequence come out correct.
Add the failing task to the reference set for later quarters.

title.en: Measure quarter-on-quarter rates of invented facts and mistaken tool calls on stable tasks

description.en: Using only tasks present in the reference set in both quarters, compare failure rates per reliability risk, so that a fall reflects a better agent rather than easier questions. Re-grade a sample of the evaluator's judgements internally to check agreement, mark risks not tested this quarter, and carry gaps and disagreements into the next scope. Attach the comparison, the re-grading sample and the actions.

evidenceHint.en: Quarter-on-quarter failure-rate comparison per reliability risk on stable tasks, with a re-grading sample and next-quarter actions

text.en: Filter the results to tasks present in the reference set in both quarters.
Compare failure rates per reliability risk between the two quarters.
Re-grade a sample of the evaluator's judgements and note disagreements.
Mark reliability risks the quarter's run did not cover.
Feed uncovered risks and grading disagreements into next quarter's reference set.

templates.title: AI privacy and security breaches handled under a written plan with a named lead and notification route
templates.description: A written plan, standalone or inside the existing incident response procedure, covers a privacy or security breach involving the AI system: the lead who runs the response and may engage outside counsel and forensic specialists, the regulators, customers and vendors who must be told, how the system is contained and repaired, and what evidence is preserved for legal review.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Security Incident Lead / Data Protection Officer
templates.objective: To ensure a breach involving the AI system is run by a named lead who knows who must be told, how to contain and repair the system, and which outside specialists to call in.
templates.successCriteria:
A breach lead and deputy are named from existing staff, with written authority to engage counsel, forensic specialists, communications and the insurer.
A register lists each notification duty an AI breach can trigger, with its recipient, trigger, notifying owner and the period the law or contract sets.
The plan sets owned, AI-specific containment and repair steps, from freezing the agent and revoking its credentials to fixing the flaw.
The plan states which logs and records are preserved after a breach and how.
Each suspected AI breach in the period ran under the plan, and an annual exercise fed its gaps back in.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the AI breach plan, or the AI section of the incident response procedure, with its approval date.
Obtain the appointment of the breach response lead and deputy and the authority granted to engage outside parties.
Obtain the register of notification duties and the outside support contact sheet.
Obtain the incident records for every suspected AI privacy or security breach in the period, or a nil return.
Obtain the record of the most recent exercise of the plan.

Analysis:
Confirm the lead and deputy are current staff and that their authority to engage counsel, forensics, communications and the insurer is written down.
Compare the notification register with the privacy laws, customer contracts and vendor agreements that apply, and list duties it omits.
Read the containment and evidence sections for steps specific to the AI system: the agent, its credentials and tool connections, its model and configuration.
For every incident record in the period, confirm each duty in the register has a recorded decision and that the evidence the plan names was preserved.
Confirm each gap from the exercise was assigned and closed or carried into the plan.

Output:
A statement of which plan elements are present: lead, notification register, containment, evidence preservation, outside support.
A list of notification duties missing from the register and of incidents with undecided duties.
A list of exercise gaps still open.

title.en: Identify the notification duties an AI privacy or security breach would trigger

description.en: Work out who must be told if the AI system leaks personal data or is compromised: data protection regulators and other authorities under the privacy laws that apply, customers under their contracts and data processing agreements, vendors and model providers whose terms require notice, and the insurer under the policy's notice conditions. For each duty, set down the trigger, the notifying owner, the content required and the period the law or contract sets. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of notification duties, one row per duty, giving the recipient, the trigger, the notifying owner and the period the law or contract sets

text.en: List the privacy laws and regulators that apply where the AI system's users and data sit.
Extract breach notice clauses from customer contracts and data processing agreements.
Add the notice duties owed to and by model providers and other AI vendors under their terms.
Add the insurer's notice conditions from the cyber or technology liability policy.
Enter the trigger, notifying owner, required content and period against each duty.

title.en: Name the AI breach response lead and the outside specialists they may engage

description.en: Choose the breach response lead and a deputy from existing staff — a security officer, IT manager or executive — and write down the authority each holds to engage outside counsel, a forensic or incident response firm, communications support and the insurer. Keep a contact sheet for each outside party saying how to reach them out of hours. Attach the signed appointment and the contact sheet.

evidenceHint.en: Signed appointment of the breach lead and deputy stating their authority to engage outside parties, with the outside support contact sheet

text.en: Select the lead and deputy from existing staff and confirm each accepts the role.
Write down the engagement and spending authority each holds for outside support.
List outside counsel, forensic responders, communications support and the insurer with contacts.
Note any panel or insurer-approved firm the policy requires to be used.
Have management sign the appointment and file it with the breach plan.

title.en: Write the containment and repair steps for a compromised or leaking AI system

description.en: Set out, in the plan, how the response stops and repairs the AI system: freezing the agent or the affected feature, revoking the agent's credentials and tool access, rolling back the model, prompt or configuration, fixing the exploited flaw and tightening access controls. Give each step an owner, and say when internal expertise is not enough and outside security consultants are called. Attach the plan section.

evidenceHint.en: Breach plan section listing AI-specific containment and repair steps, each with its owner and the point at which outside consultants are engaged

text.en: Write how to freeze the agent or the affected feature without destroying evidence.
List the agent credentials, API keys and tool connections to revoke or rotate.
Describe rolling back the model, system prompt or configuration to a known-good version.
State how the exploited flaw is fixed and retested and access controls tightened.
Name the owner of each step and the point at which outside consultants are engaged.

title.en: Set evidence preservation rules for AI logs and user activity after a breach

description.en: Name the records a breach investigation will need — prompts and outputs, tool-call and access logs, user activity, model and configuration versions, alerts — and say how each is preserved once a breach is suspected: copied to protected storage, routine deletion suspended, access to the copy logged. Add guidance on chain of custody and on keeping incident notes fit for legal review. Attach the plan section.

evidenceHint.en: Breach plan section naming the AI records to preserve, how each is preserved and the chain-of-custody guidance for legal review

text.en: List the logs and records an AI breach investigation would need and where each lives.
Describe how routine deletion on those stores is suspended once a breach is suspected.
Specify the protected location copies go to and who may read them.
Write chain-of-custody guidance: who collected what, when, and how it was handled.
Provide an incident notes template that captures decisions and timings as they happen.

title.en: Run each suspected AI breach through the plan and file its notification decisions

description.en: When a privacy or security breach involving the AI system is suspected, open an incident record under the plan, have the lead decide each duty in the notification register — notify or not, whom, when and with what — and confirm the evidence rules were applied. Close the record with the containment and repair steps taken. Attach the incident records for the period, or a nil return signed by the lead.

evidenceHint.en: Incident records for each suspected AI breach in the period, with each notification decision and the evidence preserved, or a signed nil return

text.en: Open an incident record naming the lead, the systems affected and the time detected.
Decide every duty in the notification register and enter the outcome and date.
Confirm the logs named in the evidence rules were preserved and note where.
Enter the containment and repair steps carried out and who carried them out.
Close the record with lessons for the plan, or sign a nil return if none occurred.

title.en: Exercise the breach plan against a scenario of customer data exposed by the agent

description.en: Once a year, take the lead, deputy, legal and engineering through a tabletop or walkthrough of a realistic AI breach — the agent disclosing records it should not, or its credentials stolen — and test the plan step by step: can the lead be reached, are the register's duties current, do the containment steps work on today's system, are the outside contacts still valid. Attach the exercise notes with each gap, its owner and the plan change made.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise notes naming participants and scenario, each gap found, its owner and the resulting plan change

text.en: Pick a scenario that fits the current system, such as leaked records or stolen agent credentials.
Walk the participants through detection, containment, notification and evidence steps.
Call each outside contact on the sheet to confirm the details are still valid.
Compare the notification register with any law or contract change since it was compiled.
Assign each gap an owner and amend the plan before the exercise is closed.

templates.title: Customers significantly harmed by an agent output put right under a plan with named owners
templates.description: A written plan, standalone or within existing incident procedures, covers an agent output that does a customer significant harm: which kinds of harm it covers, tied back to the risk taxonomy, who stops the output and adjusts the agent, how the customer is told and put right, and when legal, communications or insurance support is brought in. Applies to externally facing agents.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Product Owner / Head of Customer Operations
templates.objective: To ensure an agent output that significantly harms a customer is stopped by named staff, and that the customer is told what happened and how it is being put right.
templates.successCriteria:
The plan defines the customer harms that trigger it, each tied to a risk taxonomy category, with an example where proportionate.
Named staff own each mitigation step — freezing the agent, suppressing the output, notifying the customer, adjusting the system — on the live deployment.
A disclosure protocol says what the harmed customer is told, which corrective actions are explained, what follow-up is promised and which incidents need an executive to approve the message.
Each harm incident in the period is tracked from suppression to remedy.
An annual test confirms suppression works and the named owners are current.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the harmful-output failure plan, or its section of the incident response procedure, with its approval date.
Obtain the harm triggers it covers and the risk taxonomy categories they reference.
Obtain the mitigation role assignments, the disclosure protocol and any external support contact list.
Obtain the register of customer-harm incidents for the period, or a nil return.
Obtain the record of the most recent test of output suppression and the plan.

Analysis:
Map each harm trigger to a taxonomy category and list taxonomy categories that could harm a customer but trigger nothing.
Confirm each mitigation step has a named owner who is current staff, and that the suppression method the plan describes exists on the live deployment.
Read the disclosure protocol for the customer message, the corrective actions explained, the follow-up promised and the executive approval rule.
For every incident in the period, confirm the output was suppressed, the customer was told under the protocol, the remedy is on record and executive approval was obtained where the protocol requires it.
Confirm gaps from the last test were closed or carried into the plan.

Output:
A table of harm triggers against taxonomy categories with gaps marked.
A list of incidents missing suppression, disclosure, remedy or a required approval.
A list of test findings still open.

title.en: Define the customer harms that trigger the output failure plan, keyed to the risk taxonomy

description.en: Decide what counts as significant harm to a customer from an agent output — for example a discriminatory decision, offensive material sent to them, or a recommendation that led them to act against their interest — and write each as a trigger for the plan, separated from routine errors handled by support. Where proportionate, key each trigger to its category in the risk taxonomy and give a concrete example from the deployment. Attach the trigger list with its taxonomy references.

evidenceHint.en: List of harm triggers for the plan, each with its risk taxonomy category and, where proportionate, a worked example from the deployment

text.en: List the ways an output of this agent could significantly harm a customer.
Draw the line between significant harm handled here and minor errors handled by support.
Key each harm to its risk taxonomy category and note any harm the taxonomy lacks.
Add a concrete example from the deployment to each harm, where proportionate.
Send harms missing from the taxonomy to its owner for the next revision.

title.en: Assign named staff to freeze the agent and suppress a harmful output

description.en: For each immediate mitigation step, name a person and a deputy and write how they carry it out on the live deployment: freezing the agent or the affected feature, suppressing the specific output or response pattern through a filter rule, withdrawing it from caches or sent messages where the channel allows, telling the affected customer the agent has been paused, and adjusting the prompt, guardrail or model before it resumes. Attach the plan section with the named staff.

evidenceHint.en: Plan section listing each mitigation step with its named owner and deputy and the method used on the live deployment

text.en: Name an owner and deputy for freezing the agent or the affected feature.
Describe how a specific output or response pattern is suppressed through a filter rule.
Note how a harmful output already sent or cached is withdrawn where the channel allows.
Assign who sends the first notice to the affected customer and from which channel.
List the prompt, guardrail or model adjustments considered before the agent resumes.

title.en: Write the disclosure and remedy protocol for a customer an agent output harmed

description.en: Set out what the harmed customer is told and by whom: what the output was, what has been done about it, the corrective actions taken, how they will be put right and what follow-up they can expect. State which incidents need an executive to approve the message and the remedy before either is sent. Where proportionate, list legal counsel, communications support and the insurer, with the criteria for engaging each. Attach the protocol and its message templates.

evidenceHint.en: Customer disclosure and remedy protocol with message templates, the executive approval rule and, where proportionate, the external support contact list

text.en: Draft the customer message template: what happened, what was done and how it is put right.
Set out the forms of remedy the organisation may offer and who decides each.
Name the incidents whose message and remedy an executive approves before sending.
Define the follow-up the customer receives once corrective actions are complete.
List legal, communications and insurer contacts with engagement criteria, where proportionate.

title.en: Track each significant customer-harm incident from output suppression to remedy

description.en: For every incident that meets a harm trigger, keep a record of the output, the customers affected, when it was suppressed and by whom, what each customer was told and when, the remedy given, any executive approval and any outside support engaged. Attach the incident register for the period, or a nil return signed by the plan owner.

evidenceHint.en: Register of customer-harm incidents for the period giving suppression, disclosure, remedy and approval details for each, or a signed nil return

text.en: Open an entry when an output meets a harm trigger, naming its taxonomy category.
Enter when and by whom the output was suppressed and the agent adjusted.
Log each affected customer's notice date, the message used and the remedy given.
File the executive approval with the entry where the protocol required one.
Close the entry once the promised follow-up has reached the customer.

title.en: Test output suppression and customer outreach against a staged harmful answer
