description.en: Once a year, stage a harmful answer from the trigger list in a non-production copy of the agent and have the named staff run the plan: suppress the output, freeze and resume the agent, draft the customer message from the template and route it for executive approval. Note any step that failed, any named person who has left, and any trigger the taxonomy has since outgrown. Attach the test record with each gap, its owner and the plan change.

evidenceHint.en: Test record showing the staged output, the result of each plan step, the gaps found and the resulting plan changes

text.en: Choose a trigger from the list and stage a matching output in a non-production copy.
Have the named staff suppress the output, then freeze and resume the agent.
Draft the customer message from the template and route it through the approval rule.
Check every named owner, deputy and outside contact is still in place.
Revise the plan for each failed step and give each revision an owner.

templates.title: Customer losses from an incorrect agent answer traced, corrected and compensated under a plan
templates.description: A written plan, standalone or within existing incident procedures, covers a fabricated or incorrect agent output that costs a customer substantial money: who owns the response, how the wrong output is traced to its source and the agent corrected, how every affected customer and transaction is found, and how losses are put right with legal, financial and insurance support as needed. Applies to externally facing agents.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Product Owner / Finance Lead / Legal Counsel
templates.objective: To ensure an incorrect agent answer that costs customers money is traced to its source, every customer it reached is found, and each loss is corrected and compensated.
templates.successCriteria:
The plan states the loss that brings a case under it and, where proportionate, the hallucination incident types it covers, such as wrong figures or invented terms.
Named staff freeze the faulty answer type and trace the output to its cause before the agent resumes.
A prepared search finds every customer and transaction exposed to the same incorrect output while it was live.
A compensation protocol sets how affected customers are told, how loss is assessed and paid, and which cases need executive approval or outside support.
Each loss case in the period runs from trace to payment on record.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the hallucination failure plan, or its section of the incident response procedure, with its approval date.
Obtain the loss threshold, any incident types, the trace procedure and the affected-customer search.
Obtain the compensation protocol and any external support contact list.
Obtain the register of loss cases for the period, or a nil return.
Obtain the record of the most recent drill of the plan.

Analysis:
Confirm the trace procedure reaches the records needed to find a cause: the conversation, retrieved content, prompt and model version, and tool responses.
Run or inspect the affected-customer search and confirm it is bounded by the period the faulty output was live, not only by the customer who reported it.
For every loss case, confirm the trace result, the full list of affected customers and transactions, the customer notices, the loss assessment and the payment or reversal made.
Confirm executive approval or outside support was obtained in each case where the protocol requires it.
Confirm the drill reached a cause and a customer list and that its gaps were closed.

Output:
A statement of which plan elements are present: threshold, trace, search, compensation, outside support.
A list of loss cases with untraced causes, incomplete customer lists or assessed losses left unpaid.
A list of drill gaps still open.

title.en: Set the loss threshold and hallucination incident types that bring a case under the plan

description.en: Decide what level of customer financial loss counts as substantial for this deployment — a figure, a share of a transaction or a kind of decision — so staff know when a wrong answer becomes a case under this plan. Where proportionate, list the hallucination incident types it covers, such as an invented price or fee, a wrong balance or deadline, fabricated contract terms or an incorrect recommendation, with an example of each. Attach the threshold and the type list.

evidenceHint.en: Stated loss threshold for the plan and, where proportionate, the hallucination incident types with an example of each

text.en: Identify the answers customers act on with money: prices, balances, terms, deadlines, advice.
Choose the loss level or kind of decision that makes a wrong answer a case under this plan.
Check the threshold with finance against the deployment's typical transaction values.
List the hallucination incident types the plan covers, where proportionate.
Give each incident type an example drawn from the deployment's own answers.

title.en: Establish how a costly wrong answer is traced to its source and the agent corrected

description.en: Name the staff who freeze the affected answer type and those who trace it, then write the trace: pull the conversation, the content retrieved, the prompt and model version and any tool or system data the answer used, and decide whether the error came from wrong source content, a retrieval miss, the model inventing it or bad tool data. Set out the corrections that follow — fixing the source, tightening output validation, adjusting the model or prompt — and the extra monitoring on that answer type once it resumes. Attach the procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Trace and correction procedure naming who freezes and who traces, the records pulled, the cause categories and the follow-up monitoring

text.en: Name who freezes the affected answer type and who runs the trace, with deputies.
List the records the trace pulls: conversation, retrieved content, prompt, model version, tool data.
Define the cause categories: wrong source, retrieval miss, invented content or bad tool data.
Pair each cause with its correction: source fix, validation change, prompt or model adjustment.
Specify the extra monitoring placed on the answer type once it resumes.

title.en: Build the search that finds every customer and transaction given the same wrong answer

description.en: One customer's complaint rarely means one customer was affected. Prepare a query over conversation and transaction logs that, given a traced error — a source document, a prompt or model version, an answer pattern — returns every customer who received the incorrect output while it was live and every transaction they made on the strength of it. Test it on a past answer and keep the query with the plan. Attach the query, its parameters and the test run.

evidenceHint.en: Affected-customer query with its parameters and a test run on a past answer listing the customers and transactions it found

text.en: Identify the logs that tie an answer to a customer and to the transaction that followed.
Parameterise the query by source document, prompt or model version and answer pattern.
Bound the search by the period the faulty source, prompt or model was live.
Run the query on a past answer and check its results against a manual review.
Store the query with the plan and name who may run it on customer data.

title.en: Draft the compensation protocol for customers who lost money on an incorrect answer

description.en: Write how each affected customer is told which answer was wrong and what was corrected, how their loss is assessed and paid or the transaction reversed, and what follow-up they receive. State which cases an executive approves before the notice or payment goes. Where proportionate, name legal counsel for significant claims, a financial reviewer for loss assessment and the insurer, with when each is engaged and how cover is activated. Attach the protocol.

evidenceHint.en: Compensation protocol covering customer notice, loss assessment, payment or reversal, executive approval and, where proportionate, legal, financial and insurer contacts

text.en: Draft the notice telling a customer which answer was wrong and what was corrected.
Set the method for assessing each customer's loss from the transaction records.
Describe how compensation is paid or the transaction reversed, and who authorises it.
Name the cases an executive approves before the notice or payment goes out.
List counsel, a financial reviewer and the insurer with engagement criteria, where proportionate.

title.en: Open a loss case for each costly wrong answer and carry it through to compensation

description.en: For every report that meets the loss threshold, open a case under the plan and keep in it the trace result, the affected-customer search run and its output, each customer's notice, loss assessment and payment or reversal, any executive approval and any outside support engaged. Attach the loss case register for the period, or a nil return signed by the plan owner.

evidenceHint.en: Loss case register for the period giving trace result, affected customers, assessments and payments for each case, or a signed nil return

text.en: Open a case when a report meets the loss threshold, naming the incident type.
Attach the trace result and the correction made before the answer type resumed.
File the affected-customer search output with the date it was run.
Enter each customer's notice date, assessed loss and payment or reversal.
Close the case once every affected customer is settled and follow-up sent.

title.en: Re-trace a past incorrect answer to its cause and every customer it reached

description.en: Once a year, take an incorrect answer from the logs — a real past case or one seeded in a test copy — and walk the plan: run the trace to a cause, run the affected-customer search, and draft the notices and loss assessments the protocol calls for. Note where records were missing, the search missed customers or the protocol was unclear. Attach the drill record with each gap, its owner and the plan change.

evidenceHint.en: Drill record showing the answer used, the cause reached, the customers found, the gaps and the resulting plan changes

text.en: Choose a past incorrect answer, or seed one in a test copy of the agent.
Run the trace procedure and enter the cause it reached and the records used.
Run the affected-customer search and compare its list with a manual check.
Draft one notice and one loss assessment from the protocol to test its wording.
Raise a plan change for each gap the drill exposed and name its owner.

templates.title: Approval-requiring AI changes signed off by their accountable lead with evidence on file
templates.description: The organisation lists which changes to an AI system, from development through deployment, need formal review or approval — model choice, material system-prompt edits, guardrails added or removed, end-user workflow changes, changes that move evaluation results materially — names an accountable lead for each, and files every approval with its evidence; where proportionate, AI components are signed and verified in the pipeline.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Head of AI Engineering / Change Approval Owner
templates.objective: To ensure every AI-system change that needs approval has a named accountable lead who signs it off, and that each sign-off is filed with the evidence it rested on.
templates.successCriteria:
A change-type table lists the AI-system changes that need formal review or approval, across development and deployment, and the changes that do not.
Each approval-requiring change type has one accountable lead as approver, with consulted and informed roles where a RACI is used.
Every approval-requiring change in the period has a record naming the change, its type, the approver, the date and the evidence reviewed.
No change reached production without approval by the lead named for its type.
Where proportionate, AI components are signed and the pipeline refuses any unsigned or altered one.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the change-type table and the approver matrix or RACI for each type, with dates.
Obtain the approval records for the period from the change tracker, pull requests or deployment tool.
Obtain the production change history for the period: model and provider versions, system-prompt commits, guardrail configuration and workflow releases.
Where signing is used, obtain the signing configuration, the pipeline verification step and its logs for the period.

Analysis:
Read the change-type table for the change kinds that alter what the agent does — model choice, system prompt, guardrails, end-user workflow, changes that move evaluation results — and note any it leaves unclassified.
Reconcile the production change history with the approval records and list changes with no record.
For a sample of approval records across every change type, confirm the approver is the lead named for that type, the approval preceded the release and the evidence reviewed is attached.
Where signing is used, confirm the verification step ran on every release in the period and inspect a refused unsigned artefact.

Output:
A list of change kinds missing from the table.
A list of production changes released without approval, approved by the wrong lead or approved after release.
A list of sampled records lacking evidence, and of releases where signature verification did not run.

title.en: Classify which AI-system changes need formal approval before they ship

description.en: Draw up a table of the changes made to the AI system across development and deployment and mark which need formal review or approval: choosing or swapping a model or provider, material edits to the system prompt, adding or removing a guardrail, changes to the end-user workflow, and any change that moves evaluation results past a threshold the organisation sets. List the changes that need no approval and why. Attach the table with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Change-type table marking each kind of AI-system change as approval-requiring or not, with the evaluation-movement threshold the organisation set

text.en: List the kinds of change made to models, prompts, guardrails, tools, workflows and data.
Mark each kind as needing formal review, formal approval, or neither.
State the movement in evaluation results the organisation treats as material.
Explain why each kind marked as needing no approval is safe to release without it.
Date the table and file it in the engineering policy repository.

title.en: Assign an accountable approver to each approval-requiring AI change type

description.en: For every approval-requiring type in the table, name one lead accountable for approving it — by role and current holder — and a delegate for absence. Where the organisation uses a RACI, add who is consulted, such as security or legal for a guardrail removal, and who is informed. Attach the approver matrix with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Approver matrix naming the accountable lead and delegate for each change type, with consulted and informed roles where a RACI is used

text.en: Name one accountable lead by role and current holder for each change type.
Name a delegate who may approve while the lead is absent.
Add consulted and informed roles where the organisation uses a RACI.
Have each named lead confirm in writing the change types they approve.
Publish the matrix where engineers raising changes can find it.

title.en: Configure the change tracker to hold each AI approval with its supporting evidence

description.en: Set up the place approvals live — the ticketing system, pull request template or deployment tool — so a record for an approval-requiring change carries its type, the accountable lead's sign-off and date, and links to the evidence the lead reviewed, such as the diff, evaluation results and risk notes. Require the named approver's review before the change can merge or deploy. Attach the template and the setting that enforces the approver.

evidenceHint.en: Change record template with its required fields, and the branch protection or deployment-tool setting that requires the named approver

text.en: Add required fields for change type, approver, approval date and evidence links.
Link each change type to its accountable lead so the right approver is requested.
Turn on required review by the named approver in the repository or deployment tool.
Block approval until the diff and evaluation results are linked to the record.
Export the template and enforcement settings as screenshots or configuration.

title.en: Sign model weights and AI release artefacts and verify each signature in the pipeline

description.en: Where proportionate to the deployment, sign model weights, AI libraries and deployment artefacts when they are built or approved, hold the signing keys in a managed key store, and add a step to the delivery pipeline that verifies each signature and stops any unsigned or altered component reaching production. Attach the signing configuration, the verification step and a log showing an unsigned artefact refused.

evidenceHint.en: Signing configuration, the pipeline step that verifies signatures, and a log entry showing an unsigned or altered artefact refused

text.en: List the models, libraries and artefacts that reach production and where each is built.
Sign each at build or approval with keys held in a managed key store.
Add a pipeline step that verifies every signature before deployment.
Fail the deployment when a component is unsigned or its signature does not match.
Test the block with an unsigned artefact and save the refusal log.

title.en: File the lead's sign-off and its evidence against every approval-requiring AI change

description.en: As each approval-requiring change is raised, have the accountable lead for its type review the evidence and approve or reject it in the tracker before release, and keep the record — change, type, approver, date, decision and evidence links — with the change. Attach the approval log for the period, exported from the tracker.

evidenceHint.en: Approval log for the period, one row per approval-requiring change, giving type, approver, date, decision and evidence links

text.en: Classify each new change against the change-type table when it is raised.
Request approval from the accountable lead named for that type.
Link the diff, evaluation results and risk notes the lead reviewed.
Hold the release until the lead's decision is on the record.
Export the period's approval log from the tracker.

title.en: Reconcile production AI changes in the period against their approval records

description.en: Once a year, take the production change history — model and provider versions, system-prompt commits, guardrail configuration changes, workflow releases — and match each change to its approval record. Flag changes released without approval, approved by someone other than the lead named for the type, approved after release or lacking evidence, and change kinds the table does not classify. Attach the reconciliation with each exception and its resolution.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of production AI changes against approval records, listing each exception and how it was resolved

text.en: Export model, prompt, guardrail and workflow changes released to production in the period.
Match each change to its approval record by change identifier.
Flag changes with no record, the wrong approver, a late approval or missing evidence.
List change kinds found that the change-type table does not classify.
Agree a resolution and owner for each exception and update the table if needed.

templates.title: Each AI data store's hosting, encryption and read access justified by sensitivity and law
templates.description: A written record covers every store of AI system data — embeddings, conversation history, prompts and system instructions, model weights, evaluation sets, logs and backups — stating its hosting model (managed cloud, self-managed or on-premises), how it is encrypted at rest and under whose keys, and who can read it, each choice reasoned against the data's sensitivity, the regulations attached to it and operational need.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Security Engineering Lead / AI Platform Lead
templates.objective: To ensure every store of AI system data is protected in proportion to its sensitivity and regulatory weight, and that each protection choice is written down with its reason.
templates.successCriteria:
Every AI data store is listed with the data classes it holds, a sensitivity tier and the regulations those classes attract.
Each tier states its encryption at rest, key custody and storage-level read permissions, with the reason for each.
Each store has a dated hosting decision weighing cloud, self-managed and on-premises options against sensitivity, regulation and operational need.
Live encryption, key and read settings on sampled stores match their tier, and each deviation is justified or fixed.
The record is revised when a store, data class, hosting choice or applicable rule changes.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the storage security record for AI system data, with its version history for the period.
Obtain the cloud asset inventory or infrastructure-as-code listing of databases, buckets, vector indexes and model artefact stores used by the AI system.
Obtain the encryption, key-management and access-policy settings exported from each sampled store.
Obtain the change tickets and regulatory updates in the period that touched AI data storage.

Analysis:
Compare the asset inventory with the record and list AI data stores the record omits.
Check that each recorded store carries a sensitivity tier, its attached regulations and a hosting decision with reasons.
Select a sample of stores that includes every store in the highest sensitivity tier, and compare live encryption, key custody and read permissions with the tier requirement.
Read each sampled hosting decision for whether sensitivity, regulation and operational need were all weighed.
Match change tickets and regulatory updates to record revisions and note changes never carried into it.

Output:
A list of AI data stores missing from the record or lacking a tier or a hosting decision.
A per-store table of documented against live encryption, key custody and read access for the sample.
A list of storage-relevant changes in the period that the record does not reflect.

title.en: Classify each AI data store by sensitivity and the regulations its contents bring

description.en: List every store the AI system keeps data in at rest — vector indexes and embeddings, conversation history, prompt and system-instruction repositories, model weights and adapters, evaluation and fine-tuning sets, logs, caches and backups. Against each, name the data classes it holds, assign a tier from the organisation's data classification scheme and, with the privacy owner, note the regulations those classes attract. Attach the classified store list with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of AI data stores giving the data classes held, the sensitivity tier and the regulations attached to each

text.en: Pull databases, buckets and vector indexes tagged to the AI system from the cloud asset inventory.
Add model weights, adapters, prompt repositories and evaluation sets held outside those systems.
Name the data classes each store holds, such as personal data or customer content.
Assign each store a tier from the organisation's data classification scheme.
Have the privacy owner note the regulations that attach to each store's data classes.

title.en: Define encryption, key custody and read permissions required for each AI data tier

description.en: For each sensitivity tier, write the storage protections a store at that tier must carry: encryption at rest and its setting, whether keys may be provider-managed or must sit in the organisation's own key service, which roles and service identities may read the data at the storage layer, and how backups, snapshots and replicas inherit the same protection. Give the reason behind each requirement. Attach the storage security standard with its version and date.

evidenceHint.en: Storage security standard giving, per sensitivity tier, encryption at rest, key custody, storage-level read permissions and backup protection, with reasons

text.en: Set the encryption-at-rest requirement for each tier, naming the algorithm or service setting.
Decide per tier whether keys may be provider-managed or must sit in the organisation's key service.
Name the roles and service identities allowed storage-level read access at each tier.
Extend each tier's protections to backups, snapshots and replicas.
Write the reason for each requirement, citing the sensitivity or regulation behind it.

title.en: Write a hosting decision for each AI data store weighing cloud against on-premises

description.en: For each store, or each group of stores at the same tier, set down the hosting option chosen — managed cloud service, self-managed in the organisation's own cloud account, or on-premises — the alternatives considered, and how each was judged against the data's sensitivity, the regulations it carries and operational needs such as latency, scale and recovery. Name who took the decision and when. Attach the decision memos.

evidenceHint.en: Dated hosting decision memo per store or store group, naming the options considered, the choice made, its reasoning and the decision-maker

text.en: Group stores that share a tier and a hosting setup so one memo can cover them.
List the hosting options considered for each group, including on-premises where feasible.
Judge each option against sensitivity, applicable regulation and operational need.
State the choice, the residual risk accepted and who made the decision.
File each memo against the stores it covers in the classified store list.

title.en: Revise the storage security record whenever a store, data class or applicable rule changes

description.en: Treat these as triggers: a new or retired AI data store, a new data class reaching an existing store, a change of hosting, and a new or amended regulation affecting stored data. On each, update the classified store list, the tier standard or the hosting memo it touches, and log the trigger, the change made and the date, so the version history shows why the record moved. Attach the record's change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Change log for the storage security record listing each trigger, the section revised, the change made and the date

text.en: Subscribe the record owner to change tickets that create, move or retire AI data stores.
Ask the privacy owner to flag regulatory changes that affect stored AI data.
Update the store list, tier standard or hosting memo each trigger touches.
Enter the trigger, the revision and its date in the record's change log.

title.en: Inspect sampled AI data stores for encryption and read access that differ from the record

description.en: Once a year, compare the cloud asset inventory with the classified store list to find AI data stores nobody recorded. Then take a sample that includes every store in the highest tier, export each store's live encryption, key and access-policy settings, and compare them with what its tier requires. Attach the comparison with each deviation, whether it is justified or to be fixed, and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Per-store comparison of live encryption, key custody and read permissions against the tier standard, with each deviation, its disposition and owner

text.en: Match the cloud asset inventory against the classified store list for missing stores.
Select a sample of stores that takes in every store in the highest tier.
Export encryption, key and access-policy settings from each sampled store.
Compare each export with the requirements of the store's tier.
Enter each deviation as justified or to be fixed, with owner and target date.

templates.title: Model providers vetted before adoption and on a cycle, with open-weight models verified at intake
templates.description: Before a foundation-model or other upstream AI provider is used, it is assessed against set criteria — data handling and ownership, personal-data controls, security and compliance status — with the scoring, the verification done and the approval decision kept as evidence, and it is assessed again on a cycle. Where an open-weight model is used, its source, integrity and licence are checked before it is deployed.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Vendor Risk Lead / Security Engineering / AI Platform Lead
templates.objective: To ensure no upstream model or model provider reaches the agent without a recorded assessment of its data handling, personal-data controls, security and compliance, and a decision to approve it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every upstream AI provider and model the agent uses is inventoried with its assessment status and approval date.
The criteria cover data handling and ownership, personal-data controls, security, compliance and open-source licensing, and are scored.
Each approval is preceded by a dated assessment showing scores, the verification done and the accountable lead's decision.
Approved providers are reassessed on the organisation's cycle, and no production model lacks a current approval.
Each open-weight model in use has an intake record of source, hash or signature check, known issues, licence and base model.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of upstream model providers and models, with assessment status and approval dates.
Obtain the assessment criteria and scoring method in force in the period.
Obtain the assessment records for every provider approved or reassessed in the period, with the documents relied on.
Obtain the model identifiers and endpoints configured in production, from the gateway or application configuration.
Obtain the intake checklists for open-weight models deployed in the period.

Analysis:
Compare the models configured in production with the inventory and list any without a current approval.
Select a sample of assessments and confirm each applies every criterion, shows the verification done and predates its approval.
Check that each approved provider's latest assessment falls within the reassessment cycle.
For each open-weight model deployed in the period, compare the hash in its intake checklist with the value its publisher posts.
Read each intake checklist's licence conclusion against the use the model is actually put to.

Output:
A list of models or providers in use without a current approval.
A list of sampled assessments missing criteria, verification or a dated approval.
A list of open-weight models whose intake checklist is incomplete or disagrees with the publisher's values.

title.en: Inventory the foundation-model and upstream AI providers the agent depends on

description.en: List every upstream AI component the agent relies on and who supplies it: hosted foundation-model APIs, embedding and reranking models, model-hosting platforms, and open-weight models with any fine-tuned derivatives. For each, give the model and version, how it is reached, what data it receives, its assessment status and its approval date. Attach the inventory with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of upstream model providers and models, naming model and version, data received, assessment status and approval date

text.en: Pull model identifiers and provider endpoints from the gateway and application configuration.
Add embedding, reranking and classifier models alongside the main foundation model.
List open-weight models and each fine-tuned derivative together with its base model.
Note what data each provider or model receives from the agent.
Mark each entry's assessment status and approval date.

title.en: Define the scored criteria upstream model providers must meet before approval

description.en: Write the criteria every provider and model is assessed against — how it handles submitted data and what ownership it claims over it, its controls over personal data, its security measures, its compliance status and certifications, and, for open-source models, licensing and provenance — with a scoring scale and the results that block approval, as the organisation sets them. Note that provider IP indemnity, confidentiality terms and cyber or CBRN capability information are assessed under their own controls. Attach the criteria document with its version.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned criteria for assessing upstream model providers, spanning data handling, personal-data controls, security, compliance and open-source licensing, with a scoring scale

text.en: Write questions on the provider's handling and retention of submitted data and its claims over it.
Add criteria for personal-data controls and the provider's own sub-processing.
Set criteria for security measures and the certifications or reports accepted as proof.
Cover licensing and provenance for open-source and open-weight models.
Fix a scoring scale and state which results stop an approval.

title.en: Conduct pre-adoption due diligence on each model provider and decide its approval

description.en: Before a new provider or model is used, send the questionnaire built from the criteria, review the certifications and audit reports it supplies, contact references where the criteria call for them, and score the results. Put the scored assessment, with every document relied on, to the accountable lead, and file the approval or rejection with its date before any production use. Repeat the assessment for each approved provider on the organisation's cycle. Attach the completed assessment and decision.

evidenceHint.en: Completed provider assessment with questionnaire answers, certifications reviewed, references contacted, scores and the dated approval decision with its accountable lead

text.en: Send the provider the questionnaire drawn from the current criteria.
Review the certifications and audit reports it returns, noting their scope and dates.
Contact references where the criteria call for it and note what they said.
Score each criterion and summarise the residual risks for the accountable lead.
File the decision, its date and the evidence relied on before production use starts.

title.en: Verify the publisher, checksum and licence of each open-weight model at intake

description.en: Where the agent uses an open-weight model, check it before deployment: take the weights only from the publisher's repository or a registry the organisation has vetted, compare the file hashes or signature with the values the publisher posts, look up problems reported against that exact version, read the licence against the intended use, and for a fine-tuned model name the base model and check it the same way. Attach the completed intake checklist.

evidenceHint.en: Intake checklist per open-weight model naming publisher, source repository, version, hash or signature result, known-issue review, licence decision and base model

text.en: Name the publisher, repository or registry and exact version the weights came from.
Compare downloaded file hashes or the signature with the publisher's posted values.
Search issue trackers and advisories for problems reported against that version.
Check the licence terms allow the agent's intended use, commercial use included.
Identify the base model of any fine-tuned derivative and run the same checks on it.

title.en: Check approved providers for lapsed reassessments and production models lacking approval

description.en: Once a year, list approved providers whose latest assessment falls outside the organisation's reassessment cycle and schedule them; compare model identifiers in the gateway and application configuration with the inventory to find models running without approval; and sample assessments for missing criteria, absent verification or an approval dated after first use. Attach the review with each finding, its fix and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Annual review listing overdue reassessments, models in production without approval and sampled assessment gaps, each with fix and owner

text.en: List approved providers whose latest assessment is older than the reassessment cycle.
Compare configured production model identifiers with the approved inventory.
Sample assessments for missing criteria, absent verification or late approval dates.
Confirm each open-weight model in use has a complete intake checklist.
Enter each finding with its fix, owner and target date.

templates.title: Key AI decision processes reviewed each quarter, with decisions, approvals and fixes on record
templates.description: The processes the organisation uses to make decisions about its AI system — approving system changes, selecting foundation models, assessing security, and any others it relies on — are reviewed each quarter against the decision records they produced. Reviews, conclusions and approvals sit in one repository, every risk raised is tracked to remediation, and outside feedback is weighed where proportionate.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Head of AI / Risk and Compliance Lead
templates.objective: To confirm on a fixed quarterly calendar that the processes behind decisions about the AI system work as intended, and that every weakness a review finds is approved for action and fixed.
templates.successCriteria:
A dated list names each key AI decision process, its owner, its review lead and the quarters in which it is reviewed.
Every scheduled review took place, and its minutes record the decision records examined, the conclusions and who approved them.
Decision records and minutes sit in one repository, each record showing the evidence weighed and its approval.
Each risk a review raised has an owner, a remediation plan and a status, and closed items carry evidence of the fix.
Where proportionate, outside advisories, customer reports and researcher findings received were weighed in a review.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of key AI decision processes and the review calendar for the period.
Obtain the minutes of every process review held in the period, with their approvals.
Obtain an export of the decision-record repository for the period.
Obtain the remediation register for risks raised by the reviews.
Where external feedback is collected, obtain the intake log of advisories, customer reports and researcher findings.

Analysis:
Compare the calendar with the minutes and list every scheduled review that did not take place or was not approved.
For a sample of reviews, confirm the minutes name the decision records examined and that those records exist in the repository.
For a sample of decision records, check each shows the evidence weighed, the decision-maker and the approval its process requires.
Trace every risk raised in the sampled reviews to the remediation register, and check closed items for evidence of the fix.
Trace a sample of external feedback items to the review that weighed them and the outcome entered.

Output:
A process-by-quarter grid showing reviews held, missed or left unapproved.
A list of decision records missing their evidence or approval.
A list of review risks with no remediation entry or closed without evidence, and of outside feedback never weighed.

title.en: List the key AI decision processes and schedule a quarterly review of each

description.en: Name the processes through which decisions about the AI system are taken — at least approval of AI system changes, selection of foundation models and security assessment, plus any other the organisation relies on, such as the release go/no-go. For each, note its owner, the person who will lead its review, the decision records it produces and where they are kept, and book a review of it in every quarter of the calendar. Attach the process list and the calendar.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of key AI decision processes with owner, review lead and the decision records each produces, plus the quarterly review calendar

text.en: Name the change-approval, foundation-model selection and security-assessment processes first.
Add any other process the AI system's decisions depend on, such as release go/no-go.
Note each process's owner, its review lead and the decision records it produces.
Book a review of every listed process in each quarter of the calendar.
Circulate the calendar to process owners and file it beside the list.

title.en: Establish one repository for AI decision records, review minutes and their approvals

description.en: Choose a single place — a decision log, a wiki space or a ticket project — where every decision the listed processes take is entered with the evidence weighed, who decided, who approved and the date, and where each review's minutes link to the records they examined. Bring existing records in, or link to them — change approvals already held under AIUC-1 E004 are linked, not re-entered — so a reviewer never has to search several systems to see what was decided. Attach the record template and one populated example.

evidenceHint.en: Decision-record template with fields for evidence weighed, decider, approver and date, plus one populated record and the minutes linked to it

text.en: Pick the repository and limit editing to process owners and review leads.
Define fields for the decision, evidence weighed, decider, approver and date.
Add a minutes template that links each review to the records it examined.
Import or link the decision records each process produced before the repository existed.
Announce where the repository lives and who must enter decisions in it.

title.en: Hold each quarter's review of the AI decision processes against their decision records

description.en: At each scheduled review, pull the decision records the process produced since the last one and test them: did each decision weigh the evidence the process requires, carry the approval it requires, and turn out as expected? Note where the process was bypassed, slow or unclear, agree changes to it, raise each risk found for remediation, and have the minutes approved by the process owner and the review lead. Attach the approved minutes.

evidenceHint.en: Approved review minutes naming the decision records examined, the weaknesses found, the changes agreed and who approved them

text.en: Export the process's decision records dated since its previous review.
Check each record for the evidence and approval its process calls for.
Note decisions that went round the process or led to unexpected results.
Agree process changes and raise a remediation item for each risk found.
Have the process owner and review lead approve the minutes, then file them in the repository.

title.en: Track each risk raised in an AI process review through to remediation

description.en: Enter every risk or weakness a review identifies in the remediation register with the review it came from, an owner, a remediation plan and the target date that owner commits to. Report the status of open items at each following review, and close an item only once the evidence of the fix — the amended procedure, the corrected record, the added check — is attached to it. Attach the register extract for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation register extract listing each risk raised by a process review with its owner, plan, target date, status and closure evidence

text.en: Open a register entry for each risk the minutes record, citing the review it came from.
Name the owner and remediation plan, with the target date that owner commits to.
Present the status of open items at the start of each later review.
Close an item only once the evidence of its fix is attached to it.

title.en: Collect security advisories, customer reports and researcher findings for each process review

description.en: Where proportionate, keep an intake log of feedback from outside the organisation that bears on the AI system: security advisories and threat intelligence about the models and components in use, customer complaints and problem reports taken from the existing feedback channels, and findings from researchers or other third parties, including new mitigations they suggest. Before each review, give its lead the open items for that process, and enter against each whether it was adopted, deferred or rejected, and why. Attach the intake log with outcomes.

evidenceHint.en: External feedback intake log giving source, date, the process review that weighed each item and the outcome entered

text.en: Subscribe to advisories for the models, frameworks and providers the AI system uses.
Route customer problem reports and researcher findings about the AI system into the log.
Tag each item with the decision process it bears on.
Hand each review lead the open items for their process ahead of the review.
Enter the outcome — adopted, deferred or rejected — and the reason against each item.

title.en: Audit a year of AI process reviews for missed quarters and unremediated risks

description.en: Once a year, set the review calendar beside the minutes in the repository and list any quarter in which a process went unreviewed or its minutes were never approved. Check every remediation item raised during the year for an owner, a status and, if closed, evidence of the fix, and sample decision records to confirm the reviews examined what their minutes claim. Present the result to management with the actions agreed. Attach the annual check and its actions.

evidenceHint.en: Annual comparison of calendar, minutes and remediation register, listing missed or unapproved reviews and unremediated risks with agreed actions

text.en: Mark each process and quarter as reviewed, missed or unapproved from the minutes.
Check every remediation item from the year for an owner, a status and closure evidence.
Sample decision records to confirm the reviews examined what their minutes claim.
Present the gaps to management and enter the actions agreed, with owners.

templates.title: Third-party sessions and integrations into the AI system logged, with anomalous access alerted
templates.description: Every connection a third party makes into the AI system, whether a partner API client, an integration, a vendor support session or a sub-processor reaching its data, is registered and logged with who connected, when, from where, for how long and what was touched. Where proportionate, rules detect anomalous third-party access and route each alert to an owner. It covers access into the system, not the choice of vendor.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Security Operations Lead / Integrations Owner
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation can rebuild which third party reached what part of the AI system, when and how, and, where proportionate, is alerted when that access looks wrong.
templates.successCriteria:
Every third party that connects to the AI system is registered with its connection type, credential, permitted scope and internal owner.
Each third-party connection is logged with identity, authentication time, origin IP, resources accessed, session length and volume.
Every third-party credential seen in the logs matches a register entry, and every active register entry is producing logs.
Where proportionate, rules alert on unusual volume, out-of-scope endpoints, repeated failed logins and credentials used outside scope.
Each third-party access alert raised in the period has an owner and a recorded disposition.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the third-party connection register with each party's connection type, credential, permitted scope and owner.
Obtain the logging and SIEM configuration for third-party connections and a sample of log entries for each connection type.
Obtain the detection rules for anomalous third-party access and the alerts raised in the period with their dispositions, where alerting is in place.
Obtain the active third-party credentials from the API gateway and identity platforms.

Analysis:
Compare the active third-party credentials with the register and list any with no register entry.
Sample connections of each type, such as API client, integration and vendor session, and confirm each entry carries identity, time, origin, resources, duration and volume.
Rebuild one sampled third-party session end to end from the logs alone and note any gap.
Where alerting is in place, trigger a test condition such as repeated failed logins and confirm an alert reaches its owner.
Sample alerts raised in the period and confirm each has an owner and a disposition.

Output:
A list of third-party credentials or connections outside the register, and of register entries producing no logs.
A field-by-field statement of log completeness per connection type, with the result of the session rebuild.
The alert test result and a list of alerts left without an owner or disposition.

title.en: Register each partner API client, integration and vendor session with a route into the AI system

description.en: List every third party with a route into the AI system: partner and customer integrations calling its APIs, connected SaaS services, vendors with support or maintenance access and sub-processors that reach its data. For each, write down the connection type, the credential or account used, the endpoints and data it may reach and the internal owner, then pull active third-party credentials from the gateway and identity platforms to catch omissions. Attach the register with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party connection register naming each party, connection type, credential or account, permitted endpoints and data, and internal owner

text.en: List partner API clients, connected services, vendor support accounts and sub-processors.
Name the credential or account each third party connects with.
Write the endpoints and data each party is permitted to reach.
Name the internal owner responsible for each third-party connection.
Export active third-party credentials from the gateway and identity platforms to find omissions.

title.en: Capture caller identity, origin IP, resources touched and session length for third-party connections

description.en: Configure the API gateway, identity provider and remote-access tooling to log every third-party connection and forward it to the central logging or SIEM platform. Each entry carries the party and credential, authentication time and result, origin IP and user agent, endpoints and records accessed, data volume exchanged and session start and end, and is tagged with its register entry so it can be filtered by party. Attach the logging configuration and a sample entry per connection type.

evidenceHint.en: Logging or SIEM configuration for third-party connections, with a sample entry per connection type showing identity, authentication time, origin IP, resources, volume and session length

text.en: Turn on access logging for third-party traffic at the gateway, identity provider and remote-access tool.
Capture party, credential, authentication time and result in each entry.
Capture origin IP, user agent, resources accessed and data volume for each request.
Log session start and end so the length of each session can be worked out.
Tag each entry with its register entry and forward it to the SIEM.

title.en: Write detection rules for unusual third-party call volume, out-of-scope endpoints and failed logins

description.en: Where proportionate, write SIEM rules for third-party access that departs from what the register permits or from what the party normally does: call volume well above its baseline, calls to endpoints outside its permitted scope, repeated failed logins on a vendor account, and a credential used from an unexpected origin or beyond its scope. Route each rule to the connection's internal owner. Attach the rule definitions and their routing.

evidenceHint.en: SIEM detection rules for anomalous third-party access covering volume, out-of-scope endpoints, failed logins and credential misuse, with the owner each routes to

text.en: Baseline each third party's normal call volume and endpoints from the logs.
Alert when a party's call volume departs sharply from its baseline.
Alert on calls to endpoints outside the scope the register permits.
Alert on repeated failed vendor logins and on credentials used from new origins.
Route each rule's alerts to the internal owner named in the register.

title.en: Close each anomalous third-party access alert with its owner's disposition

description.en: Where proportionate and alerting is in place, have the owner of the connection concerned take each alert: check the logs and, where needed, the third party to learn whether the access was expected, decide what action it needs, and close the alert with its disposition, whether expected, misconfigured or suspected misuse passed to the security team. Attach the alert register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Register of third-party access alerts in the period, each with the party, the rule fired, the owner, triage notes, disposition and closure date

text.en: Assign each alert to the owner of the third-party connection it concerns.
Check the logs and, where needed, the third party to see whether the access was expected.
Write the disposition: expected, misconfiguration or suspected misuse.
Pass suspected misuse to the security team with the session's logs.
Close the alert with its disposition and the date.

title.en: Cross-check third-party connections in the access logs against the third-party register

description.en: Once a year, compare the third parties seen in the access logs with the register, and the register with the logs. List connections from parties or credentials that are not registered, register entries that produce no logs, and metadata fields missing from sampled entries, then rebuild one third-party session from the logs alone to confirm it can be reconstructed. Attach the comparison with each gap, its fix and owner.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of logged third-party connections against the register, with unregistered connections, silent entries, missing fields, a rebuilt session and each gap's fix

text.en: Extract the distinct third-party credentials seen in the period's logs.
List logged credentials with no register entry, and entries that produced no logs.
Sample entries per connection type and note any metadata field missing.
Rebuild one third-party session from the logs alone, start to finish.
Enter each gap with its fix, owner and target date.

templates.title: Acceptable use of the AI system defined, breaches detected and users told
templates.description: An acceptable use policy tells users what they must not do with the AI system — attempt jailbreaks or prompt injection, extract data they are not entitled to, produce harmful content, misuse customer data — and users accept it before use. Breaches are detected against the policy's own clauses, the user is told which rule they crossed, and where the risk warrants it violations are tracked as cases and trends reviewed.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: General Counsel / Trust & Safety Lead
templates.objective: To give users a clear statement of prohibited AI use and make it real by detecting breaches of it and telling each user when they have crossed a line.
templates.successCriteria:
The acceptable use policy names each prohibited use relevant to the system and is accepted by users before first use, standalone or within the terms of service.
Every clause of the policy maps to a detection signal, or carries a written reason why its breaches cannot be detected in use.
A user whose request breaches the policy receives a notice naming the rule breached, on every product surface.
Where violation tracking is in place, each detected breach in the period is a case with an owner and a recorded resolution.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the acceptable use policy in force with its effective date, and the acceptance flow or terms that incorporate it.
Obtain the clause-to-signal map and the detection configuration it points to.
Obtain screenshots or recordings of the breach notice on each product surface.
Obtain the violation case log for the period and the most recent effectiveness review, where these are kept.

Analysis:
Compare the policy's prohibited uses with the system's capabilities and the risk taxonomy, noting misuse the policy does not address.
Trace each clause to a live detection signal and note clauses with neither a signal nor a stated reason.
Submit test requests breaching a sample of clauses in a test environment and confirm detection fires and the notice names the right rule.
Sample clause-tagged detection events from across the period and trace each to a case with an owner and a resolution.
Read the effectiveness review for violation trends and the policy or detection changes it led to.

Output:
A clause-by-clause table of detection coverage and notice behaviour.
A list of sampled breaches with no case or no resolution.
A statement of misuse the policy fails to cover.

title.en: Write the acceptable use policy and place it where users accept it before first use

description.en: Draw the prohibited uses from what the system can do and from the risk taxonomy: jailbreak and prompt-injection attempts, extracting data or system behaviour the user is not entitled to, producing harmful content, misusing customer or personal data, and anything specific to the deployment. Number each clause, state how breaches are handled in line with the enforcement actually configured, and publish it standalone or within the terms of service. Attach the policy with its effective date.

evidenceHint.en: Published acceptable use policy, or the terms-of-service section carrying it, listing numbered prohibited uses and breach handling, with its effective date

text.en: List prohibited uses drawn from the system's capabilities and the risk taxonomy.
Number each prohibition so detection rules and notices can cite it.
State how breaches are handled, matching the enforcement actually configured.
Publish the policy where users accept it before first use.
Note the effective date and how existing users are asked to accept the new version.

title.en: Map each acceptable-use clause to the signal that detects a breach of it

description.en: For every numbered prohibition, name the signal that shows a breach in use — a prompt-analysis rule, an output filter flag, a usage-pattern anomaly, an alert on suspicious access — reusing signals other controls already produce and tagging their events with the clause. Add a rule where a clause has none, or write why its breaches cannot be detected in use. Where proportionate, make high-risk clauses block or alert in real time rather than only log. Attach the clause-to-signal map.

evidenceHint.en: Clause-to-signal map naming, for each acceptable-use prohibition, the rule or flag that reveals a breach and whether it logs, alerts or blocks

text.en: List each numbered clause of the acceptable use policy.
Name the existing rule, filter flag or anomaly signal that reveals a breach of it.
Tag each signal's events with the clause number they evidence.
Add a detection rule for any clause left without a signal, or write why none is possible.
Set real-time blocking or alerting for the clauses whose risk warrants it.

title.en: Configure the breach notice telling a user which acceptable-use rule they crossed

description.en: When a clause-tagged detection event fires on a user's request, show that user a notice naming the rule breached in plain language, saying what happened to the request and linking to the policy. Build it for every surface through which users reach the system. Attach screenshots or recordings of the notice on each surface.

evidenceHint.en: Screenshots or recordings of the acceptable-use breach notice on each product surface, showing the rule named and the link to the policy

text.en: Write plain-language notice text for each clause or group of clauses.
Trigger the notice from the clause tag carried on the detection event.
Say whether the request was refused, altered or only flagged.
Link the notice to the relevant clause of the published policy.
Capture the notice on every product surface for the evidence file.

title.en: Track acceptable-use violations as cases from detection through to resolution

description.en: Where proportionate, open a case for each detected breach, or for each user with repeated breaches, assign an owner, and close it with the resolution — a warning, a restriction under the policy's breach handling, or no action with a reason. Attach the case log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Violation case log for the period, one row per case, giving the clause breached, owner, resolution and closure date

text.en: Open a case from each clause-tagged detection event or repeat-breach pattern.
Assign each case an owner on opening.
Apply the response the policy's breach handling sets out.
Close each case with its resolution and the date.
Export the period's case log with clause and resolution columns.

title.en: Analyse acceptable-use violation trends and revise the policy and its detection

description.en: Where proportionate, once in each review period read the case log and detection data for trends — clauses most breached, repeat users, misuse no clause covers — check how well each signal performed against case outcomes, and decide changes to the policy, the signals and any user guidance or training. Attach the review with the changes it decided.

evidenceHint.en: Effectiveness review of acceptable-use violations with trend analysis, signal performance notes and the policy, signal or guidance changes decided

text.en: Count breaches by clause and by repeat user across the period.
Note misuse observed that no clause of the policy covers.
Check each signal's misses and false alarms against case outcomes.
Decide policy, detection and user-guidance changes, each with an owner.
Minute the review and file it with the policy version it produced.

templates.title: Processing locations of the agent and each AI sub-processor recorded and kept current
templates.description: The organisation keeps a dated record of where the agent's data is processed: the cloud regions hosting the service, the region of each inference endpoint and of any training or fine-tuning job, and the locations where each AI sub-processor, model providers included, handles that data. Where data crosses a border, the record names the transfer mechanism relied on. It is updated as infrastructure and providers change.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Data Protection Officer / Cloud Infrastructure Lead
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation can say where the agent's data is processed, by itself and by each AI sub-processor, and on what basis any data crossing a border is transferred.
templates.successCriteria:
The record lists each region hosting the service, each inference endpoint region and each training or fine-tuning location, and matches deployed configuration.
Each AI sub-processor appears with the locations where it processes or stores the organisation's data, taken from its own terms or notices.
Every flow of data across a border is listed with the transfer mechanism relied on and any transfer assessment the applicable law requires.
Each region change and sub-processor location notice in the period is reflected in a dated revision of the record.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the processing-location record and its version history for the period.
Obtain the infrastructure-as-code or cloud console export of deployed regions, and the model-provider endpoints and regions configured in production.
Obtain the AI sub-processor list, each sub-processor's current location statement and the location change notices received in the period.
Obtain the transfer register and any transfer assessments for cross-border flows.

Analysis:
Compare deployed regions and configured endpoints with the record and list any location it omits.
Compare each sub-processor's own location statement with the record entry for it.
Trace each cross-border flow in the record to a transfer mechanism and, where the law requires one, an assessment, and note flows with neither.
Match infrastructure changes and sub-processor notices in the period to dated revisions of the record.
Check gateway configuration for AI providers called in production that the sub-processor list does not name.

Output:
A list of processing locations found in configuration or provider statements but missing from the record.
A table of cross-border flows with their mechanism, flagging any flow left uncovered.
A list of changes in the period that were never carried into the record.

title.en: Map the regions where the agent's hosting, inference and training workloads run

description.en: From infrastructure-as-code and provider console settings, list every region the organisation itself uses for the agent: application hosting, databases, inference endpoints whether self-hosted or a provider's regional endpoint, training and fine-tuning jobs, and failover or backup regions. Draw them onto the agent's data flow diagram so each flow shows the location it passes through. Attach the region list and the annotated diagram.

evidenceHint.en: Dated region list for hosting, inference, training and failover, with the data flow diagram annotated with each processing location

text.en: Export deployed regions for compute, databases and storage from infrastructure-as-code.
List the regional endpoint configured for each hosted model and each self-hosted model server.
Add the regions where training, fine-tuning or batch evaluation jobs run.
Include the failover and backup regions that receive the agent's data.
Annotate the data flow diagram with the location of every hop and date it.

title.en: List each AI sub-processor with the countries where it handles the organisation's data

description.en: For every third party that processes the agent's data — foundation-model providers, hosted vector databases, evaluation, monitoring and labelling services — take from its processing terms, sub-processor page or published notices the countries or regions where it processes and stores that data, including the onward sub-processors it discloses. Note where the organisation's own settings, such as a regional endpoint, narrow those locations. Attach the sub-processor location list with the source of each entry.

evidenceHint.en: AI sub-processor list giving each provider's processing and storage locations, its disclosed onward sub-processors and the source document for each entry

text.en: Name each third party that receives the agent's data, working from the vendor contracts.
Take each provider's processing and storage locations from its own terms or notices.
Add the onward sub-processors and locations each provider discloses.
Note account settings, such as a regional endpoint, that confine processing to fewer places.
Cite the document and date each location entry was taken from.

title.en: Assess each cross-border data flow and name the transfer mechanism covering it

description.en: Where the deployment sends data across a border — to a model provider's region, a sub-processor abroad or a training job elsewhere — pick out each such flow from the region map and sub-processor list, with the data it carries and whether it feeds inference or training. Name the mechanism the applicable law accepts for it, such as an adequacy finding or standard contractual clauses, complete any transfer assessment that law calls for, and note the mitigations adopted. Attach the transfer register.

evidenceHint.en: Transfer register listing each cross-border flow, the data carried, the mechanism relied on and any transfer assessment completed

text.en: Pick out every flow in the region map and sub-processor list that leaves its origin country.
Note the data each flow carries and whether it serves inference or training.
Name the transfer mechanism relied on and file the signed instrument beside it.
Complete a transfer assessment wherever the applicable law calls for one.
Enter mitigations adopted for higher-risk flows, such as pseudonymisation or a pinned region.

title.en: Update the processing-location record when a region, endpoint or sub-processor changes

description.en: Make location changes reach the record as they happen: infrastructure changes that add or move a region, a newly configured model endpoint, and each location change notice a sub-processor sends. For each, revise the region map, the sub-processor list or the transfer register, and log the change with its date so the version history explains every revision. Attach the record's revision history for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Revision history of the processing-location record, each entry citing the infrastructure change or provider notice behind it and its date

text.en: Add a location check to infrastructure changes that create or move a region.
Route sub-processor location change notices to the record owner on receipt.
Revise the region map, sub-processor list or transfer register the change affects.
Enter each revision with its date and the change or notice behind it.

title.en: Reconcile documented processing regions with deployed configuration and provider notices

description.en: Once a year, export the regions actually deployed and the model endpoints actually configured and compare them with the region map; compare each sub-processor's current location statement with its entry; and check that every cross-border flow still has a mechanism in force. Search gateway configuration for AI providers the list does not name. Attach the reconciliation with each mismatch, its fix and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Annual reconciliation of the location record against deployed regions, configured endpoints and provider statements, with each mismatch, fix and owner

text.en: Export deployed regions and configured model endpoints and compare them with the region map.
Compare each sub-processor's current location statement with its record entry.
Check that each cross-border flow still has a transfer mechanism in force.
Search gateway configuration for AI providers missing from the sub-processor list.
Enter each mismatch with its fix, owner and target date, and date the review.

templates.title: Laws and standards binding the agent mapped to required protections and reviewed each half-year
templates.description: A register names the AI laws, data protection laws, sector rules and standards that apply to the agent where it is sold and used, the protections each requires — data protections especially — and how the organisation, at its size and in its operations, meets each one. It is reviewed at least every six months and whenever a law changes or the business enters a new jurisdiction.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: General Counsel / Compliance Lead / Data Protection Officer
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation knows which AI and data laws and standards bind it, what each requires and how it meets them, and keeps that view current as law and markets move.
templates.successCriteria:
The register lists each applicable AI law, data protection law, sector rule and adopted standard, with what brings it into scope.
Each entry states the protections the law or standard requires, data protections included, and the organisation's approach to meeting them.
Each approach is sized to the organisation's scale and operations and points to the procedure or control that carries it out.
Register reviews are dated no more than six months apart, and each produces a versioned register.
Each regulatory change or new jurisdiction in the period was assessed against the register, with its outcome recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the regulatory register with its version history, and the minutes or tickets of each review held in the period.
Obtain the log of regulatory triggers assessed in the period, with the outcome of each.
Obtain the countries and sectors in which the agent was sold or used in the period, from contracts or billing records.
Obtain, for a sample of register entries, the procedures or controls their stated approach relies on.

Analysis:
Measure the interval between successive register reviews and note any gap longer than six months.
Compare the countries and sectors served with the jurisdictions and sectors the register covers and list any left out.
Select a sample of entries and confirm each states its required protections and an approach, and that the procedures it relies on exist.
Match each trigger in the log to a register revision or to a recorded decision that none was needed.
Compare published regulatory updates for the listed jurisdictions in the period with the trigger log and note any change it missed.

Output:
A statement of the review dates and of any interval over six months.
A list of jurisdictions, sectors or laws missing from the register.
A list of sampled entries lacking stated protections, an approach or the procedures that approach depends on.

title.en: Identify the AI, data protection and sector rules that apply in each market the agent serves

description.en: Start from where the agent is sold, where its users and data subjects are, the sectors its customers work in, and the organisation's role in each deployment — whether it builds the AI system or deploys one supplied by another. For each market, list the AI-specific laws, data protection laws, sector requirements and the voluntary standards the organisation has committed to, with what brings each into scope. Attach the register with its date and version.

evidenceHint.en: Dated, versioned register of applicable AI, data protection and sector laws and adopted standards, each with the jurisdiction and activity bringing it into scope

text.en: List the countries where the agent is sold or used and where its data subjects are.
Note the customer sectors served and any sector rule that reaches AI use in them.
State the organisation's role, builder or deployer, for each deployment.
Add the AI and data protection laws each market and role bring into scope.
Include standards the organisation has publicly or contractually committed to meeting.

title.en: State the protections each register entry requires and the approach to meeting it

description.en: Against every entry, set out what the law or standard requires of the agent — data protections such as a lawful basis, minimisation and data-subject rights, and AI duties such as transparency, documentation or risk management where they apply — and the organisation's approach to each, sized to its scale and operations. Point to the procedure, control or document that carries the approach out and name who owns it. Attach the completed register.

evidenceHint.en: Register entries each listing the required protections, the compliance approach, the procedure or control delivering it and its owner

text.en: Summarise in plain terms what each entry requires of the agent.
Separate the data protections an entry demands from its other AI-specific duties.
Describe the approach the organisation takes, scaled to its size and operations.
Link each approach to the procedure, control or document that carries it out.
Name the owner of each approach and mark entries still without one.

title.en: Assess each new law, guidance change or market entry against the regulatory register

description.en: Watch the sources the organisation relies on for regulatory change in its markets, and treat as a trigger any new or amended law or guidance, any move into a new jurisdiction or sector, and any new agent use that could change the organisation's role. Log each trigger as it arises, assess whether it adds or alters a register entry, and make the change or note why none is needed. Attach the trigger log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Trigger log of regulatory changes and business expansions in the period, each with its assessment outcome and any register change made

text.en: Name the regulatory update sources the legal team watches for each market.
Ask sales and product to flag new jurisdictions, sectors and agent uses before launch.
Log each trigger with its date, its source and the entries it might affect.
Revise the register or note why the trigger needs no change.

title.en: Convene the six-monthly regulatory register review and issue its revised version

description.en: At least every six months, take the register through a review with the people who own its entries: confirm each entry still applies, fold in the triggers logged since the last review, check each approach is still current, and agree changes with an owner and date for each. Issue the revised register with a new version number and review date. Attach the review minutes or ticket and the revised register.

evidenceHint.en: Minutes or ticket of each six-monthly review naming attendees and decisions, with the revised register's version number and date

text.en: Schedule the review no more than six months after the previous one.
Walk through each entry to confirm it still applies and its approach is current.
Fold in the triggers logged since the previous review and their outcomes.
Agree changes, owners and dates for each gap the review finds.
Issue the revised register with a new version number and review date.

title.en: Compare the register's jurisdictions and sectors with where the agent is actually sold and used

description.en: Before each review, pull the countries and sectors of current customers from contracts or billing records, and the locations of users from usage data, and set them against the jurisdictions and sectors the register covers. A market served but missing from the register is a trigger to assess straight away rather than at the next review. Attach the comparison with each gap found and the entry or decision it led to.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of countries and sectors served against register coverage, listing each gap and the register entry or decision it produced

text.en: Export customer countries and sectors from contracts or billing records.
Add user locations from usage data where customers roll the agent out to others.
Set both lists against the jurisdictions and sectors the register names.
Raise each uncovered market as a trigger for immediate assessment.

templates.title: AI quality management system sized to the organisation, from objectives to corrective action
templates.description: Optional under AIUC-1, and scaled to the size of the organisation. A documented quality management system governs its AI systems: quality objectives and metrics, a risk-management approach matched to each system's risk level, change-management and documentation procedures, and issue tracking that takes defects through root cause to corrective action, plus data-management and stakeholder-communication procedures where proportionate.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Quality Lead / Head of AI Engineering
templates.objective: To run the organisation's AI systems under a quality management system sized to it, so quality targets are set, measured and acted on, and defects end in verified corrective action.
templates.successCriteria:
A quality manual sets quality objectives, metrics with targets, and a risk-management approach scaled to each AI system's risk level.
The change-management procedure and documentation standards for AI design and development are written, owned and in use.
The issue tracker holds each AI defect with its source, root cause, corrective action and the check that the action worked.
Quality metrics were measured against target in each reporting period, and each missed target opened an issue.
Where proportionate, data-management and stakeholder-communication procedures are written and owned.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
