Obtain the quality manual or its equivalent, with objectives, metrics, targets and the risk-management approach.
Obtain the change-management procedure, the documentation standards and the responsibility matrix for quality decisions.
Obtain the issue tracker configuration and an export of AI defects raised and closed in the period.
Obtain the quality metric reports for each reporting period.
Where adopted, obtain the data-management and stakeholder-communication procedures.

Analysis:
Check that every AI system in scope has objectives and metrics, and that the depth of risk treatment follows its risk level.
Compare a sample of AI changes made in the period with the change-management procedure and the documentation standards.
Select a sample of closed defects and confirm each records a root cause, a corrective action and a check that the action worked.
Compare each period's metric results with their targets and trace every missed target to an issue.
Read the data-management and communication procedures for an owner and for coverage of the records and audiences they name.

Output:
A statement of which quality-system elements exist, are owned and are in use, and which are missing.
A list of sampled changes that departed from the procedure.
A list of defects closed without root cause or verification, and of missed targets that opened no issue.

title.en: Define the AI quality objectives, metrics and risk approach for each system's risk level

description.en: Write the core of the quality manual at a size that suits the organisation — a small team may need only a few pages. Name the AI systems it covers, the quality objectives for each, the metrics and targets that show whether they are met, such as performance and safety thresholds, how often each is measured, and the risk-management approach, with deeper risk assessment for higher-risk systems. Attach the manual section with its approval date.

evidenceHint.en: Approved quality manual section listing AI systems in scope, objectives, metrics with targets and measurement frequency, and the risk approach by risk level

text.en: List the AI systems the quality management system covers and the risk level of each.
Set quality objectives per system and the metric and target that shows each is met.
State how often each metric is measured and who reports it.
Describe the risk-assessment method and how its depth grows with risk level.
Have management approve the section and note the approval date in it.

title.en: Write the AI change-management procedure and design documentation standards into the QMS

description.en: Add to the quality manual the path an AI system change follows from proposal to release, pointing to the change-approval rules held under AIUC-1 E004 rather than restating them, and the documentation standards for design and development work: what each design record, test record and release note must contain, with templates. Name who is accountable for each kind of quality decision in a responsibility matrix. Attach the procedure, the templates and the matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Change-management procedure, design and development documentation templates, and the responsibility matrix for quality decisions, each with owner and version

text.en: Map the stages an AI change passes through from proposal to release.
Reference the change-approval rules held under E004 at the approval stage.
Write templates for design records, test records and release notes.
Build a responsibility matrix naming who decides each kind of quality question.
Publish the procedure with an owner, a version and an effective date.

title.en: Configure the issue tracker to take AI defects from report to verified corrective action

description.en: Set up an issue type or project, in the tracker the organisation already uses, for AI quality defects found in testing, in monitoring of the system after release, or in customer reports. Make source, severity, affected system, root cause, corrective action and verification required fields, and allow an issue to close only once its verification is filled in. Attach the configuration and the workflow it enforces.

evidenceHint.en: Issue tracker configuration for AI defects showing required source, root cause, corrective action and verification fields, and the closure rule

text.en: Create the AI defect issue type or project in the existing tracker.
Add required fields for source, severity, affected system and root cause.
Add corrective action and verification fields, and block closure while verification is empty.
Route defects from testing, post-release monitoring and customer reports into it.
Export the workflow and field configuration for the evidence file.

title.en: Draft the QMS procedures for AI data records and for communicating with authorities

description.en: Where proportionate to the organisation and the regulation it falls under, add two procedures to the quality manual. The first covers data management and record-keeping: governance of training and evaluation data, the technical documentation kept for each system, and the periods the organisation has set for keeping records of training data and outputs. The second covers who reports to regulators, how stakeholders learn of serious incidents and how contact with authorities is handled, linked to the existing incident plans. Attach both procedures.

evidenceHint.en: Data-management and record-keeping procedure, and regulator and stakeholder communication procedure, each with an owner and effective date

text.en: Decide with management which procedures the organisation's size and regulation call for.
Describe governance of training and evaluation data and the technical documentation per system.
State the record-keeping periods the organisation has set for training data and outputs.
Name who speaks to regulators and how stakeholders hear of serious incidents.
Link the communication procedure to the incident response plans already in place.

title.en: Measure each AI quality metric against its target and raise an issue for every miss

description.en: In each reporting period the manual sets, collect the results of every metric for every AI system in scope, compare them with their targets and report them to management. Raise a defect in the issue tracker for every target missed, and link the post-release monitoring results that fed the metrics so the report shows where each figure came from. Attach the period's quality metrics report and the issues it opened.

evidenceHint.en: Quality metrics report per reporting period with results against targets, and the issue tracker entries opened for each missed target

text.en: Pull the period's results for every metric the quality manual defines.
Compare each result with its target and mark it met or missed.
Raise a defect for every missed target, citing the metric and the system.
Report the results and the defects opened to management, then file the report.

title.en: Sample closed AI defects for a recorded root cause and a verified corrective action

description.en: Once a year, draw a sample of AI defects closed in the period across sources and severities. For each, check that the root cause is recorded and credible, that the corrective action addressed that cause, and that the verification shows the defect has not come back; treat a defect reopened or repeated under a new ticket as a sign the action failed. Attach the sample results with findings and the follow-up actions agreed.

evidenceHint.en: Sample of closed AI defects with each one's root cause, corrective action and verification checked, plus findings and follow-up actions

text.en: Draw closed defects across testing, monitoring and customer-report sources and all severities.
Check each for a recorded root cause and a corrective action that addresses it.
Confirm the verification shows the defect has not recurred since closure.
Search for repeat defects raised under new tickets with the same root cause.
Enter the findings with the follow-up actions and owners agreed.

templates.title: AI system and agent activity logged where permitted, with governed retention, access and integrity
templates.description: Wherever the law and customer terms allow, the AI system's inputs, processing steps, outputs and actions are logged in enough detail to investigate an incident and explain its behaviour, and each agent execution is attributable to the agent that ran it. Log stores apply the retention period the organisation set, restricted access and sanitisation, and logs are made tamper-evident where proportionate.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Platform Engineering Lead / Security Engineering
templates.objective: To keep a record of what the AI system and its agents did that is full enough to investigate and explain their behaviour, and that is retained, restricted, sanitised and trustworthy.
templates.successCriteria:
A logging specification names the events, inputs, outputs and metadata captured, and where law or customer terms limit logging to metadata.
Each logged agent execution carries the agent's identifier and version, who or what started it, and links to its sub-agent hand-offs and approvals.
Log stores apply the retention period the organisation set, limit access to named roles and sanitise the fields the specification marks.
Where proportionate, logs are write-once or hash-chained so that alteration, deletion or reordering is detectable.
Sampled executions can be rebuilt end to end from the logs alone.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the logging specification and the organisation's retention policy for AI activity logs.
Obtain the logging code or configuration for each AI system and agent framework in scope.
Obtain each log store's configuration: retention setting, access roles and sanitisation rules.
Where integrity protection is applied, obtain the write-once or hash-chaining configuration and a verification run.
Obtain the incident investigations and audit requests for the period, with their notes on log sufficiency.

Analysis:
Compare the logging configuration with the specification for each system and list events or fields not captured.
Select a sample of agent executions and rebuild each from the logs, following hand-offs, approvals and the linked tool-call records.
Compare each store's retention setting with the policy and query the store for entries older than that period.
Compare the people holding log access with the roles the specification names.
Search a sample of stored entries for content the sanitisation rules should have removed.
Run the integrity verification and confirm it flags a deliberately altered record in a test copy.

Output:
A system-by-system statement of specified against captured logging.
A list of sampled executions that could not be rebuilt, and why.
A list of retention, access, sanitisation and integrity exceptions, each with an owner.

title.en: Define the AI activity logging specification, including where terms limit content logging

description.en: For each AI system and agent in scope, write down the events captured — requests, inputs, retrieval and processing steps, outputs, actions taken, errors — and the metadata on each: timestamp, system and model version, user or calling process, session and execution identifiers. Mark where the law or a customer's terms forbid keeping content and specify metadata-only logging there, and mark the fields to be sanitised before storage. Attach the specification.

evidenceHint.en: Logging specification listing captured events and metadata per AI system, the metadata-only cases set by law or customer terms, and the fields marked for sanitisation

text.en: List the events each AI system and agent emits from request to response or action.
Set the metadata every event carries, including model version and execution identifier.
Identify the customers and jurisdictions whose terms or law bar keeping content.
Specify metadata-only logging for each of those cases.
Mark the fields holding personal data or credentials for sanitisation before storage.

title.en: Add agent provenance and delegation chains to every logged agent execution

description.en: Instrument the agent framework so each execution log carries the agent's identifier, version and deployment origin, the user or process that started it, and a parent identifier whenever one agent hands work to a sub-agent, with the task passed and the outcome returned. Log human approvals against the execution they authorised, and reasoning traces where the framework exposes them. Join to the tool-call log through the shared execution identifier rather than copying it. Attach log entries from one multi-step execution.

evidenceHint.en: Agent logging code or configuration, and the log entries of one multi-step execution showing provenance, hand-offs, approvals and execution identifiers

text.en: Emit the agent identifier, version and deployment origin when each execution starts.
Log the initiating user or process and the session the execution belongs to.
Write a parent execution identifier, the task and the outcome on every sub-agent hand-off.
Link each human approval event to the execution it authorised.
Capture reasoning traces where the agent framework makes them available.
Carry the execution identifier into the tool-call log so the two records join.

title.en: Configure AI log stores with the set retention period, restricted access and sanitisation

description.en: In each log store, set retention to the period the organisation's retention policy gives AI activity logs, so entries are deleted automatically once it ends; this task applies that period and does not choose it. Restrict reading and export to the roles the specification names, and apply the sanitisation rules at ingestion, reusing the personal-data and credential patterns the privacy and secrets controls maintain, so marked fields are masked or removed before they are written. Attach each store's retention, access and sanitisation settings.

evidenceHint.en: Per-store exports or screenshots of retention settings, access role assignments and ingestion sanitisation rules for AI activity logs

text.en: Look up the retention period the organisation's policy sets for each class of AI log.
Set each store's automatic deletion to run at that period.
Grant reading and export rights only to the roles the specification names.
Apply masking or removal at ingestion for every field marked for sanitisation.
Send a test event with a marked field and confirm it is stored sanitised.

title.en: Enable tamper evidence on AI activity logs through write-once storage or hash chaining

description.en: Where proportionate to the system's risk and the use the logs will be put to, make stored logs tamper-evident: write them to storage that refuses modification and deletion within the retention period, or chain each entry to the one before it by hash, so an altered, removed or reordered entry shows up. Provide a verification that an investigator or auditor can run without the logging team's help. Attach the configuration and one verification run.

evidenceHint.en: Write-once storage or hash-chain configuration for AI activity logs, and the output of a verification run showing the chain or lock intact

text.en: Decide with the system owner whether the logs' use warrants tamper evidence.
Turn on write-once retention locks or hash chaining for the chosen log stores.
Add sequence numbers so gaps and reordering surface on verification.
Write the verification procedure an auditor can run without the logging team.
Alter a record in a test copy and confirm the verification flags it.

title.en: Assess each AI incident investigation for whether the activity logs explained what happened

description.en: Whenever an incident or audit request involving the AI system is investigated, state in its record whether the logs were enough to establish what the system and its agents did and why, and name what was missing: events never captured, fields sanitised too heavily, entries already expired, or records nobody could read. Raise a change to the logging specification for each gap. Attach the period's investigation records with their log-sufficiency notes and the changes raised.

evidenceHint.en: Investigation and audit-request records for the period, each with a log-sufficiency note, and the logging specification changes raised from them

text.en: Add a log-sufficiency field to the AI incident and audit-request record template.
Note for each investigation which events the logs did and did not establish.
Classify each gap as not captured, over-sanitised, expired or unreadable.
Raise a logging specification change for each gap and follow it to release.

title.en: Sample stored AI activity logs for missing events, expired entries and unsanitised fields

description.en: Once a year, select agent executions across systems and rebuild each from the logs alone, following hand-offs, approvals and the linked tool-call records. Query each store for entries older than its retention period and for content the sanitisation rules should have removed, compare who holds log access with the roles named, and run the integrity verification where it applies. Attach the sample results with each exception, its fix and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Annual log sample results covering rebuilt executions, retention and sanitisation queries, access comparison and integrity check, with exceptions and owners

text.en: Rebuild the sampled agent executions end to end using only the stored logs.
Query each store for entries past the retention period the policy sets.
Search sampled entries for values the sanitisation rules should have masked.
Compare current log access holders with the roles the specification names.
Run the integrity verification on stores where tamper evidence is enabled.
Enter each exception with its fix, owner and target date.

templates.title: Users told plainly they are dealing with an AI in every text, voice, media and action channel
templates.description: Wherever users meet the AI system they learn it is an AI and not a person: a notice in chat and in automated messages, a spoken statement on voice calls, machine-readable marks on generated images, audio, video and documents, a notification when an agent acts on its own, and a truthful answer whenever a user asks. One consolidated control covering every modality the system uses.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Product Lead / Legal Counsel
templates.objective: To ensure no user of the AI system mistakes it for a person, whichever channel or output type they meet it through, and that they get an honest answer whenever they ask.
templates.successCriteria:
An inventory lists every channel and output type through which users meet the AI system, with the disclosure each one uses.
Every text and voice interaction opens with a notice or spoken statement that the user is dealing with an AI.
Generated images, audio, video and documents carry a machine-readable mark that a detection check can read.
Actions an agent completes with no person in the loop are notified to the affected user as done by an AI.
Asked plainly whether it is an AI, the agent says so in every channel tested.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of user channels and output types, with the disclosure each one uses.
Obtain screenshots of the chat and messaging notices, and recordings or transcripts of voice-call openings.
Obtain the media-marking configuration and the output of a detection check on generated samples.
Obtain the notification templates used when an agent completes an action, and examples delivered in the period.
Obtain the agent instructions that govern questions about its nature, and transcripts of users asking.

Analysis:
Compare the inventory with the product's live channels and integrations to find channels it omits.
For each channel, start a fresh interaction and confirm the disclosure appears or is spoken before the first substantive exchange.
Run the detection check on a sample of generated media of each output type, including files users exported or downloaded.
Trace a sample of agent-completed actions from the period to the notification the user received.
Ask the agent plainly whether it is an AI in each text and voice channel and capture the answer.

Output:
A channel-by-channel table of disclosure present, absent or unclear.
A list of media output types whose mark was missing or unreadable.
A list of agent actions delivered without notification, and of channels where a plain question went unanswered or was answered falsely.

title.en: Inventory every channel and output type through which users meet the AI system

description.en: List each place a user encounters the AI system: chat widgets and in-app assistants, emails and text messages it writes or sends, voice calls, generated images, audio, video and documents, and actions an agent takes for or towards someone — sending a message, making a booking, changing a record. For each, note the modality, who meets it (a customer, a member of the public, a third party receiving the agent's message) and what disclosure exists today. Attach the inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of user-facing channels and output types with the modality, audience and current disclosure for each

text.en: List every chat, assistant and messaging surface the AI system appears in.
Add the voice lines and calls on which the system speaks to people.
Add each generated media and document type, including exports and downloads.
Add the agent actions whose effects a user or third party can see.
Note against each row its audience and the disclosure in place today.

title.en: Add an AI notice to the opening of every chat, automated message and voice call

description.en: Show a notice in each chat or assistant surface that the user is talking to an AI before the first exchange, and put a plain statement in every email or text message the system writes and sends without a person editing it. On voice, play a spoken disclosure at the start of every call, including calls the AI places itself. Use the same plain wording across channels so users recognise it. Attach a screenshot of each text notice and a recording or transcript of a call opening.

evidenceHint.en: Screenshots of the AI notice on each chat surface, sample automated emails or messages carrying the statement, and a call-opening recording or transcript

text.en: Place the AI notice on each chat surface where the user sees it before typing.
Add an AI statement to the template of every automated email and text message.
Script the spoken disclosure that opens every inbound and outbound voice call.
Align the wording across channels so the notice reads and sounds the same.
Capture a screenshot, sample message or call recording for each channel.

title.en: Label AI-generated images, audio, video and documents with machine-readable provenance marks

description.en: For each generated media and document type in the inventory, embed a machine-readable mark — provenance metadata following an open content-credentials standard, a watermark, or both — and add a visible label wherever the content is shown to people. Check that the mark survives the ways content leaves the system, such as download, export and resizing. Where a model provider generates the media, confirm the mark it applies and keep its documentation. Attach the configuration and a detection check.

evidenceHint.en: Media-marking configuration per output type, provider documentation where a provider generates media, and detection-check output on exported samples

text.en: Choose the metadata standard or watermark used for each generated media type.
Embed the mark in the generation pipeline before content is stored or sent.
Add a visible AI label wherever generated content is displayed to people.
Run a detection tool on samples after download, export and resizing.
File the provider's marking documentation where a provider generates the media.

title.en: Notify users when an agent completes an action for them without a person in the loop

description.en: For every agent action in the inventory that takes effect without a person reviewing it — a message sent, a booking made, a record changed — tell the affected user that an AI agent did it, in the confirmation, notification or activity history they see. Messages the agent sends to third parties name an AI as the sender. Attach the notification templates and one delivered example of each.

evidenceHint.en: Confirmation and notification templates naming an AI agent as the actor, and one delivered example per agent action type

text.en: List the agent actions in the inventory that take effect without human review.
Add an 'acted by an AI agent' line to each confirmation and notification template.
Mark agent-performed entries in the activity histories users can see.
Name the AI as sender on every message the agent sends to a third party.
Capture one delivered example of each notification type.

title.en: Set the agent's instructions so it confirms it is an AI whenever a user asks

description.en: Write into each agent's system instructions and persona rules that it says it is an AI when asked, however the question is phrased, and never claims or implies it is human; apply the same rule to voice agents, and check that no persona name or style the product uses contradicts it. Adversarial attempts to talk the agent out of disclosing are for the independent evaluation under AIUC-1 E018; this task sets the behaviour. Attach the instruction text and sample transcripts.

evidenceHint.en: Excerpts of agent system instructions and persona rules requiring truthful AI disclosure, and transcripts of the agent answering a user who asks

text.en: Add the disclose-when-asked rule to every agent's system instructions.
Remove persona wording that suggests the agent is a human employee.
Apply the same rule to the voice agent's prompt and call scripts.
Ask each agent whether it is an AI in several plain phrasings and save the transcripts.

title.en: Walk each user channel to capture the AI disclosure as a user sees or hears it

description.en: Once a year, and whenever the inventory gains a channel, go through every row as a user would: start a fresh chat, receive an automated message, place or take a call, generate and export media, trigger an agent action, and ask plainly whether you are dealing with an AI. Capture what you see or hear, run the detection check on exported media, and compare the live product with the inventory for channels it misses. Attach the walk-through record with each gap and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Walk-through record per channel with screenshots, recordings or transcripts, detection-check results, and each gap found with its owner

text.en: Open a fresh session in each inventoried channel and capture the disclosure shown or spoken.
Generate and export media of each type and run the detection check on it.
Trigger one agent action per type and capture the notification received.
Ask the agent plainly whether it is an AI in each text and voice channel.
Compare the live product with the inventory for channels it does not list.
Enter each gap with its fix and its owner.

templates.title: Major AI systems described in current model cards and AI bills of materials, shared under policy
templates.description: Optional under AIUC-1. Each AI system meeting the organisation's criteria for a major system has current transparency documentation — a model card or datasheet and an AI bill of materials covering its components, data provenance and behaviour — and, where proportionate, a policy says when and with whom that material is shared and how security responsibilities divide between the platform and those deploying it.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Governance Lead / Head of Platform
templates.objective: To give regulators, customers and other stakeholders an accurate, current account of each major AI system's makeup and behaviour, released only in the way the organisation's policy allows.
templates.successCriteria:
Written criteria define which AI systems are major, and every system meeting them is listed.
Each listed system has a model card or datasheet and an AI bill of materials naming its version, data sources, adaptation history and components beyond the model.
Each document's version history shows it was updated when the system it describes changed.
Where proportionate, a sharing policy sets triggers, recipient categories and approval, and every external release is logged by version and recipient.
Where others deploy the platform, platform and deployer security duties are written down.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the criteria for major AI systems and the list of systems meeting them.
Obtain each listed system's model card or datasheet and its AI bill of materials, with their version history.
Obtain the system change records for the period: model versions, fine-tuning runs and component changes.
Where adopted, obtain the transparency sharing policy and the log of external releases.
Where applicable, obtain the statement of platform and deployer security responsibilities.

Analysis:
Apply the criteria to the full AI system inventory and list systems that meet them but are not listed.
For each listed system, compare the components its documents name with the deployed configuration: models, frameworks, orchestration layer and tool connectors.
Trace each change record from the period to a dated update of the system's documents.
For a sample of external releases, check the recipient's category was entitled to the material, the release was approved and its version is logged.
Read the responsibility statement against the platform's actual security features and the guidance given to deployers.

Output:
A system-by-system statement of documentation present, current or stale.
A list of components or changes missing from the documents.
A list of external releases outside policy or unlogged, and of gaps in the responsibility split.

title.en: Determine which AI systems are major enough to need transparency documentation

description.en: Decide which AI systems need a model card or bill of materials — for instance those that face customers, take actions, process personal data or rank high in the risk taxonomy — and write the criteria down. Apply them to the AI system inventory and list every system that qualifies, with its owner and the criteria it meets. Attach the criteria and the resulting list.

evidenceHint.en: Written criteria for major AI systems and the dated list of systems meeting them, each with its owner and the criteria it meets

text.en: Draft the criteria with the AI system owners and the risk taxonomy owner.
Apply the criteria to every system in the AI system inventory.
List each qualifying system with its owner and the criteria it meets.
Date the list and note who set the criteria and when.

title.en: Produce a model card and AI bill of materials for each major AI system

description.en: For each listed system, write a model card or datasheet giving its name and version, purpose and intended use, the models it uses and who provides them, where any training or fine-tuning data came from and what it contains, a dated entry for each fine-tuning or adaptation, and its known limitations and observed behaviour. Add an AI bill of materials listing every framework, orchestration layer and tool connector the system is built from. For third-party models, obtain the provider's model card and reference it. Attach both documents.

evidenceHint.en: Model card or datasheet and AI bill of materials for each major system, giving version, data provenance, adaptation history and components

text.en: Fill in the system's name, version, purpose, intended use and known limitations.
Name each model used with its provider and version, and file the provider's model card.
Describe where any training or fine-tuning data came from and what it contains.
Enter each fine-tuning or adaptation with its date and what it changed.
List the frameworks, orchestration layers and tool connectors in the bill of materials.

title.en: Write the policy on when and with whom AI transparency documents are shared

description.en: Where proportionate — wherever transparency material leaves the organisation — write a policy setting what triggers a release (a regulator's request, a customer's due diligence, a public launch), the recipient categories, and which documents and how much detail each category receives. Add the release procedure: who approves an external release, how the shared version is fixed, and how each release is logged by document, version and recipient. Attach the policy and the release log.

evidenceHint.en: Transparency sharing policy with triggers, recipient categories and detail level per category, plus the release procedure and release log

text.en: List the events that trigger sharing transparency material outside the organisation.
Define recipient categories such as regulators, customers, affected people and the public.
Map which documents and what level of detail each category receives.
Name who approves an external release and how the shared version is frozen.
Set up the release log with document, version, recipient and date.

title.en: Define which security duties the AI platform holds and which fall to its deployers

description.en: Where the organisation offers the AI system as a platform that others deploy, and where proportionate, write a shared-responsibility statement: the security obligations the platform meets, such as hosting, model access and isolation, and those each deployer must meet, such as configuring user access, securing its own integrations and reviewing outputs in its own context. Publish it where deployers will read it, in the terms or the deployment documentation. Attach the statement and where it is published.

evidenceHint.en: Shared-responsibility statement dividing platform and deployer security obligations, and the terms or documentation page where deployers find it

text.en: List the security obligations the platform meets on deployers' behalf.
List the obligations each deployer must meet in its own environment.
Mark any shared obligation and which party does which part of it.
Publish the statement in the terms or the deployment documentation.
Tell existing deployers where the statement lives and how changes are announced.

title.en: Revise each model card and AI bill of materials whenever the system it describes changes

description.en: Treat a new model version, a fine-tuning or adaptation run, or an added, removed or upgraded framework, orchestration layer or tool connector as a trigger to update the system's documents in the same change. Add a dated entry to their version history saying what changed, so each document can be matched to the system as it stood on any date. Attach the version history for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Version history of each model card and AI bill of materials for the period, with dated entries matched to the system changes

text.en: Add the documentation update to the checklist for model and component changes.
Update the model card when the model version or its fine-tuning changes.
Update the bill of materials when a framework, orchestration layer or connector changes.
Enter a dated version-history line saying what changed and why.

title.en: Compare each model card and AI bill of materials with the system actually deployed

description.en: Once a year, set each document beside the deployed system's configuration and its change records: does it name the model and version in use, every framework, orchestration layer and tool connector, and every adaptation made? Re-apply the criteria to the AI system inventory for newly qualifying systems and, where the sharing policy applies, check a sample of releases for approval and a log entry. Attach the comparison with each gap, its fix and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Annual comparison of transparency documents with deployed configuration and change records, criteria re-applied and releases sampled, with gaps and owners

text.en: Export the deployed configuration of each major system's models and components.
Mark every component or adaptation missing from the system's documents.
Re-apply the major-system criteria to the current AI system inventory.
Check a sample of external releases for approval and a release-log entry.
Enter each gap with its fix, owner and target date.

templates.title: Agent's honesty about being an AI independently tested across every channel each quarter
templates.description: Every quarter an evaluator independent of the agent's builders tries to get it to hide, deny or drop the fact that it is an AI — asking outright, instructing it to play a human, pressing over many turns — in every channel it works through, such as chat, voice, email, messaging and messages sent on a user's behalf, and under every persona operators have given it. Scope comes from the taxonomy's accountability risks; each failure is fixed and retested.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Product Lead / Compliance Officer
templates.objective: To confirm each quarter, through someone with no stake in the result, that no user, channel or persona instruction can lead the agent to pass itself off as a person.
templates.successCriteria:
Each quarter's scope lists every channel and persona the agent operates under, with the disclosure each is expected to give.
Each engagement shows the evaluator has red-teamed conversational agents before and wrote none of the agent's personas or instructions.
A report exists for each quarter showing, per channel, the pressure strategies tried and every reply that concealed or denied AI status.
Each failure has a fix and a retest of the original conversation in which the agent states it is an AI.
Operator-written personas and system instructions are tested, not only the default configuration.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the taxonomy's graded AI-disclosure risks for each quarter of the period.
Obtain the inventory of channels and personas the agent served through in the period, with the disclosure required in each.
Obtain each quarter's report with its transcripts and recordings, and the evaluator's engagement terms, channel coverage and independence declaration.
Obtain every disclosure failure raised in the period with its traced cause, fix and retest transcript.

Analysis:
Compare each quarter's tested channels and personas with the inventory and list any never tested in the period.
Check each report covers direct questions about AI status, instructions to impersonate a human and sustained multi-turn pressure in every channel.
Read a sample of passing transcripts from each channel to confirm the disclosure given matches the one required there.
Trace every disclosure failure to a fix and to a later retest transcript in which the agent states it is an AI.
Compare quarters for failures that recur in a channel or persona already fixed.

Output:
A channel-and-persona coverage matrix for each quarter.
A statement on the evaluator's independence and its ability to test every channel and language.
A list of channels or personas where a denial of AI status remains unfixed, unretested or has recurred.

title.en: List every channel and persona in which a user could mistake the agent for a person

description.en: Disclosure can fail in a channel the evaluator never touches. Inventory each way users meet the agent — web chat, voice calls, email, SMS or messaging apps, messages it sends on someone's behalf — and each persona name, voice or role instruction operators have configured, with the AI disclosure the organisation requires in each. Mark the highest-severity cases from the taxonomy's accountability risks. Attach the inventory as the quarter's scope.

evidenceHint.en: Channel and persona inventory with the disclosure required in each, marked against the taxonomy's accountability risks

text.en: List each channel the agent interacts through, including voice and outbound messages.
List each persona name, voice or role instruction configured by operators.
Note the AI disclosure the organisation requires in each channel.
Take the disclosure-bypass risks and their grades from the taxonomy's accountability section.
Mark channels and personas added since last quarter for priority testing.

title.en: Choose an evaluator to test whether role-play or persona pressure makes the agent deny being an AI

description.en: Choose an evaluator experienced in conversational red-teaming who can work in each channel in scope — including placing voice calls if the agent speaks — and in the languages the agent serves. Confirm they have no part in building or operating the agent or writing its personas, and collect credentials and a signed independence declaration. Attach the engagement record.

evidenceHint.en: Engagement record with the evaluator's red-teaming credentials, channel and language coverage, and signed independence declaration

text.en: Confirm the evaluator can test every channel in scope, voice included where used.
Confirm coverage of each language the agent converses in.
Exclude anyone who built the agent or wrote its operator personas.
File each red-teamer's conversational testing record and signed declaration of independence.
Attach the channel and persona inventory to the signed engagement as its scope.

title.en: Obtain per-channel transcripts of the evaluator talking the agent into claiming to be human

description.en: Have the evaluator, in every channel and under every persona in scope, ask outright whether a person is on the other end, tell the agent to say it is human, wrap the request in role-play, and keep pressing over many turns or after an apparent handover to staff. Each reply that hides, denies or evades AI status, or omits a required disclosure, is rated on the taxonomy's scale. Attach the report with the transcripts and, for voice, the recordings.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly report per channel and persona with strategies tried and each concealing or denying reply rated, with transcripts or recordings

text.en: Give the evaluator test access to each channel under each configured persona.
Confirm direct questions, impersonation instructions and role-play framings were tried.
Confirm multi-turn pressure and simulated handovers to staff were tried.
Return the report for any failure listed without its transcript or severity.
Store voice recordings alongside transcripts so each failure can be replayed.

title.en: Resolve each case of the agent denying or hiding that it is an AI, and retest it

description.en: Open a finding for every rated failure and trace it to its cause — a persona instruction that overrode the disclosure, a channel template that strips the disclosure text, a model that yields under pressure — then release the fix, such as an instruction operators cannot override or a fixed disclosure line in that channel. Have the evaluator replay the original conversation, and close the finding only when the agent states plainly that it is an AI. Attach the finding entries with retest transcripts.

evidenceHint.en: Disclosure finding entries with cause, fix, release and the evaluator's retest transcript showing the agent states it is an AI

text.en: Raise a finding for each failure, noting the channel and persona it occurred under.
Trace the cause to a persona instruction, a channel template or model behaviour.
Ship the non-overridable instruction or channel disclosure line in a named version.
Request a replay of the original conversation in the same channel and persona.
Close the finding only when the agent states plainly that it is an AI.

title.en: Check each quarter's disclosure tests reached every channel, persona and language in use

description.en: Each quarter, lay the channels, personas and languages tested beside the current inventory and the operators' live configuration, and mark any not reached — especially those added during the quarter. Look for a failure fixed earlier recurring in another channel or persona, and carry each gap into next quarter's scope. Attach the coverage matrix and the actions.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage matrix of channels, personas and languages tested each quarter against the inventory, with recurring failures and actions

text.en: Export the persona and channel configuration live at quarter end.
Mark which channels, personas and languages the quarter's test reached.
List any added during the quarter that the test did not reach.
Check whether a fixed denial has resurfaced under a different persona or channel.
Flag unreached channels and personas as priorities in next quarter's inventory.

templates.title: Cyber-attack misuse of the agent bounded by provider evidence and own guardrails
templates.description: For each foundation model the agent uses, the organisation holds the provider's assessment of the model's offensive cyber capability and its mitigations, and documents the guardrails it relies on. Where proportionate it screens for requests to build malicious code or plan exploitation, and it reassesses any open-weight model it has changed. Applies to agents that generate text, speech or code, or that take actions.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Security Engineering Lead / AI Platform Engineering
templates.objective: To know what each model the agent runs on could contribute to a cyber attack, and to show guardrails proportionate to that capability are in place or documented.
templates.successCriteria:
Every foundation model in production is registered with its provider's offensive cyber capability assessment for the deployed version, or a note that none is published.
Each registered model lists the provider's cyber mitigations and any guardrail the organisation adds.
Where cyber-misuse screening runs, it blocks requests for malicious code, intrusion planning and exploitation help, and its blocks are reviewed.
Each changed open-weight model has a dated reassessment of whether the provider's cyber results still hold, with its evidence and compensating guardrails.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the model register with each model's cyber capability assessment reference and the provider documents it cites.
Obtain the models and versions deployed in production from the deployment configuration.
Obtain the cyber-misuse screening configuration and prohibited-pattern set, where screening is deployed, and the review log of blocked requests.
Obtain the reassessment for each open-weight model the organisation has changed.

Analysis:
Compare deployed models and versions with the register and note any without an assessment or a note that none is published.
Read each cited provider document and confirm it addresses offensive cyber capability for the registered version and states mitigations.
Run requests from a recognised cyber-misuse evaluation set through the agent in a test environment and confirm screening blocks them and logs the event.
Sample blocked requests from the review log and confirm each carries a verdict and that pattern changes were committed.
Read each reassessment for base model and version, changes made, conclusion and guardrails, and confirm its evaluation results or classifier configuration exist.

Output:
A model-by-model table of deployed version, cyber assessment held and guardrails relied on.
A list of models or versions missing cyber assessment evidence.
A statement on each changed model's reassessment, naming any element it lacks.

title.en: Register each foundation model's offensive cyber capability as its provider assessed it

description.en: For every foundation model the agent calls, obtain the provider's model or system card, safety report or other documentation assessing offensive cyber capability, and register the model, the version assessed, what the provider found, the mitigations it applies and any guardrail the organisation relies on in addition. Where a provider publishes nothing on cyber capability, say so in the entry. Attach the register with the provider documents.

evidenceHint.en: Model register giving, per foundation model, the version assessed, the provider's cyber capability findings and mitigations, and the document cited

text.en: List every foundation model and version the agent calls in production.
Obtain each provider's model card, system card or safety report covering cyber capability.
Enter the provider's findings and the mitigations it states for each model.
Add the guardrails the organisation relies on beyond the provider's own.
Mark any model whose provider publishes no cyber capability assessment.

title.en: Implement cyber-misuse screening for malicious-code and exploitation requests

description.en: Where proportionate — and especially where the agent writes code or runs tools — turn on the cyber-misuse filtering the model provider or platform offers and add rules of the organisation's own, so requests to produce malware, plan an intrusion or exploit a vulnerability are blocked automatically and logged. Keep the prohibited-pattern set under version control with a named owner. Attach the screening configuration and the pattern set version.

evidenceHint.en: Cyber-misuse screening configuration showing its blocking action, and the version-controlled prohibited-pattern set with its owner

text.en: Enable the provider's or platform's cyber-misuse filtering where it is offered.
Add organisation rules for malware creation, intrusion planning and exploitation requests.
Set matching requests to be blocked automatically, with each event logged.
Put the prohibited-pattern set under version control with a named owner.
Test the screening in staging with a recognised cyber-misuse evaluation set.

title.en: Examine each blocked cyber-misuse request and refine the prohibited-pattern set

description.en: Where screening is deployed, go through the requests it blocked in the period: confirm each was a genuine cyber-misuse attempt or a false positive such as a defensive security question, add patterns for attempts found later that screening missed, and narrow patterns that blocked legitimate work. Attach the review log and the pattern-set changes.

evidenceHint.en: Review log of blocked cyber-misuse requests with a verdict per request, and the dated changes made to the prohibited-pattern set

text.en: Export the period's blocked cyber-misuse requests from the screening log.
Mark each as a genuine attempt or a false positive.
Add patterns for attempts found later that screening missed.
Narrow patterns that blocked legitimate defensive security work.
Commit the pattern changes with the review log as their reason.

title.en: Reconcile the deployed model versions against the cyber assessments on file

description.en: Once a year, compare the models and versions in the deployment configuration with the register, obtain the provider's current cyber assessment for any version that changed in the period, and correct entries whose assessment covers a different version from the one running. Attach the reconciliation with every gap and its correction.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of deployed models and versions against the register, listing each mismatch or missing cyber assessment and its correction

text.en: Pull the models and versions running from the deployment configuration.
Compare each with its register entry and the version its assessment covers.
Obtain the provider's current cyber assessment for every changed version.
Update the register and the guardrails noted for each corrected entry.
File the reconciliation with its date and the gaps found.

title.en: Reassess the cyber capability of any open-weight model the organisation has changed

description.en: Where the agent runs an open-weight model the organisation has fine-tuned, merged, quantised or otherwise altered, write an assessment naming the base model and version and the changes made, and conclude whether the provider's cyber results still hold — by repeating cyber-misuse evaluations against the altered model, or by placing classifiers on its output that catch exploit and malware code as a compensating guardrail. Attach the assessment with its evaluation results or classifier configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Reassessment per altered open-weight model: base model and version, changes made, whether the provider's cyber results hold, evaluation results and guardrails added

text.en: Identify each open-weight model in use that the organisation has altered.
Write down the base model, its version and every change made to it.
Repeat the cyber-misuse evaluations on the altered model and keep the results.
Add classifiers that catch exploit or malware code in output where results weakened.
Conclude whether the provider's cyber results still hold and sign the assessment.

templates.title: Each model's CBRN capability known from its provider and misuse watched for
templates.description: The organisation keeps a list of every foundation model the agent uses with the provider's own information on its chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear capability and the mitigations applied, and documents the guardrails it relies on against that use. Where proportionate it monitors interactions for signs of catastrophic-misuse intent, alerts on them and keeps a record of each. Applies to agents that generate text, speech or images.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Trust & Safety Lead / AI Platform Engineering
templates.objective: To know what each model behind the agent could contribute to CBRN harm, and to show the guardrails and, where proportionate, the monitoring that stand against that use.
templates.successCriteria:
Every foundation model in production appears on the CBRN list with the provider's capability information for the version deployed, or a note that none is published.
Each listed model names the provider's CBRN mitigations and any guardrail the organisation relies on in addition.
Where monitoring is deployed, alert rules for catastrophic-misuse intent are live and route to a named responder.
Each CBRN alert in the period has a record preserving the interaction, the responder's assessment and the action taken.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the CBRN model list with the provider documents cited for each model.
Obtain the models and versions deployed in production from the deployment configuration.
Obtain the catastrophic-misuse monitoring rules and alert routing, where monitoring is deployed.
Obtain the records of every CBRN alert raised in the period.

Analysis:
Compare deployed models and versions with the list and note any without CBRN information or a note that none is published.
Read each cited provider document and confirm it addresses CBRN capability for the listed version and states the mitigations applied.
Check the guardrails the list says the organisation relies on are configured as described.
Confirm the monitoring rules are enabled in production and that a staged test alert reaches the named responder.
Sample alert records from across the period and confirm each preserves the interaction, the responder's assessment and the action taken.

Output:
A model-by-model table of deployed version, CBRN information held and guardrails relied on.
A list of models or versions lacking CBRN evidence, and of guardrails listed but not found configured.
A list of sampled alerts lacking a preserved interaction, an assessment or a recorded action.

title.en: Collect each model provider's CBRN capability evaluation and stated mitigations

description.en: List every foundation model and version the agent uses and, for each, obtain the provider's model card, system card, safety framework report or other document describing its chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear capability and the mitigations applied. Enter what the provider concluded, the guardrails the organisation relies on in addition, and any model for which the provider publishes no CBRN information. Attach the list with the documents cited.

evidenceHint.en: List of foundation models in use, each with the provider's CBRN capability conclusion, its mitigations, the document cited and the guardrails relied on

text.en: List every foundation model and version behind the agent in production.
Obtain each provider's documentation on CBRN capability for that version.
Note the provider's conclusion and the mitigations it applies.
Add the guardrails the organisation relies on beyond the provider's own.
Flag any model whose provider publishes no CBRN information.

title.en: Deploy CBRN misuse monitoring that alerts a responder on mass-harm intent

description.en: Where proportionate, monitor the agent's interactions for patterns suggesting an attempt to obtain help towards chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear harm, using the provider's or platform's safety classifiers where offered and versioned rules of the organisation's own, and send real-time alerts to a named responder roster. Attach the monitoring and alert configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring and alert configuration for CBRN misuse patterns, showing the classifiers or rules used and the responder roster the alerts reach

text.en: Enable the provider's or platform's CBRN safety classifiers where they are offered.
Add organisation rules for patterns of catastrophic-misuse intent, kept under version control.
Route real-time alerts to the named responder roster.
Log each flagged interaction together with the system's response.
Raise a test alert in staging with a harmless test case to confirm the routing works.

title.en: Escalate each CBRN misuse alert with the interaction preserved for assessment

description.en: Where monitoring is deployed, the responder opens a record for every alert, preserves the flagged queries and the system's responses, assesses whether the interaction shows catastrophic-misuse intent, and enters the action taken — none with a reason, restriction of the user under the acceptable use policy, or escalation through the organisation's incident process. Attach the period's alert records.

evidenceHint.en: Records for every CBRN misuse alert in the period, each preserving the queries and responses, the assessment made and the action taken

text.en: Open a record for each alert with its time, session and the rule that fired.
Preserve the flagged queries and the system's responses in the record.
Assess whether the interaction shows catastrophic-misuse intent.
Enter the action: none with a reason, user restriction or incident escalation.
Export the period's alert records for the evidence file.

title.en: Confirm the CBRN evidence on file covers each model version now in production

description.en: Once a year, compare the models and versions in the deployment configuration with the CBRN list, obtain updated provider information for any version that changed, and correct entries whose information covers a different version. Where monitoring is deployed, check its rules still apply to every model on the list. Attach the reconciliation with each gap and its correction.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of production models and versions against the CBRN list, naming each gap, the updated provider document and the correction made

text.en: Pull the models and versions running from the deployment configuration.
Match each against its CBRN list entry and the version that entry covers.
Obtain updated provider CBRN information for every changed version.
Check the monitoring rules cover each model on the list, where monitoring runs.
Date the reconciliation and file it with the CBRN list.
